/* Caption: Compute the factorial of a number recursively. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(n) that calls itself.
   2. Return 1 when n is 1 or less.
   3. Otherwise return n * factorial(n - 1).
   4. Print 8! as an unsigned long long. */
/* n! = n * (n - 1)!, and 0! = 1 stops the recursion. */
unsigned long long factorial(int n) {
    if (n <= 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    return n * factorial(n - 1);
}

int main(void) {
    int n = 8;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", n, factorial(n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() calls itself: n! is n * (n - 1)!, and the recursion stops when
   n is 1 or less. main() prints 8! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very
   fast. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I find the total of all elements in an array using a loop in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write add_all() that takes the array scores and its length count.
   2. Start total at 0 and add every element in a while loop.
   3. Return total.
   4. In main(), fill scores with 5 values and print the sum. */
/* Return the sum of the first n elements. */
double add_all(const double scores[], int count) {
    double total = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < count) {
        total += scores[i];
        i++;
    }
    return total;
}

int main(void) {
    double scores[] = {8.0, 68.2, 48.9, 23.3, 94.4};
    const int count = 5;
    printf("Sum: %.2f\n", add_all(scores, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: add_all() receives the array scores and its length count. It starts total
   at 0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills
   scores with 5 double values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I test if "rocket" reads the same backwards in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for line.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check rocket and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *line) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(line) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (line[i] != line[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *line = "rocket";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", line, is_palindrome(line) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word rocket and
   prints the result. */
// END

   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 3 to the power 4. */

/* Caption: C program to raise a number to an integer power with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 3 to the power 10. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("3^10 = %lld\n", power(3, 10));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 3 to the power 10. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the greatest common divisor of two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 195 and 268. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 195, y = 268;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 195 and 268. */
// END

/* Caption: Generate the Fibonacci sequence. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with prev = 0 and curr = 1.
   2. Repeat 10 times and print prev each time.
   3. Compute next = prev + curr, then set prev = curr and curr = next. */
int main(void) {
    long prev = 0, curr = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", prev);
        long next = prev + curr;
        prev = curr;
        curr = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in prev and curr. Each round it prints
   prev, then moves the pair forward: prev becomes curr and curr becomes their sum. It
   prints the first 10 Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to allocate an array with malloc and fill it with multiples. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 6 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill table with multiples.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(table) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 6;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *table = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (table == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        table[i] = 5 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", table[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(table);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 6 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills table with multiples, the second prints
   them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to reverse the digits of a number. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Multiply result by 10, add n % 10, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 317631 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int reverse_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result = result * 10 + n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 317631;
    printf("reverse of digits of %d: %d\n", number, reverse_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_digits() shifts result one place left (result * 10) and adds the
   last digit of n, which reverses the order. main() applies it to 317631. */
// END

/* Caption: Use bubble sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the double array prices.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for ascending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(double prices[], int count) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < count - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (prices[j] > prices[j + 1]) {
                double tmp = prices[j];
                prices[j] = prices[j + 1];
                prices[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double prices[] = {98.3, 57.0, 86.9, 42.9, 42.1, 46.1, 94.9};
    int count = 7;
    bubble_sort(prices, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", prices[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through prices again and again and swaps neighbours
   that are in the wrong order, so the largest values move to the end first. main() then
   prints the 7 values in ascending order. */
// END

   how many of the 11 values are odd. */

/* Caption: Convert 801 to binary. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 801 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 801;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 16);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 801
   in binary. */
// END

/* toupper changes lowercase letters and leaves other characters alone. */
void to_upper(char *line) {
    for (int i = 0; line[i] != '\0'; i++) {

    }
}

/* Caption: How do I search an array for a value and print its position in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and key.
   2. Compare each element with key.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 84 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of key, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int numbers[], int n, int key) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (numbers[i] == key) {
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {64, 17, 46, 92, 84, 18, 54, 84, 57, 27};
    const int n = 10;
    int key = 84;
    int pos = linear_search(numbers, n, key);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", key, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", key);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of numbers one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to key, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 84 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I reverse the elements of an array in place in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for nums.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap nums[i] and nums[j], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when i meets j and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(double nums[], int length) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = length - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        double tmp = nums[i];
        nums[i] = nums[j];
        nums[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double nums[] = {11.7, 47.4, 83.3, 27.3};
    int length = 4;
    reverse_array(nums, length);
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", nums[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves i forward and
   j backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second array.
   main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

   and counts the matches. main() prints how many times u appears in the sentence. */
// END

/* Caption: Write lines to a text file and read them back. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open output.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 3 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("output.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "c gives you direct control over memory\n");
    fprintf(file, "good comments explain why the code exists\n");
    fprintf(file, "learning c teaches how computers work\n");
    fclose(file);

    /* Reopen the file for reading and print it line by line. */
    file = fopen("output.txt", "r");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fopen() in write mode creates output.txt, fprintf() writes 3 lines into it
   and fclose() saves it. The file is then opened again in read mode, and fgets() reads it
   back line by line into the buffer line, which is printed. Every fopen() result is
   checked for NULL. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to check whether a number is prime. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Check 58 and print the result. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 58;
    printf("%d %s prime\n", number, is_prime(number) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() checks 58 and prints whether it is prime. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the length of a string without strlen. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write string_length() with a counter len = 0.
   2. Move through the string until the null character.
   3. Return len and print the length of level. */
/* Count characters until the terminating '\0'. */
int string_length(const char *buffer) {
    int len = 0;
    while (buffer[len] != '\0') {
        len++;
    }
    return len;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *buffer = "level";
    printf("Length of \"%s\" is %d\n", buffer, string_length(buffer));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: string_length() counts characters until it reaches the null character that
   ends every C string. main() prints the length of the word level. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to print the first 10 Fibonacci numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write fib(n) that returns n when n < 2.
   2. Otherwise return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2).
   3. Print fib(i) for i from 0 to 9. */
/* Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two before it. */
long fib(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return n;
    }
    return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2);
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", fib(i));
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fib() returns n for 0 and 1 and otherwise adds the two previous Fibonacci
   numbers by calling itself twice, which is simple but slow for large n. main() prints the
   first 10 numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I count the odd values in a list of integers in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_odd() that takes numbers and n.
   2. For each element, test numbers[k] % 2 != 0.
   3. Add one to count for every odd number.
   4. Return count and print it. */
/* A number is odd when the remainder after dividing by 2 is one. */
int count_odd(const int numbers[], int n) {
    int count = 0;
    int k = 0;
    while (k < n) {
        if (numbers[k] % 2 != 0) {
            count++;
        }
        k++;
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {17, 59, 14, 33, 33, 39, 66};
    int n = sizeof(numbers) / sizeof(numbers[0]);
    printf("Count of odd values = %d\n", count_odd(numbers, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_odd() tests each element of numbers with the % operator: a remainder
   of 1 after dividing by 2 means the number is odd, so count goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 7 values are odd. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to write a function that returns the quotient and remainder through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write divide(a, b, &quotient, &remainder) that returns a bool.
   2. Return false if b is 0.
   3. Store a / b and a % b through the pointers and return true.
   4. Divide 337 by 7 and print the results or the error. */
/* Returns false for division by zero; otherwise stores both results. */
bool divide(int a, int b, int *quotient, int *remainder) {
    if (b == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *quotient = a / b;
    *remainder = a % b;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 337, b = 7;
    int q, r;
    if (divide(a, b, &q, &r)) {
        printf("%d / %d = %d remainder %d\n", a, b, q, r);
    } else {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: divide() has four parameters: two inputs and two pointers for the results.
   Its bool return value reports success, while the quotient and remainder are written
   through the pointers. main() divides 337 by 7 and prints both results. */
// END

/* Caption: Use bubble sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the double array values.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for ascending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(double values[], int size) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < size - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (values[j] > values[j + 1]) {
                double tmp = values[j];
                values[j] = values[j + 1];
                values[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double values[] = {30.1, 33.2, 86.3, 57.6, 60.5, 77.3};
    const int size = 6;
    bubble_sort(values, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", values[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through values again and again and swaps neighbours
   that are in the wrong order, so the largest values move to the end first. main() then
   prints the 6 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Use binary search to locate a value in a sorted list. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to len - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 172. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int samples[], int len, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = len - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (samples[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (samples[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {69, 80, 123, 150, 172, 199};
    const int len = 6;
    int index = binary_search(samples, len, 172);
    printf("Index of 172: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from lo to hi,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 172 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to implement a simple linked list with malloc and free. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ListNode with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct ListNode {
    int value;
    struct ListNode *next;
} ListNode;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
ListNode *push_front(ListNode *head, int value) {
    ListNode *node = malloc(sizeof(ListNode));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const ListNode *head) {
    for (const ListNode *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(ListNode *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        ListNode *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    ListNode *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 49);
    head = push_front(head, 31);
    head = push_front(head, 67);
    head = push_front(head, 20);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each ListNode holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Return a sum and an average together using pointer parameters. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_and_average() with the pointers sum and average.
   2. Add the values into *sum.
   3. Store *sum / n in *average.
   4. Declare total and mean, pass their addresses and print them. */
void sum_and_average(const double v[], int n, double *sum, double *average) {
    *sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        *sum += v[i];
    }
    *average = *sum / n;
}

int main(void) {
    double values[] = {22.4, 4.2, 59.7, 93.8, 4.8, 63.4};
    int n = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    double total, mean;
    sum_and_average(values, n, &total, &mean);
    printf("Sum: %.2f, Average: %.2f\n", total, mean);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_and_average() takes the array, its length and two pointers. It adds up
   the 6 values through *sum and then stores *sum / n in *average. main() declares total
   and mean on one line and passes their addresses. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to write lines to a text file and read them back. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open output.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 2 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("output.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "good comments explain why the code exists\n");
    fprintf(file, "the compiler turns source code into machine code\n");
    fclose(file);

    /* Reopen the file for reading and print it line by line. */
    file = fopen("output.txt", "r");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fopen() in write mode creates output.txt, fprintf() writes 2 lines into it
   and fclose() saves it. The file is then opened again in read mode, and fgets() reads it
   back line by line into the buffer line, which is printed. Every fopen() result is
   checked for NULL. */
// END

/* Caption: Decide if 2038 is a leap year. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_leap(year).
   2. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year, unless it is divisible by 100.
   3. Years divisible by 400 are leap years again.
   4. Check 2038 and print the result. */
/* Leap years divide by 4, except centuries, which must divide by 400. */
int is_leap(int year) {
    return (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || year % 400 == 0;
}

int main(void) {
    int year = 2038;
    if (is_leap(year)) {
        printf("%d is a leap year\n", year);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not a leap year\n", year);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_leap() returns true for years divisible by 4, except century years,
   which must also be divisible by 400. main() checks 2038 and prints whether it is a leap
   year. */
// END

/* Caption: Return the minimum, maximum and average of an array in a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stats struct with min, max and average.
   2. Write array_stats() that fills one Stats in a loop.
   3. Return the struct.
   4. Print st.min, st.max and st.average. */
typedef struct {
    int min;
    int max;
    double average;
} Stats;

/* Pack several results into one struct and return it. */
Stats array_stats(const int v[], int n) {
    Stats s = {v[0], v[0], 0.0};
    double total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (v[i] < s.min) {
            s.min = v[i];
        }
        if (v[i] > s.max) {
            s.max = v[i];
        }
        total += v[i];
    }
    s.average = total / n;
    return s;
}

int main(void) {
    int prices[] = {60, 99, 3, 3, 82, 21, 64, 76};
    int n = sizeof(prices) / sizeof(prices[0]);
    Stats st = array_stats(prices, n);
    printf("Min %d, Max %d, Average %.2f\n", st.min, st.max, st.average);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Stats groups three results. array_stats() fills one Stats while it loops
   over the 8 values and returns the whole struct, which is a clean way to return several
   results at once. main() reads them as st.min, st.max and st.average. */
// END

/* Caption: Use insertion sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the int array data.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(int data[], int len) {
    for (int i = 1; i < len; i++) {
        int current = data[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && data[j] > current) {
            data[j + 1] = data[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        data[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int data[] = {64, 42, 13, 32, 73, 15, 62, 52, 4};
    const int len = 9;
    insertion_sort(data, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%d ", data[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 9 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the index of a number using linear search. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and target.
   2. Compare each element with target.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 192 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of target, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int data[], int size, int target) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        if (data[i] == target) {
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int data[] = {25, 69, 45, 93, 25, 90, 62, 13};
    const int size = 8;
    int target = 192;
    int pos = linear_search(data, size, target);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", target, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", target);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of data one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to target, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 192 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the distance between two points using a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Point struct with x and y.
   2. Write distance() using sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy).
   3. Print the distance between p and q. */
typedef struct {
    double x;
    double y;
} Point;

/* Pythagoras: sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). */
double distance(Point a, Point b) {
    double dx = b.x - a.x;
    double dy = b.y - a.y;
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

int main(void) {
    Point p = {8, -8};
    Point q = {5, 10};
    printf("Distance: %.3f\n", distance(p, q));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Point is a typedef struct with x and y. distance() uses Pythagoras, sqrt(dx
   * dx + dy * dy), to measure the gap between the two points, and main() prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to multiply two fractions using a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Fraction struct with num and den.
   2. Write multiply() that returns num = a.num * b.num and den = a.den * b.den.
   3. Print 2/9 times 6/5. */
typedef struct {
    int num;
    int den;
} Fraction;

/* Multiply the numerators and the denominators. */
Fraction multiply(Fraction a, Fraction b) {
    Fraction r = {a.num * b.num, a.den * b.den};
    return r;
}

int main(void) {
    Fraction x = {2, 9}, y = {6, 5};
    Fraction p = multiply(x, y);
    printf("%d/%d * %d/%d = %d/%d\n", x.num, x.den, y.num, y.den, p.num, p.den);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Fraction stores a numerator and a denominator. multiply() takes two
   Fractions and returns a new one with num = a.num * b.num and den = a.den * b.den. main()
   multiplies 2/9 by 6/5 (without reducing the result). */
// END

/* Caption: Program to compute the factorial of a number with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(value) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by every number from 2 to value.
   3. Return result.
   4. Print 12! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int value) {
    unsigned long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= value; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int value = 12;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", value, factorial(value));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() multiplies result by every number from 2 up to value. main()
   prints 12! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to compute 8 to the power of 6 without pow(). */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 8 to the power 6. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("8^6 = %lld\n", power(8, 6));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 8 to the power 6. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to count the even values in a list of integers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes numbers and length.
   2. For each element, test numbers[i] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to found for every even number.
   4. Return found and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int numbers[], int length) {
    int found = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        if (numbers[i] % 2 == 0) {
            found++;
        }
    }
    return found;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {83, 59, 67, 34, 95, 44, 28};
    int length = 7;
    printf("Even numbers: %d\n", count_even(numbers, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_even() tests each element of numbers with the % operator: a remainder
   of 0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so found goes up by one. main()
   prints how many of the 7 values are even. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to find a number in a sorted array with binary search. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to count - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 201. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int prices[], int count, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = count - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (prices[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (prices[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {

/* Caption: Decide if 1937 is a leap year. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_leap(year).
   2. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year, unless it is divisible by 100.
   3. Years divisible by 400 are leap years again.
   4. Check 1937 and print the result. */
/* Leap years divide by 4, except centuries, which must divide by 400. */
int is_leap(int year) {
    return (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || year % 400 == 0;
}

int main(void) {
    int year = 1937;
    if (is_leap(year)) {
        printf("%d is a leap year\n", year);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not a leap year\n", year);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_leap() returns true for years divisible by 4, except century years,
   which must also be divisible by 400. main() checks 1937 and prints whether it is a leap
   year. */
// END

/* Caption: Use dynamic memory to store the first 9 evens. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 9 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill table with evens.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(table) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 9;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *table = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (table == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        table[i] = 2 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", table[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(table);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 9 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills table with evens, the second prints them,
   and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Use insertion sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the int array samples.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(int samples[], int count) {
    for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {
        int current = samples[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && samples[j] > current) {
            samples[j + 1] = samples[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        samples[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {59, 72, 67, 19, 63, 83, 88, 33};
    const int count = 8;
    insertion_sort(samples, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%d ", samples[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 8 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.

   evenly, n is not prime. main() tests every number from 2 to 34 and prints the primes. */

/* Caption: Check whether a word is a palindrome. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for word.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check stats and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *word) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(word) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (word[i] != word[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *word = "stats";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", word, is_palindrome(word) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word stats and prints
   the result. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I swap two variables using pointers in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two int values.
   2. Save *a in tmp, copy *b into *a, then tmp into *b.
   3. In main(), print a and b, call swap(&a, &b) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(int *a, int *b) {
    int tmp = *a;
    *a = *b;
    *b = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 67, b = 86;
    printf("Before: %d %d\n", a, b);
    swap(&a, &b);
    printf("After:  %d %d\n", a, b);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of a and b, so writing through the pointers
   *a and *b changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to find the least common multiple of two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm: replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   2. Write lcm() as a / gcd(a, b) * b.
   3. Print the LCM of 101 and 256. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

/* lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b (divide first to avoid overflow). */
long lcm(int a, int b) {
    return (long)a / gcd(a, b) * b;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("lcm(101, 256) = %ld\n", lcm(101, 256));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. lcm() divides a by the gcd before multiplying by b, which avoids overflow.
   main() prints the LCM of 101 and 256. */
// END

/* Caption: Sum a int array with a helper function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:

   2. Start result at 0 and add every element in a while loop.
   3. Return result.
   4. In main(), fill nums with 8 values and print the sum. */
/* Return the sum of the first n elements. */
int array_sum(const int nums[], int n) {
    int result = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < n) {
        result += nums[i];
        i++;
    }
    return result;
}

    int n = sizeof(nums) / sizeof(nums[0]);
    printf("The sum is %d\n", array_sum(nums, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: array_sum() receives the array nums and its length n. It starts result at
   0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills nums
   with 8 int values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I find a number in a sorted array with binary search in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set low to 0 and high to len - 1.
   3. While low <= high, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 29. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int marks[], int len, int key) {
    int low = 0;
    int high = len - 1;
    while (low <= high) {
        int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (marks[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (marks[mid] < key) {
            low = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            high = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int marks[] = {29, 47, 67, 85, 109, 110, 119};
    int len = sizeof(marks) / sizeof(marks[0]);
    int index = binary_search(marks, len, 29);
    printf("Index of 29: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from low to high,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 29 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Multiply two 2x2 matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define N as 2.
   2. For every i and j, add a[i][k] * b[k][j] over k into product[i][j].
   3. Print product row by row. */
#define N 2

int main(void) {
    int a[N][N] = {{1, 4}, {9, 5}};
    int b[N][N] = {{3, 1}, {2, 9}};
    int product[N][N] = {0};
    /* product[i][j] is row i of a times column j of b. */
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) {
                product[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            printf("%4d", product[i][j]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: For each entry product[i][j] the innermost loop adds a[i][k] * b[k][j] over
   k, which is row i of a times column j of b. main() multiplies two 2x2 matrices and
   prints the product. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write mean() that takes values and size.
   2. Add the values into the double sum.
   3. Return sum / size.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* The mean is the total divided by the count. */
double mean(const long values[], int size) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int j = 0; j < size; j++) {
        sum += values[j];
    }
    return sum / size;
}

int main(void) {
    long values[] = {33L, 36L, 8L};
    int size = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    printf("Average: %.2f\n", mean(values, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: mean() adds the 3 values of values into the double sum and divides by size,
   so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers. main() prints
   it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Duration struct with hours, minutes and seconds.
   2. Write from_seconds() that fills it using / and %.
   3. Convert 28459 seconds and print the members. */

    int hours;
    int minutes;
    int seconds;
} Duration;

Duration from_seconds(int total) {
    Duration d;
    d.hours = total / 3600;
    d.minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    d.seconds = total % 60;
    return d;
}

    return 0;

   then returns the struct. main() converts 28459 seconds and prints the members. */

/* Caption: Sort an array in descending order using selection sort. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the int array readings.
   2. For each position, find the largest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(int readings[], int size) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < size; j++) {
            if (readings[chosen] < readings[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        int tmp = readings[i];
        readings[i] = readings[chosen];
        readings[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int readings[] = {74, 90, 24, 54, 33, 58, 87};
    int size = 7;
    selection_sort(readings, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%d ", readings[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the largest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 7 values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to count how many even numbers are in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes nums and size.
   2. For each element, test nums[i] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to tally for every even number.
   4. Return tally and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int nums[], int size) {
    int tally = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        if (nums[i] % 2 == 0) {
            tally++;
        }
    }
    return tally;
}

    int nums[] = {40, 6, 89, 12, 34, 46, 95};
    const int size = 7;
    printf("Even numbers: %d\n", count_even(nums, size));
    return 0;
}

   0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so tally goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 7 values are even. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I compute the distance between two points using a struct in C? */

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Point struct with x and y.
   2. Write distance() using sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy).
   3. Print the distance between p and q. */
typedef struct {
    double x;
    double y;
} Point;

/* Pythagoras: sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). */
double distance(Point a, Point b) {
    double dx = b.x - a.x;
    double dy = b.y - a.y;
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

int main(void) {
    Point p = {1, 5};
    Point q = {3, -4};
    printf("Distance: %.3f\n", distance(p, q));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Point is a typedef struct with x and y. distance() uses Pythagoras, sqrt(dx
   * dx + dy * dy), to measure the gap between the two points, and main() prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to sort an array in descending order using selection sort. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the long array prices.
   2. For each position, find the largest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(long prices[], int count) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < count; j++) {
            if (prices[chosen] < prices[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        long tmp = prices[i];
        prices[i] = prices[chosen];
        prices[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long prices[] = {68L, 43L, 81L, 56L, 11L, 61L, 42L, 88L, 35L, 19L};
    int count = sizeof(prices) / sizeof(prices[0]);
    selection_sort(prices, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", prices[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the largest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 10 values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to build a FIFO queue using a ring buffer. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 32 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 3 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 32

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 78);
    enqueue(&q, 2);
    enqueue(&q, 84);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 32 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 3 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Convert 237 to binary. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 237 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 237;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 8);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 237
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: Add up all the numbers in an array of int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write total_of() that takes the array ages and its length size.
   2. Start result at 0 and add every element in a for loop.
   3. Return result.
   4. In main(), fill ages with 9 values and print the sum. */
/* Walk through the array and accumulate each value. */
int total_of(const int ages[], int size) {
    int result = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        result += ages[i];
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {

    int size = sizeof(ages) / sizeof(ages[0]);
    printf("Sum: %d\n", total_of(ages, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: total_of() receives the array ages and its length size. It starts result at
   0, adds every element to it in a for loop and returns the total. main() fills ages with
   9 int values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I count how many digits a number has in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Divide n by 10 and add one to result.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 500399 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int count_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result++;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 500399;
    printf("count of digits of %d: %d\n", number, count_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_digits() removes the last digit (n / 10) and adds one to result each
   time, until n reaches 0. main() applies it to 500399. */
// END

/* Caption: Count the even values in a list of integers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes samples and length.
   2. For each element, test samples[idx] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to count for every even number.
   4. Return count and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int samples[], int length) {
    int count = 0;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < length; idx++) {
        if (samples[idx] % 2 == 0) {
            count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {21, 66, 70, 88, 44, 68, 86, 24, 36, 68, 2};
    int length = sizeof(samples) / sizeof(samples[0]);
    printf("Count of even values = %d\n", count_even(samples, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_even() tests each element of samples with the % operator: a remainder
   of 0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so count goes up by one. main()
   prints how many of the 11 values are even. */
// END

/* Caption: Add two matrices element by element. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 3 and COLS as 4.
   2. Loop over every row r and column c.
   3. Store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print it. */
#define ROWS 3
#define COLS 4

int main(void) {
    int a[ROWS][COLS] = {{2, 0, 8, 8}, {9, 6, 6, 1}, {0, 4, 1, 8}};
    int b[ROWS][COLS] = {{0, 7, 3, 4}, {9, 7, 0, 4}, {5, 5, 1, 8}};
    int sum[ROWS][COLS];
    /* Each entry of the result is the sum of the matching entries. */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            sum[r][c] = a[r][c] + b[r][c];
            printf("%3d", sum[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Both matrices are 3x4 two-dimensional arrays. Two nested loops visit every
   row r and column c, store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print each row. */
// END

/* Caption: Print the factorial of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(value) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by every number from 2 to value.
   3. Return result.
   4. Print 15! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int value) {
    unsigned long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= value; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int value = 15;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", value, factorial(value));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() multiplies result by every number from 2 up to value. main()
   prints 15! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: Allocate an array with malloc and fill it with cubes. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 6 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill arr with cubes.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(arr) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 6;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *arr = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (arr == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        arr[i] = i * i * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", arr[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(arr);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 6 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills arr with cubes, the second prints them,
   and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I use insertion sort to put numbers in descending order in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the long array items.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the smaller values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(long items[], int length) {
    for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        long current = items[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && items[j] < current) {
            items[j + 1] = items[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        items[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long items[] = {20L, 50L, 87L, 61L, 97L, 96L, 97L};
    int length = sizeof(items) / sizeof(items[0]);
    insertion_sort(items, length);
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", items[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the smaller values
   of the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 7
   values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Implement a circular queue with an array. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 16 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 3 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 16

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 26);
    enqueue(&q, 23);
    enqueue(&q, 60);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 16 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 3 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Count the vowels in a sentence. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_vowels() with count = 0.
   2. For each character, check whether strchr finds it in aeiouAEIOU.
   3. Return count and print it. */
/* strchr finds the letter in the list of vowels, or returns NULL. */
int count_vowels(const char *text) {
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; text[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (strchr("aeiouAEIOU", text[i]) != NULL) {
            count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *sentence = "pointers store the address of another variable";
    printf("Vowels: %d\n", count_vowels(sentence));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_vowels() uses strchr to test whether each character is one of
   aeiouAEIOU and counts the matches. main() prints the number of vowels in the sentence. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to print the first 25 Fibonacci numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write fib(n) that returns n when n < 2.
   2. Otherwise return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2).
   3. Print fib(i) for i from 0 to 24. */
/* Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two before it. */
long fib(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return n;
    }
    return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2);
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", fib(i));
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fib() returns n for 0 and 1 and otherwise adds the two previous Fibonacci
   numbers by calling itself twice, which is simple but slow for large n. main() prints the
   first 25 numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: List the prime numbers below a limit. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Print every prime from 2 to 116. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int n = 2; n <= 116; n++) {
        if (is_prime(n)) {
            printf("%d ", n);
        }
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() tests every number from 2 to 116 and prints the primes. */
// END

/* Caption: Decide if 2099 is a leap year. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_leap(year).
   2. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year, unless it is divisible by 100.
   3. Years divisible by 400 are leap years again.
   4. Check 2099 and print the result. */
/* Leap years divide by 4, except centuries, which must divide by 400. */
int is_leap(int year) {
    return (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || year % 400 == 0;
}

int main(void) {
    int year = 2099;
    if (is_leap(year)) {
        printf("%d is a leap year\n", year);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not a leap year\n", year);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_leap() returns true for years divisible by 4, except century years,
   which must also be divisible by 400. main() checks 2099 and prints whether it is a leap
   year. */
// END

/* Caption: Use bubble sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the int array numbers.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for ascending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(int numbers[], int length) {
    for (int i = 0; i < length - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < length - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (numbers[j] > numbers[j + 1]) {
                int tmp = numbers[j];
                numbers[j] = numbers[j + 1];
                numbers[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {14, 46, 53, 77, 80, 67, 91, 52};
    int length = 8;
    bubble_sort(numbers, length);
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        printf("%d ", numbers[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through numbers again and again and swaps neighbours
   that are in the wrong order, so the largest values move to the end first. main() then
   prints the 8 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to return the minimum, maximum and average of an array in a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stats struct with min, max and average.
   2. Write array_stats() that fills one Stats in a loop.
   3. Return the struct.
   4. Print st.min, st.max and st.average. */
typedef struct {
    int min;
    int max;
    double average;
} Stats;

/* Pack several results into one struct and return it. */
Stats array_stats(const int v[], int n) {
    Stats s = {v[0], v[0], 0.0};
    double total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (v[i] < s.min) {
            s.min = v[i];
        }
        if (v[i] > s.max) {
            s.max = v[i];
        }
        total += v[i];
    }
    s.average = total / n;
    return s;
}

int main(void) {
    int items[] = {75, 44, 12, 87, 59};
    int n = sizeof(items) / sizeof(items[0]);
    Stats st = array_stats(items, n);
    printf("Min %d, Max %d, Average %.2f\n", st.min, st.max, st.average);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Stats groups three results. array_stats() fills one Stats while it loops
   over the 5 values and returns the whole struct, which is a clean way to return several
   results at once. main() reads them as st.min, st.max and st.average. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to add up all the numbers in an array of double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write total_of() that takes the array numbers and its length size.
   2. Start acc at 0 and add every element in a while loop.
   3. Return acc.
   4. In main(), fill numbers with 8 values and print the sum. */
/* Return the sum of the first n elements. */
double total_of(const double numbers[], int size) {
    double acc = 0;
    int k = 0;
    while (k < size) {
        acc += numbers[k];
        k++;
    }
    return acc;
}

int main(void) {
    double numbers[] = {95.0, 18.2, 28.8, 60.9, 24.8, 18.8, 50.0, 77.8};
    int size = sizeof(numbers) / sizeof(numbers[0]);
    printf("Sum: %.2f\n", total_of(numbers, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: total_of() receives the array numbers and its length size. It starts acc at
   0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills numbers
   with 8 double values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: Build a linked list, print it, and free it. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 69);
    head = push_front(head, 82);
    head = push_front(head, 44);
    head = push_front(head, 57);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Limit a number to a range with a three-parameter function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write clamp(value, low, high).
   2. Return low if the value is too small and high if it is too big.
   3. Otherwise return the value.
   4. Set low = 40 and high = 59 and print clamp() for -5, 45 and 101. */
/* Return value, but never less than low or more than high. */
int clamp(int value, int low, int high) {
    if (value < low) {
        return low;
    }
    if (value > high) {
        return high;
    }
    return value;
}

int main(void) {
    int low = 40, high = 59;
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", -5, clamp(-5, low, high));
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 45, clamp(45, low, high));
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 101, clamp(101, low, high));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: clamp() takes three parameters: the value and the two limits. It returns
   low when the value is too small, high when it is too big and the value itself otherwise.
   main() declares low = 40 and high = 59 on one line and clamps -5, 45 and 101. */
// END

   character with toupper(), which only changes lowercase letters. main() prints the

/* Caption: Write a C program to multiply two 3x3 matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define N as 3.
   2. For every i and j, add a[i][k] * b[k][j] over k into product[i][j].
   3. Print product row by row. */
#define N 3

int main(void) {
    int a[N][N] = {{7, 3, 5}, {0, 1, 8}, {3, 7, 8}};
    int b[N][N] = {{2, 2, 6}, {7, 7, 5}, {9, 1, 8}};
    int product[N][N] = {0};
    /* product[i][j] is row i of a times column j of b. */
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) {
                product[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            printf("%4d", product[i][j]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: For each entry product[i][j] the innermost loop adds a[i][k] * b[k][j] over
   k, which is row i of a times column j of b. main() multiplies two 3x3 matrices and
   prints the product. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes prices and count.
   2. Add the values into the double sum.
   3. Return sum / count.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double compute_mean(const long prices[], int count) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < count; idx++) {
        sum += prices[idx];
    }
    return sum / count;
}

int main(void) {
    long prices[] = {19L, 46L, 36L, 11L, 32L, 82L, 15L};
    int count = 7;
    printf("Average: %.2f\n", compute_mean(prices, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 7 values of prices into the double sum and divides
   by count, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to use dynamic memory to store the first 6 evens. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 6 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill table with evens.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(table) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 6;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *table = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (table == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        table[i] = 2 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", table[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(table);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 6 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills table with evens, the second prints them,
   and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Swap two variables using pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two int values.
   2. Save *first in tmp, copy *second into *first, then tmp into *second.
   3. In main(), print first and second, call swap(&first, &second) and print them
      again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(int *first, int *second) {
    int tmp = *first;
    *first = *second;
    *second = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    int first = 49, second = 51;
    printf("Before: %d %d\n", first, second);
    swap(&first, &second);
    printf("After:  %d %d\n", first, second);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of first and second, so writing through the
   pointers *first and *second changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during
   the exchange. main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and
   after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Reverse the characters of a word. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_string() for text.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap the two characters and move i and j inwards until they meet.
   4. Reverse rotor and print it. */
/* Swap characters from both ends until they meet in the middle. */
void reverse_string(char *text) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(text) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        char tmp = text[i];
        text[i] = text[j];
        text[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char text[] = "rotor";
    reverse_string(text);
    printf("%s\n", text);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_string() swaps characters from both ends of text, moving inwards
   until the two indexes meet. main() reverses the word rotor in place and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Implement a circular queue with an array. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 16 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 5 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 16

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 79);
    enqueue(&q, 94);
    enqueue(&q, 94);
    enqueue(&q, 99);
    enqueue(&q, 45);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 16 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 5 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Raise a number to an integer power with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 6 to the power 2. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("6^2 = %lld\n", power(6, 2));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 6 to the power 2. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I search an array for its largest value in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write max_of() that takes prices and length.
   2. Store prices[0] in m.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in m.
   4. Return m and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
double max_of(const double prices[], int length) {
    double m = prices[0];
    for (int k = 1; k < length; k++) {
        if (prices[k] > m) {
            m = prices[k];
        }
    }
    return m;
}

int main(void) {
    double prices[] = {73.7, 39.6, 33.7, 71.5};
    int length = 4;
    printf("Largest: %.2f\n", max_of(prices, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: max_of() takes the first element as the largest value so far and stores it
   in m. The loop compares every other element with m using > and keeps the largest one.
   main() prints the largest of the 4 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Use insertion sort to put numbers in descending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the long array readings.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the smaller values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(long readings[], int n) {
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
        long current = readings[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && readings[j] < current) {
            readings[j + 1] = readings[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        readings[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long readings[] = {24L, 68L, 83L, 75L, 76L, 42L, 17L};
    const int n = 7;
    insertion_sort(readings, n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", readings[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the smaller values
   of the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 7
   values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I generate the Fibonacci sequence in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with a = 0 and b = 1.
   2. Repeat 16 times and print a each time.
   3. Compute next = a + b, then set a = b and b = next. */
int main(void) {
    long a = 0, b = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", a);
        long next = a + b;
        a = b;
        b = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in a and b. Each round it prints a,
   then moves the pair forward: a becomes b and b becomes their sum. It prints the first 16
   Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the least common multiple of two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm: replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   2. Write lcm() as a / gcd(a, b) * b.
   3. Print the LCM of 129 and 84. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

/* lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b (divide first to avoid overflow). */
long lcm(int a, int b) {
    return (long)a / gcd(a, b) * b;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("lcm(129, 84) = %ld\n", lcm(129, 84));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. lcm() divides a by the gcd before multiplying by b, which avoids overflow.
   main() prints the LCM of 129 and 84. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to return a Duration struct built from a number of seconds. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Duration struct with hours, minutes and seconds.
   2. Write from_seconds() that fills it using / and %.
   3. Convert 50301 seconds and print the members. */
typedef struct {
    int hours;
    int minutes;
    int seconds;
} Duration;

Duration from_seconds(int total) {
    Duration d;
    d.hours = total / 3600;
    d.minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    d.seconds = total % 60;
    return d;
}

int main(void) {
    Duration d = from_seconds(50301);
    printf("%d h %d min %d s\n", d.hours, d.minutes, d.seconds);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: from_seconds() fills the three members of a Duration struct using / and %,
   then returns the struct. main() converts 50301 seconds and prints the members. */
// END

#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open data.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 2 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("data.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog\n");
