/* Caption: C program to write a function with four parameters that returns the maximum. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write max2() that returns the larger of two values.
   2. Write max_of_four() as max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d)).
   3. Print the largest of the four values. */
/* Return the larger of two values. */
int max2(int a, int b) {
    return a > b ? a : b;
}

/* Reuse max2 to compare four values. */
int max_of_four(int a, int b, int c, int d) {
    return max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d));
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 88, b = 30, c = 55, d = 34;
    printf("Largest: %d\n", max_of_four(a, b, c, d));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: max_of_four() takes four parameters and reuses the helper max2(), which
   returns the larger of two values: it compares a with b, c with d, and then the two
   winners. main() prints the largest of 88, 30, 55 and 34. */
// END

/* Caption: Create a singly linked list by inserting at the head. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 55);
    head = push_front(head, 67);
    head = push_front(head, 2);
    head = push_front(head, 76);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write mean() that takes ages and len.
   2. Add the values into the double sum.
   3. Return sum / len.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* The mean is the total divided by the count. */
double mean(const long ages[], int len) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int j = 0; j < len; j++) {
        sum += ages[j];
    }
    return sum / len;
}

int main(void) {
    long ages[] = {1L, 44L, 25L, 99L};
    int len = sizeof(ages) / sizeof(ages[0]);
    printf("Mean = %.2f\n", mean(ages, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: mean() adds the 4 values of ages into the double sum and divides by len, so
   the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers. main() prints it
   with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I search a sorted array by halving the search range each step in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set left to 0 and right to len - 1.
   3. While left <= right, compare the middle element middle with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 31. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int readings[], int len, int key) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = len - 1;
    while (left <= right) {
        int middle = left + (right - left) / 2;
        if (readings[middle] == key) {
            return middle;
        } else if (readings[middle] < key) {
            left = middle + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            right = middle - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int readings[] = {23, 30, 31, 47, 59, 61, 112, 121, 127, 136, 144, 194};
    int len = sizeof(readings) / sizeof(readings[0]);
    int index = binary_search(readings, len, 31);
    printf("Index of 31: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from left to
   right, compares the middle element middle with the key and throws away the half that
   cannot contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 31 and prints
   its index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to sort an array in descending order using insertion sort. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the long array data.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the smaller values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(long data[], int count) {
    for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {
        long current = data[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && data[j] < current) {
            data[j + 1] = data[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        data[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long data[] = {73L, 68L, 31L, 85L, 28L, 55L, 67L, 37L};
    int count = sizeof(data) / sizeof(data[0]);
    insertion_sort(data, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", data[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the smaller values
   of the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 8
   values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to check whether a word is a palindrome. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for line.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check civic and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *line) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(line) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (line[i] != line[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *line = "civic";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", line, is_palindrome(line) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word civic and prints
   the result. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to count how many odd numbers are in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_odd() that takes numbers and size.
   2. For each element, test numbers[k] % 2 != 0.
   3. Add one to count for every odd number.
   4. Return count and print it. */
/* A number is odd when the remainder after dividing by 2 is one. */
int count_odd(const int numbers[], int size) {
    int count = 0;
    for (int k = 0; k < size; k++) {
        if (numbers[k] % 2 != 0) {
            count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {90, 42, 94, 40, 42};
    int size = 5;
    printf("Odd numbers: %d\n", count_odd(numbers, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_odd() tests each element of numbers with the % operator: a remainder
   of 1 after dividing by 2 means the number is odd, so count goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 5 values are odd. */
// END

/* Caption: Check every element of an array to find a target value. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and needle.
   2. Compare each element with needle.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 184 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of needle, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int values[], int size, int needle) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        if (values[i] == needle) {
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int values[] = {56, 11, 43, 30, 50, 35, 72, 55};
    int size = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    int needle = 184;
    int pos = linear_search(values, size, needle);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", needle, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", needle);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of values one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to needle, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 184 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to write a function that returns the midpoint of two points as a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Point struct with x and y.
   2. Write midpoint() that returns a Point with the averages of x and y.
   3. Print mid.x and mid.y. */
typedef struct {
    double x;
    double y;
} Point;

/* A function can return a whole struct. */
Point midpoint(Point a, Point b) {
    Point m = {(a.x + b.x) / 2, (a.y + b.y) / 2};
    return m;
}

int main(void) {
    Point p = {-18, -2}, q = {-16, -13};
    Point mid = midpoint(p, q);
    printf("Midpoint: (%.1f, %.1f)\n", mid.x, mid.y);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: midpoint() takes two Point structs and returns a new Point whose x and y
   are the averages of theirs. main() declares p and q on one line, (-18, -2) and (-16,
   -13), and prints the midpoint using mid.x and mid.y. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I compute the sum of the digits of an integer in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Add n % 10 to result, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 888067 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int sum_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result += n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 888067;
    printf("sum of digits of %d: %d\n", number, sum_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_digits() adds the last digit (n % 10) to result and then removes it (n
   / 10) until no digits are left. main() applies it to 888067. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a function that swaps two double values through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two double values.
   2. Save *x in tmp, copy *y into *x, then tmp into *y.
   3. In main(), print x and y, call swap(&x, &y) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(double *x, double *y) {
    double tmp = *x;
    *x = *y;
    *y = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    double x = 6.2, y = 26.6;
    printf("Before: %.2f %.2f\n", x, y);
    swap(&x, &y);
    printf("After:  %.2f %.2f\n", x, y);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of x and y, so writing through the pointers
   *x and *y changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the largest number in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write find_max() that takes data and length.
   2. Store data[0] in m.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in m.
   4. Return m and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
double find_max(const double data[], int length) {
    double m = data[0];
    for (int j = 1; j < length; j++) {
        if (data[j] > m) {
            m = data[j];
        }
    }
    return m;
}

int main(void) {
    double data[] = {41.8, 79.2, 46.3, 52.3, 11.4, 30.1, 19.8, 68.0, 69.8};
    const int length = 9;
    printf("The largest value is %.2f\n", find_max(data, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: find_max() takes the first element as the largest value so far and stores
   it in m. The loop compares every other element with m using > and keeps the largest one.
   main() prints the largest of the 9 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to reverse an array by swapping from both ends. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for prices.
   2. Set start to the first index and end to the last.
   3. Swap prices[start] and prices[end], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when start meets end and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(int prices[], int count) {
    int start = 0;
    int end = count - 1;
    while (start < end) {
        int tmp = prices[start];
        prices[start] = prices[end];
        prices[end] = tmp;
        start++;
        end--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int prices[] = {20, 87, 82, 86, 42, 12, 35, 14, 15};
    int count = sizeof(prices) / sizeof(prices[0]);
    reverse_array(prices, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%d ", prices[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves start forward
   and end backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second
   array. main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I return the smallest element of an array of int values in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write min_of() that takes nums and size.
   2. Store nums[0] in smallest.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the smallest value in smallest.
   4. Return smallest and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the smallest value seen so far. */
int min_of(const int nums[], int size) {
    int smallest = nums[0];
    for (int k = 1; k < size; k++) {
        if (nums[k] < smallest) {
            smallest = nums[k];
        }
    }
    return smallest;
}

int main(void) {
    int nums[] = {53, 29, 1, 69, 61};
    int size = 5;
    printf("Smallest: %d\n", min_of(nums, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: min_of() takes the first element as the smallest value so far and stores it
   in smallest. The loop compares every other element with smallest using < and keeps the
   smallest one. main() prints the smallest of the 5 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Convert 474 to binary. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 474 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 474;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 16);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 474
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I use bubble sort to put numbers in ascending order in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the int array scores.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for ascending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(int scores[], int count) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < count - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (scores[j] > scores[j + 1]) {
                int tmp = scores[j];
                scores[j] = scores[j + 1];
                scores[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {30, 49, 76, 11, 98, 7, 68, 96};
    int count = sizeof(scores) / sizeof(scores[0]);
    bubble_sort(scores, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%d ", scores[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through scores again and again and swaps neighbours
   that are in the wrong order, so the largest values move to the end first. main() then
   prints the 8 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to implement insertion sort for an array of long values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the long array scores.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(long scores[], int n) {
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
        long current = scores[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && scores[j] > current) {
            scores[j + 1] = scores[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        scores[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long scores[] = {20L, 81L, 54L, 58L, 48L, 37L, 76L};
    int n = sizeof(scores) / sizeof(scores[0]);
    insertion_sort(scores, n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", scores[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 7 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to divide two integers and get both the quotient and the remainder. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write divide(a, b, &quotient, &remainder) that returns a bool.
   2. Return false if b is 0.
   3. Store a / b and a % b through the pointers and return true.
   4. Divide 472 by 12 and print the results or the error. */
/* Returns false for division by zero; otherwise stores both results. */
bool divide(int a, int b, int *quotient, int *remainder) {
    if (b == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *quotient = a / b;
    *remainder = a % b;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 472, b = 12;
    int q, r;
    if (divide(a, b, &q, &r)) {
        printf("%d / %d = %d remainder %d\n", a, b, q, r);
    } else {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: divide() has four parameters: two inputs and two pointers for the results.
   Its bool return value reports success, while the quotient and remainder are written
   through the pointers. main() divides 472 by 12 and prints both results. */
// END

   and prints the midpoint using mid.x and mid.y. */

/* Caption: C program to use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 98 and 165. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 98, y = 165;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 98 and 165. */
// END

/* Return the larger of two values. */
int max2(int a, int b) {
    return a > b ? a : b;

    return 0;

   returns the larger of two values: it compares a with b, c with d, and then the two
   winners. main() prints the largest of 93, 43, 63 and 5. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to search a sorted array by halving the search range each step. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set low to 0 and high to length - 1.
   3. While low <= high, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 91. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int scores[], int length, int key) {
    int low = 0;
    int high = length - 1;
    while (low <= high) {
        int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (scores[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (scores[mid] < key) {
            low = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            high = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {14, 17, 39, 77, 91, 108, 138, 161, 196};
    int length = sizeof(scores) / sizeof(scores[0]);
    int index = binary_search(scores, length, 91);
    printf("Index of 91: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from low to high,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 91 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I print all prime numbers up to 62 in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Print every prime from 2 to 62. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int n = 2; n <= 62; n++) {
        if (is_prime(n)) {
            printf("%d ", n);
        }
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() tests every number from 2 to 62 and prints the primes. */
// END

/* Caption: Implement a circular queue with an array. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 32 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 4 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 32

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 6);
    enqueue(&q, 26);
    enqueue(&q, 94);
    enqueue(&q, 62);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 32 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 4 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Use a struct to return several results from one function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stats struct with min, max and average.
   2. Write array_stats() that fills one Stats in a loop.
   3. Return the struct.
   4. Print st.min, st.max and st.average. */
typedef struct {
    int min;
    int max;
    double average;
} Stats;

/* Pack several results into one struct and return it. */
Stats array_stats(const int v[], int n) {
    Stats s = {v[0], v[0], 0.0};
    double total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (v[i] < s.min) {
            s.min = v[i];
        }
        if (v[i] > s.max) {
            s.max = v[i];
        }
        total += v[i];
    }
    s.average = total / n;
    return s;
}

int main(void) {
    int values[] = {69, 98, 40, 63, 23, 89, 26, 66, 73};
    int n = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    Stats st = array_stats(values, n);
    printf("Min %d, Max %d, Average %.2f\n", st.min, st.max, st.average);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Stats groups three results. array_stats() fills one Stats while it loops
   over the 9 values and returns the whole struct, which is a clean way to return several
   results at once. main() reads them as st.min, st.max and st.average. */
// END

/* Caption: Write lines to a text file and read them back. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open notes.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 2 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("notes.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "always free the memory you allocate\n");
    fprintf(file, "learning c teaches how computers work\n");
    fclose(file);

    /* Reopen the file for reading and print it line by line. */
    file = fopen("notes.txt", "r");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fopen() in write mode creates notes.txt, fprintf() writes 2 lines into it
   and fclose() saves it. The file is then opened again in read mode, and fgets() reads it
   back line by line into the buffer line, which is printed. Every fopen() result is
   checked for NULL. */
// END

/* Caption: Return two values from a function using pointer parameters. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write circle_measures() with the pointers area and circumference.
   2. Store PI * r * r and 2 * PI * r through them.
   3. Print both for a radius of 17.7. */
#define PI 3.14159265

void circle_measures(double radius, double *area, double *circumference) {
    *area = PI * radius * radius;
    *circumference = 2 * PI * radius;
}

int main(void) {
    double radius = 17.7;
    double area, circumference;
    circle_measures(radius, &area, &circumference);
    printf("Area: %.2f, Circumference: %.2f\n", area, circumference);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: circle_measures() computes two results from one radius and stores them
   through the pointers area and circumference. main() declares both variables on one line,
   passes their addresses and prints the results for a radius of 17.7. */
// END

/* Caption: Check every element of an array to find a target value. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and key.
   2. Compare each element with key.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 4 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of key, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int numbers[], int count, int key) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (numbers[i] == key) {
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {93, 4, 28, 21, 18, 77, 20, 98, 4};
    int count = 9;
    int key = 4;
    int pos = linear_search(numbers, count, key);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", key, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", key);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of numbers one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to key, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 4 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

#include <stdio.h>

/* Leap years divide by 4, except centuries, which must divide by 400. */
int is_leap(int year) {

int main(void) {

/* Caption: Write a C program to build a linked list, print it, and free it. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 33);
    head = push_front(head, 35);
    head = push_front(head, 62);
    head = push_front(head, 96);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to divide two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Read num1 and num2.
   2. If num2 is 0, print an error and stop.
   3. Print num1 / num2 and the remainder num1 % num2. */
int main(void) {
    int num1, num2;
    printf("Enter two numbers: ");
    if (scanf("%d %d", &num1, &num2) != 2) {
        printf("Invalid input\n");
        return 1;
    }
    /* Dividing by zero is not allowed, so check first. */
    if (num2 == 0) {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
        return 1;
    }
    /* Integer division drops the fraction; % gives the remainder. */
    printf("Quotient: %d, remainder: %d\n", num1 / num2, num1 % num2);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The program reads num1 and num2 from the keyboard with scanf and stops with
   a message if the input is not valid. It checks that num2 is not zero, then prints num1 /
   num2, where integer division drops the fraction, and the remainder num1 % num2. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to find the number of digits in an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Divide n by 10 and add one to result.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 602847 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int count_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result++;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 602847;
    printf("count of digits of %d: %d\n", number, count_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_digits() removes the last digit (n / 10) and adds one to result each
   time, until n reaches 0. main() applies it to 602847. */
// END

/* Caption: Add two matrices element by element. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 4 and COLS as 2.
   2. Loop over every row r and column c.
   3. Store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print it. */
#define ROWS 4
#define COLS 2

int main(void) {
    int a[ROWS][COLS] = {{9, 4}, {3, 7}, {3, 0}, {6, 2}};
    int b[ROWS][COLS] = {{0, 5}, {4, 8}, {1, 3}, {6, 5}};
    int sum[ROWS][COLS];
    /* Each entry of the result is the sum of the matching entries. */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            sum[r][c] = a[r][c] + b[r][c];
            printf("%3d", sum[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Both matrices are 4x2 two-dimensional arrays. Two nested loops visit every
   row r and column c, store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print each row. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to implement a circular queue with an array. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 8 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 6 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 8

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 36);
    enqueue(&q, 69);
    enqueue(&q, 97);
    enqueue(&q, 15);
    enqueue(&q, 32);
    enqueue(&q, 95);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 8 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 6 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: How do I count how many odd numbers are in an array in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_odd() that takes samples and len.
   2. For each element, test samples[i] % 2 != 0.
   3. Add one to found for every odd number.
   4. Return found and print it. */
/* A number is odd when the remainder after dividing by 2 is one. */
int count_odd(const int samples[], int len) {
    int found = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < len) {
        if (samples[i] % 2 != 0) {
            found++;
        }
        i++;
    }
    return found;
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {28, 52, 50, 75, 31, 79, 40, 39};
    const int len = 8;
    printf("Odd numbers: %d\n", count_odd(samples, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_odd() tests each element of samples with the % operator: a remainder
   of 1 after dividing by 2 means the number is odd, so found goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 8 values are odd. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to find the largest number in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write find_max() that takes scores and size.
   2. Store scores[0] in m.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in m.
   4. Return m and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
double find_max(const double scores[], int size) {
    double m = scores[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
        if (scores[i] > m) {
            m = scores[i];
        }
    }
    return m;
}

int main(void) {
    double scores[] = {46.0, 17.7, 83.7, 30.4, 9.5, 56.4, 54.6, 81.7, 90.6, 81.3};
    int size = 10;
    printf("The largest value is %.2f\n", find_max(scores, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: find_max() takes the first element as the largest value so far and stores
   it in m. The loop compares every other element with m using > and keeps the largest one.
   main() prints the largest of the 10 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to search an array for its smallest value. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write smallest_value() that takes marks and length.
   2. Store marks[0] in current.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the smallest value in current.
   4. Return current and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the smallest value seen so far. */
int smallest_value(const int marks[], int length) {
    int current = marks[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        if (marks[i] < current) {
            current = marks[i];
        }
    }
    return current;
}

int main(void) {
    int marks[] = {23, 29, 78, 82};
    int length = sizeof(marks) / sizeof(marks[0]);
    printf("The smallest value is %d\n", smallest_value(marks, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: smallest_value() takes the first element as the smallest value so far and
   stores it in current. The loop compares every other element with current using < and
   keeps the smallest one. main() prints the smallest of the 4 values. */
// END

   3. Print the result. */

}
/* Explanation: Instead of a loop it uses Gauss's formula n * (n + 1) / 2, which gives the
   sum of 1 to 5 in one step. */

/* Caption: Check whether a number is prime. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Check 178 and print the result. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 178;
    printf("%d %s prime\n", number, is_prime(number) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() checks 178 and prints whether it is prime. */
// END

/* Caption: Test if "bridge" reads the same backwards. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for str.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check bridge and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *str) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(str) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (str[i] != str[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *str = "bridge";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", str, is_palindrome(str) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word bridge and
   prints the result. */
// END

    }
    return 0;

   x + c. main() declares m = 0.1 and c = 6.7 on one line and prints y for every x from 0
   to 3. */

/* Caption: Reverse the elements of an array in place. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for scores.
   2. Set left to the first index and right to the last.
   3. Swap scores[left] and scores[right], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when left meets right and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(int scores[], int len) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = len - 1;
    while (left < right) {
        int tmp = scores[left];
        scores[left] = scores[right];
        scores[right] = tmp;
        left++;
        right--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {7, 73, 29, 73};
    const int len = 4;
    reverse_array(scores, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%d ", scores[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves left forward
   and right backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second
   array. main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to write a function that swaps two double values through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two double values.
   2. Save *a in tmp, copy *b into *a, then tmp into *b.
   3. In main(), print a and b, call swap(&a, &b) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(double *a, double *b) {
    double tmp = *a;
    *a = *b;
    *b = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    double a = 1.7, b = 64.6;
    printf("Before: %.2f %.2f\n", a, b);
    swap(&a, &b);
    printf("After:  %.2f %.2f\n", a, b);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of a and b, so writing through the pointers
   *a and *b changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 396
   in binary. */

/* Caption: C program to print an integer with its digits reversed. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Multiply result by 10, add n % 10, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 603558 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int reverse_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result = result * 10 + n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 603558;
    printf("reverse of digits of %d: %d\n", number, reverse_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_digits() shifts result one place left (result * 10) and adds the
   last digit of n, which reverses the order. main() applies it to 603558. */

/* Caption: How do I allocate an array with malloc and fill it with evens in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 13 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill list with evens.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(list) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 13;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *list = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (list == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        list[i] = 2 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", list[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(list);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 13 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it
   fails, which the program checks. The first loop fills list with evens, the second prints
   them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I compute the LCM of two integers using the GCD in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm: replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   2. Write lcm() as a / gcd(a, b) * b.
   3. Print the LCM of 162 and 256. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

/* lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b (divide first to avoid overflow). */
long lcm(int a, int b) {
    return (long)a / gcd(a, b) * b;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("lcm(162, 256) = %ld\n", lcm(162, 256));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. lcm() divides a by the gcd before multiplying by b, which avoids overflow.
   main() prints the LCM of 162 and 256. */
// END

/* Caption: Show the Fibonacci series with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with first = 0 and second = 1.
   2. Repeat 8 times and print first each time.
   3. Compute next = first + second, then set first = second and second = next. */
int main(void) {
    long first = 0, second = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", first);
        long next = first + second;
        first = second;
        second = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in first and second. Each round it
   prints first, then moves the pair forward: first becomes second and second becomes their
   sum. It prints the first 8 Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to sum a double array with a helper function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write array_sum() that takes the array samples and its length size.
   2. Start result at 0 and add every element in a for loop.
   3. Return result.
   4. In main(), fill samples with 4 values and print the sum. */
/* Add every element to a running total. */
double array_sum(const double samples[], int size) {
    double result = 0;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < size; idx++) {
        result += samples[idx];
    }
    return result;

    int size = 4;
    printf("Sum: %.2f\n", array_sum(samples, size));

   result at 0, adds every element to it in a for loop and returns the total. main() fills
   samples with 4 double values and prints their sum. */

/* Caption: How do I compute the distance between two points using a struct in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Point struct with x and y.
   2. Write distance() using sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy).
   3. Print the distance between p and q. */
typedef struct {
    double x;
    double y;
} Point;

/* Pythagoras: sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). */
double distance(Point a, Point b) {
    double dx = b.x - a.x;
    double dy = b.y - a.y;
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

int main(void) {
    Point p = {-6, 0};
    Point q = {9, 3};
    printf("Distance: %.3f\n", distance(p, q));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Point is a typedef struct with x and y. distance() uses Pythagoras, sqrt(dx
   * dx + dy * dy), to measure the gap between the two points, and main() prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to implement a simple linked list with malloc and free. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Item with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 6 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Item {
    int value;
    struct Item *next;
} Item;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Item *push_front(Item *head, int value) {
    Item *node = malloc(sizeof(Item));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Item *head) {
    for (const Item *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Item *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Item *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Item *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 27);
    head = push_front(head, 82);
    head = push_front(head, 90);
    head = push_front(head, 29);
    head = push_front(head, 14);
    head = push_front(head, 8);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Item holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 6
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */

   binary. */

/* Caption: Build a FIFO queue using a ring buffer. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 16 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 4 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 16

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 75);
    enqueue(&q, 48);
    enqueue(&q, 60);
    enqueue(&q, 70);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 16 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 4 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to compute the product of two square matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define N as 3.
   2. For every i and j, add a[i][k] * b[k][j] over k into product[i][j].
   3. Print product row by row. */
#define N 3

int main(void) {
    int a[N][N] = {{1, 8, 3}, {1, 3, 1}, {4, 8, 6}};
    int b[N][N] = {{0, 9, 5}, {6, 5, 0}, {4, 3, 5}};
    int product[N][N] = {0};
    /* product[i][j] is row i of a times column j of b. */
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) {
                product[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            printf("%4d", product[i][j]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: For each entry product[i][j] the innermost loop adds a[i][k] * b[k][j] over
   k, which is row i of a times column j of b. main() multiplies two 3x3 matrices and
   prints the product. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I reverse an array by swapping from both ends in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for items.
   2. Set left to the first index and right to the last.
   3. Swap items[left] and items[right], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when left meets right and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(long items[], int count) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = count - 1;
    while (left < right) {
        long tmp = items[left];
        items[left] = items[right];
        items[right] = tmp;
        left++;
        right--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long items[] = {55L, 42L, 8L, 12L, 45L, 89L};
    const int count = 6;
    reverse_array(items, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", items[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves left forward
   and right backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second
   array. main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* true when low <= x <= high */
bool in_range(int x, int low, int high) {

}

int main(void) {
    int value = 0, low = 37, high = 46;

/* Caption: Build a linked list, print it, and free it. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 6 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 25);
    head = push_front(head, 76);
    head = push_front(head, 46);
    head = push_front(head, 17);
    head = push_front(head, 5);
    head = push_front(head, 48);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 6
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a function that swaps two long values through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two long values.
   2. Save *x in tmp, copy *y into *x, then tmp into *y.
   3. In main(), print x and y, call swap(&x, &y) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(long *x, long *y) {
    long tmp = *x;
    *x = *y;
    *y = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    long x = 65L, y = 33L;
    printf("Before: %ld %ld\n", x, y);
    swap(&x, &y);
    printf("After:  %ld %ld\n", x, y);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of x and y, so writing through the pointers
   *x and *y changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to sort an array in ascending order using insertion sort. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the long array nums.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(long nums[], int count) {
    for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {
        long current = nums[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && nums[j] > current) {
            nums[j + 1] = nums[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        nums[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long nums[] = {54L, 25L, 83L, 20L, 69L, 60L, 72L, 86L, 31L, 12L};
    int count = 10;
    insertion_sort(nums, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", nums[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 10 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to return two values from a function using pointer parameters. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_and_average() with the pointers sum and average.
   2. Add the values into *sum.
   3. Store *sum / n in *average.
   4. Declare total and mean, pass their addresses and print them. */
void sum_and_average(const double v[], int n, double *sum, double *average) {
    *sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        *sum += v[i];
    }
    *average = *sum / n;
}

int main(void) {
    double prices[] = {22.6, 37.0, 78.4, 90.0, 98.6};
    int n = sizeof(prices) / sizeof(prices[0]);
    double total, mean;
    sum_and_average(prices, n, &total, &mean);
    printf("Sum: %.2f, Average: %.2f\n", total, mean);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_and_average() takes the array, its length and two pointers. It adds up
   the 5 values through *sum and then stores *sum / n in *average. main() declares total
   and mean on one line and passes their addresses. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes nums and len.
   2. Add the values into the double total.
   3. Return total / len.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double compute_mean(const long nums[], int len) {
    double total = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        total += nums[i];
    }
    return total / len;
}

int main(void) {
    long nums[] = {91L, 37L, 18L, 75L, 27L};
    int len = 5;
    printf("Mean = %.2f\n", compute_mean(nums, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 5 values of nums into the double total and divides
   by len, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Write lines to a text file and read them back. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open output.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 2 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("output.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "c gives you direct control over memory\n");
    fprintf(file, "always free the memory you allocate\n");
    fclose(file);

    /* Reopen the file for reading and print it line by line. */
    file = fopen("output.txt", "r");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fopen() in write mode creates output.txt, fprintf() writes 2 lines into it
   and fclose() saves it. The file is then opened again in read mode, and fgets() reads it
   back line by line into the buffer line, which is printed. Every fopen() result is
   checked for NULL. */
// END

/* Caption: Raise a number to an integer power with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 8 to the power 8. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("8^8 = %lld\n", power(8, 8));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 8 to the power 8. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to find the least common multiple of two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm: replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   2. Write lcm() as a / gcd(a, b) * b.
   3. Print the LCM of 161 and 269. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

/* lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b (divide first to avoid overflow). */
long lcm(int a, int b) {
    return (long)a / gcd(a, b) * b;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("lcm(161, 269) = %ld\n", lcm(161, 269));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. lcm() divides a by the gcd before multiplying by b, which avoids overflow.
   main() prints the LCM of 161 and 269. */
// END

/* Caption: Implement insertion sort for an array of double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the double array values.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(double values[], int length) {
    for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        double current = values[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && values[j] > current) {
            values[j + 1] = values[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        values[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double values[] = {18.6, 11.6, 87.4, 13.4, 71.6, 66.3, 63.1};
    int length = 7;
    insertion_sort(values, length);
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", values[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 7 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I add two 3x4 matrices in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 3 and COLS as 4.
   2. Loop over every row r and column c.
   3. Store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print it. */
#define ROWS 3
#define COLS 4

int main(void) {
    int a[ROWS][COLS] = {{1, 2, 2, 4}, {5, 4, 5, 7}, {0, 3, 3, 2}};
    int b[ROWS][COLS] = {{6, 9, 4, 2}, {1, 8, 8, 3}, {6, 8, 0, 7}};
    int sum[ROWS][COLS];
    /* Each entry of the result is the sum of the matching entries. */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            sum[r][c] = a[r][c] + b[r][c];
            printf("%3d", sum[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Both matrices are 3x4 two-dimensional arrays. Two nested loops visit every
   row r and column c, store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print each row. */
// END

/* Caption: Return two values from a function using pointer parameters. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write min_max() with the array, its length and the pointers min and max.
   2. Start both at the first element.
   3. Update *min and *max while looping over the rest.
   4. Declare smallest and largest, pass their addresses and print them. */
/* One pass finds both results; they are stored through the pointers. */
void min_max(const int samples[], int length, int *min, int *max) {
    *min = samples[0];
    *max = samples[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        if (samples[i] < *min) {
            *min = samples[i];
        }
        if (samples[i] > *max) {
            *max = samples[i];
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {3, 87, 69, 15, 91, 58, 58, 6};
    const int length = 8;
    int smallest, largest;
    min_max(samples, length, &smallest, &largest);
    printf("Min: %d, Max: %d\n", smallest, largest);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: A C function can return only one value, so min_max() returns void and
   writes its two results through the pointer parameters min and max. main() declares
   smallest and largest on one line and passes their addresses with &, then prints both
   results for the 8 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to convert seconds into hours, minutes and seconds. */

/* Plan:
   1. Write split_seconds() with the pointers hours, minutes and seconds.
   2. Store total / 3600, (total % 3600) / 60 and total % 60 through them.
   3. Convert 30089 seconds and print the parts. */
void split_seconds(int total, int *hours, int *minutes, int *seconds) {
    *hours = total / 3600;
    *minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    *seconds = total % 60;
}

int main(void) {
    int total = 30089;
    int h, m, s;
    split_seconds(total, &h, &m, &s);
    printf("%d seconds = %d h %d min %d s\n", total, h, m, s);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: split_seconds() fills three results through pointers: hours is total /
   3600, minutes is what is left divided by 60, and seconds is total % 60. main() declares
   h, m and s on one line and converts 30089 seconds. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to count how many even numbers are in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes data and length.
   2. For each element, test data[j] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to count for every even number.
   4. Return count and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int data[], int length) {
    int count = 0;
    for (int j = 0; j < length; j++) {
        if (data[j] % 2 == 0) {
            count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    int data[] = {57, 40, 74, 7, 82};
    int length = sizeof(data) / sizeof(data[0]);
    printf("Even numbers: %d\n", count_even(data, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_even() tests each element of data with the % operator: a remainder of
   0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so count goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 5 values are even. */
// END

/* Caption: Check whether a number is prime. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Check 363 and print the result. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 363;
    printf("%d %s prime\n", number, is_prime(number) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() checks 363 and prints whether it is prime. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I return the smallest element of an array of double values in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write smallest_value() that takes samples and n.
   2. Store samples[0] in smallest.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the smallest value in smallest.
   4. Return smallest and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the smallest value seen so far. */
double smallest_value(const double samples[], int n) {
    double smallest = samples[0];
    for (int j = 1; j < n; j++) {
        if (samples[j] < smallest) {
            smallest = samples[j];
        }
    }
    return smallest;
}

int main(void) {
    double samples[] = {18.8, 83.8, 76.1, 22.7, 23.5};
    int n = 5;
    printf("Smallest: %.2f\n", smallest_value(samples, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: smallest_value() takes the first element as the smallest value so far and
   stores it in smallest. The loop compares every other element with smallest using < and
   keeps the smallest one. main() prints the smallest of the 5 values. */
// END

/* F = C * 9 / 5 + 32 */

}

/* Caption: Implement bubble sort for an array of long values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the long array nums.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for descending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(long nums[], int count) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < count - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (nums[j] < nums[j + 1]) {
                long tmp = nums[j];
                nums[j] = nums[j + 1];
                nums[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long nums[] = {55L, 28L, 91L, 4L, 16L, 39L, 93L, 52L, 42L};
    const int count = 9;
    bubble_sort(nums, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", nums[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through nums again and again and swaps neighbours that
   are in the wrong order, so the smallest values move to the end first. main() then prints
   the 9 values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Save text to a file with fprintf and print it with fgets. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open output.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 3 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("output.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "the compiler turns source code into machine code\n");
    fprintf(file, "c gives you direct control over memory\n");
    fprintf(file, "pointers store the address of another variable\n");

    /* Reopen the file for reading and print it line by line. */
    file = fopen("output.txt", "r");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}

   and fclose() saves it. The file is then opened again in read mode, and fgets() reads it
   back line by line into the buffer line, which is printed. Every fopen() result is

/* Caption: Convert 138 to binary. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 138 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 138;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 8);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 138
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to reverse the characters of a word. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_string() for buffer.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap the two characters and move i and j inwards until they meet.
   4. Reverse stats and print it. */
/* Swap characters from both ends until they meet in the middle. */
void reverse_string(char *buffer) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(buffer) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        char tmp = buffer[i];
        buffer[i] = buffer[j];
        buffer[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char buffer[] = "stats";
    reverse_string(buffer);
    printf("%s\n", buffer);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_string() swaps characters from both ends of buffer, moving inwards
   until the two indexes meet. main() reverses the word stats in place and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the arithmetic mean of 4 int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write array_average() that takes scores and count.
   2. Add the values into the double sum.
   3. Return sum / count.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double array_average(const int scores[], int count) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    int j = 0;
    while (j < count) {
        sum += scores[j];
        j++;
    }
    return sum / count;
}

    const int count = 4;
    printf("Mean = %.2f\n", array_average(scores, count));
    return 0;

   by count, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */

/* Caption: C program to write a function that returns the quotient and remainder through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write divide(a, b, &quotient, &remainder) that returns a bool.
   2. Return false if b is 0.
   3. Store a / b and a % b through the pointers and return true.
   4. Divide 23 by 5 and print the results or the error. */
/* Returns false for division by zero; otherwise stores both results. */
bool divide(int a, int b, int *quotient, int *remainder) {
    if (b == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *quotient = a / b;
    *remainder = a % b;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 23, b = 5;
    int q, r;
    if (divide(a, b, &q, &r)) {
        printf("%d / %d = %d remainder %d\n", a, b, q, r);
    } else {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: divide() has four parameters: two inputs and two pointers for the results.
   Its bool return value reports success, while the quotient and remainder are written
   through the pointers. main() divides 23 by 5 and prints both results. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to use dynamic memory to store the first 14 evens. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 14 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill table with evens.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(table) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 14;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *table = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (table == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        table[i] = 2 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", table[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(table);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 14 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it
   fails, which the program checks. The first loop fills table with evens, the second
   prints them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the largest number in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write find_max() that takes samples and count.
   2. Store samples[0] in m.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in m.
   4. Return m and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
long find_max(const long samples[], int count) {

    for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {

    printf("Largest: %ld\n", find_max(samples, count));
    return 0;
}

   it in m. The loop compares every other element with m using > and keeps the largest one.
   main() prints the largest of the 4 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to turn the rows of a 4x4 matrix into columns. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 4 and COLS as 4.
   2. Copy m[r][c] into t[c][r] for every element.
   3. Print t row by row. */
#define ROWS 4
#define COLS 4

int main(void) {
    int m[ROWS][COLS] = {{9, 3, 9, 1}, {0, 2, 4, 5}, {6, 1, 3, 7}, {0, 6, 8, 3}};
    int t[COLS][ROWS];
    /* Element (r, c) moves to (c, r). */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            t[c][r] = m[r][c];
        }
    }
    for (int r = 0; r < COLS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < ROWS; c++) {
            printf("%3d", t[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The nested loops copy m[r][c] into t[c][r], so the 4x4 matrix becomes 4x4.
   A second pair of loops prints the result. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the largest of four numbers with a function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write max2() that returns the larger of two values.
   2. Write max_of_four() as max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d)).
   3. Print the largest of the four values. */
/* Return the larger of two values. */
int max2(int a, int b) {
    return a > b ? a : b;
}

/* Reuse max2 to compare four values. */
int max_of_four(int a, int b, int c, int d) {
    return max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d));
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 51, b = 25, c = 24, d = 72;
    printf("Largest: %d\n", max_of_four(a, b, c, d));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: max_of_four() takes four parameters and reuses the helper max2(), which
   returns the larger of two values: it compares a with b, c with d, and then the two
   winners. main() prints the largest of 51, 25, 24 and 72. */
// END
