/* Caption: Program to use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 11 and 34. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 11, y = 34;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 11 and 34. */
// END

/* Caption: Reverse the elements of an array in place. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for scores.
   2. Set start to the first index and end to the last.
   3. Swap scores[start] and scores[end], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when start meets end and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(int scores[], int count) {
    int start = 0;
    int end = count - 1;
    while (start < end) {
        int tmp = scores[start];
        scores[start] = scores[end];
        scores[end] = tmp;
        start++;
        end--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {77, 42, 42, 42, 32};
    int count = sizeof(scores) / sizeof(scores[0]);
    reverse_array(scores, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%d ", scores[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves start forward
   and end backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second
   array. main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to find the total of all elements in an array using a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_values() that takes the array marks and its length size.
   2. Start sum at 0 and add every element in a for loop.
   3. Return sum.
   4. In main(), fill marks with 6 values and print the sum. */
/* Add every element to a running total. */
double sum_values(const double marks[], int size) {
    double sum = 0;
    for (int j = 0; j < size; j++) {
        sum += marks[j];
    }
    return sum;
}

int main(void) {
    double marks[] = {33.1, 22.8, 20.6, 59.4, 13.5, 34.2};
    int size = 6;
    printf("Total = %.2f\n", sum_values(marks, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_values() receives the array marks and its length size. It starts sum at
   0, adds every element to it in a for loop and returns the total. main() fills marks with
   6 double values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to add two matrices element by element. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 2 and COLS as 4.
   2. Loop over every row r and column c.
   3. Store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print it. */
#define ROWS 2
#define COLS 4

int main(void) {
    int a[ROWS][COLS] = {{5, 6, 9, 9}, {4, 5, 2, 1}};
    int b[ROWS][COLS] = {{9, 5, 4, 1}, {4, 6, 0, 5}};
    int sum[ROWS][COLS];
    /* Each entry of the result is the sum of the matching entries. */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            sum[r][c] = a[r][c] + b[r][c];
            printf("%3d", sum[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Both matrices are 2x4 two-dimensional arrays. Two nested loops visit every
   row r and column c, store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print each row. */
// END

/* Caption: Build a linked list, print it, and free it. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ListNode with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 3 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct ListNode {
    int value;
    struct ListNode *next;
} ListNode;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
ListNode *push_front(ListNode *head, int value) {
    ListNode *node = malloc(sizeof(ListNode));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const ListNode *head) {
    for (const ListNode *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(ListNode *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        ListNode *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    ListNode *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 16);
    head = push_front(head, 18);
    head = push_front(head, 90);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each ListNode holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 3
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Sort an array in ascending order using insertion sort. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the double array ages.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(double ages[], int count) {
    for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {
        double current = ages[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && ages[j] > current) {
            ages[j + 1] = ages[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        ages[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double ages[] = {74.7, 13.1, 75.6, 92.8, 91.3};
    const int count = 5;
    insertion_sort(ages, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", ages[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 5 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

long long power(int base, int exp) {

/* Caption: Use dynamic memory to store the first 8 squares. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 8 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill table with squares.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(table) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 8;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *table = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (table == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        table[i] = i * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", table[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(table);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 8 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills table with squares, the second prints
   them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I search an array for its smallest value in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write find_min() that takes samples and n.
   2. Store samples[0] in smallest.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the smallest value in smallest.
   4. Return smallest and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the smallest value seen so far. */
int find_min(const int samples[], int n) {
    int smallest = samples[0];
    for (int idx = 1; idx < n; idx++) {
        if (samples[idx] < smallest) {
            smallest = samples[idx];

    return smallest;
}

    const int n = 9;
    printf("Smallest: %d\n", find_min(samples, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: find_min() takes the first element as the smallest value so far and stores
   it in smallest. The loop compares every other element with smallest using < and keeps
   the smallest one. main() prints the smallest of the 9 values. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I implement a circular queue with an array in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 8 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 3 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 8

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 4);
    enqueue(&q, 61);
    enqueue(&q, 96);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 8 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 3 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Program to count the even values in a list of integers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes nums and count.
   2. For each element, test nums[i] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to tally for every even number.
   4. Return tally and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int nums[], int count) {
    int tally = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (nums[i] % 2 == 0) {
            tally++;
        }
    }
    return tally;
}

int main(void) {
    int nums[] = {17, 79, 37, 39, 12, 38, 20, 25, 77, 97, 82};
    int count = sizeof(nums) / sizeof(nums[0]);
    printf("Even numbers: %d\n", count_even(nums, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_even() tests each element of nums with the % operator: a remainder of
   0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so tally goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 11 values are even. */
// END

/* Caption: Generate the Fibonacci sequence. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write fib(n) that returns n when n < 2.
   2. Otherwise return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2).
   3. Print fib(i) for i from 0 to 22. */
/* Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two before it. */
long fib(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return n;
    }
    return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2);
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 23; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", fib(i));
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fib() returns n for 0 and 1 and otherwise adds the two previous Fibonacci
   numbers by calling itself twice, which is simple but slow for large n. main() prints the
   first 23 numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Reverse a string in place. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_string() for word.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap the two characters and move i and j inwards until they meet.
   4. Reverse noon and print it. */
/* Swap characters from both ends until they meet in the middle. */
void reverse_string(char *word) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(word) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        char tmp = word[i];
        word[i] = word[j];
        word[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char word[] = "noon";
    reverse_string(word);
    printf("%s\n", word);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_string() swaps characters from both ends of word, moving inwards
   until the two indexes meet. main() reverses the word noon in place and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to return the largest element of an array of double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write largest_value() that takes numbers and length.
   2. Store numbers[0] in largest.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in largest.
   4. Return largest and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
double largest_value(const double numbers[], int length) {
    double largest = numbers[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        if (numbers[i] > largest) {
            largest = numbers[i];
        }
    }
    return largest;
}

int main(void) {
    double numbers[] = {91.1, 26.2, 17.2, 66.8, 55.5, 95.0};
    int length = sizeof(numbers) / sizeof(numbers[0]);
    printf("Largest: %.2f\n", largest_value(numbers, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: largest_value() takes the first element as the largest value so far and
   stores it in largest. The loop compares every other element with largest using > and
   keeps the largest one. main() prints the largest of the 6 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Count how many words are separated by spaces in a string. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <ctype.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_words() with words = 0 and an in_word flag.
   2. A space ends a word; a non-space after a space starts a new word and adds one to
      words.
   3. Return words and print it. */
/* A new word starts when a non-space follows a space (or the start). */
int count_words(const char *text) {
    int words = 0;
    int in_word = 0;
    for (int i = 0; text[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (isspace((unsigned char)text[i])) {
            in_word = 0;
        } else if (!in_word) {
            in_word = 1;
            words++;
        }
    }
    return words;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *sentence = "keep functions short and focused";
    printf("Words: %d\n", count_words(sentence));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_words() uses the flag in_word: a new word starts when a non-space
   character follows a space or the start of the text. main() prints the number of words in
   the sentence. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I return both the smallest and the largest value of an array through pointers in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write min_max() with the array, its length and the pointers min and max.
   2. Start both at the first element.
   3. Update *min and *max while looping over the rest.
   4. Declare lowest and highest, pass their addresses and print them. */
/* One pass finds both results; they are stored through the pointers. */
void min_max(const int data[], int size, int *min, int *max) {
    *min = data[0];
    *max = data[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
        if (data[i] < *min) {
            *min = data[i];
        }
        if (data[i] > *max) {
            *max = data[i];
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int data[] = {47, 75, 47, 74, 87};
    int size = 5;
    int lowest, highest;
    min_max(data, size, &lowest, &highest);
    printf("Min: %d, Max: %d\n", lowest, highest);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: A C function can return only one value, so min_max() returns void and
   writes its two results through the pointer parameters min and max. main() declares
   lowest and highest on one line and passes their addresses with &, then prints both
   results for the 5 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to test if "deified" reads the same backwards. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for text.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check deified and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *text) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(text) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (text[i] != text[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *text = "deified";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", text, is_palindrome(text) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word deified and
   prints the result. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to search an array for a value and print its position. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and target.
   2. Compare each element with target.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 67 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of target, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int numbers[], int length, int target) {
    for (int idx = 0; idx < length; idx++) {
        if (numbers[idx] == target) {
            return idx;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {16, 54, 28, 45, 11, 40, 67, 19, 66};
    const int length = 9;
    int target = 67;
    int pos = linear_search(numbers, length, target);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", target, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", target);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of numbers one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to target, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 67 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Build a fixed-size integer stack in C. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stack with room for 16 items and a top counter.
   2. Write push() and pop(), returning false when the stack is full or empty.
   3. Push 3 values.
   4. Pop and print until the stack is empty. */
#define CAPACITY 16

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int top;   /* number of items on the stack */
} Stack;

bool push(Stack *s, int value) {
    if (s->top == CAPACITY) {
        return false;   /* stack is full */
    }
    s->items[s->top++] = value;
    return true;
}

bool pop(Stack *s, int *value) {
    if (s->top == 0) {
        return false;   /* stack is empty */
    }
    *value = s->items[--s->top];
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Stack s = {.top = 0};
    push(&s, 26);
    push(&s, 65);
    push(&s, 46);
    int value;
    /* Items come back out in reverse order (last in, first out). */
    while (pop(&s, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Stack keeps up to 16 items in an array, and top counts how many are
   stored. push() adds at the top and pop() removes from the top; both return false when
   they cannot. main() pushes 3 values and pops them all, so they come out in reverse order
   (last in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Print the binary representation of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 880 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 880;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 16);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 880
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to use dynamic memory to store the first 9 squares. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 9 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill table with squares.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(table) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 9;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *table = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (table == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        table[i] = i * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", table[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(table);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 9 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills table with squares, the second prints
   them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to implement insertion sort for an array of double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the double array values.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(double values[], int length) {
    for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        double current = values[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && values[j] > current) {
            values[j + 1] = values[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        values[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double values[] = {71.8, 65.4, 60.7, 49.2, 76.7, 9.0, 94.3};
    int length = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    insertion_sort(values, length);
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", values[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 7 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to turn the rows of a 2x3 matrix into columns. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 2 and COLS as 3.
   2. Copy m[r][c] into t[c][r] for every element.
   3. Print t row by row. */
#define ROWS 2
#define COLS 3

int main(void) {
    int m[ROWS][COLS] = {{0, 7, 8}, {9, 6, 8}};
    int t[COLS][ROWS];
    /* Element (r, c) moves to (c, r). */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            t[c][r] = m[r][c];
        }
    }
    for (int r = 0; r < COLS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < ROWS; c++) {
            printf("%3d", t[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The nested loops copy m[r][c] into t[c][r], so the 2x3 matrix becomes 3x2.
   A second pair of loops prints the result. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I find a number in a sorted array with binary search in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set left to 0 and right to size - 1.
   3. While left <= right, compare the middle element middle with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 95. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int prices[], int size, int key) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = size - 1;
    while (left <= right) {
        int middle = left + (right - left) / 2;
        if (prices[middle] == key) {
            return middle;
        } else if (prices[middle] < key) {
            left = middle + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            right = middle - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int prices[] = {11, 59, 81, 95, 120, 141, 150};
    int size = 7;
    int index = binary_search(prices, size, 95);
    printf("Index of 95: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from left to
   right, compares the middle element middle with the key and throws away the half that
   cannot contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 95 and prints
   its index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to count the even values in a list of integers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes values and n.
   2. For each element, test values[i] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to matches for every even number.
   4. Return matches and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int values[], int n) {
    int matches = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (values[i] % 2 == 0) {
            matches++;
        }
    }
    return matches;
}

int main(void) {
    int values[] = {92, 42, 45, 54, 19, 3, 73};
    int n = 7;
    printf("Even numbers: %d\n", count_even(values, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_even() tests each element of values with the % operator: a remainder
   of 0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so matches goes up by one. main()
   prints how many of the 7 values are even. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the least common multiple of two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm: replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   2. Write lcm() as a / gcd(a, b) * b.
   3. Print the LCM of 108 and 21. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

/* lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b (divide first to avoid overflow). */
long lcm(int a, int b) {
    return (long)a / gcd(a, b) * b;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("lcm(108, 21) = %ld\n", lcm(108, 21));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. lcm() divides a by the gcd before multiplying by b, which avoids overflow.
   main() prints the LCM of 108 and 21. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I reverse an array by swapping from both ends in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for nums.
   2. Set start to the first index and end to the last.
   3. Swap nums[start] and nums[end], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when start meets end and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(long nums[], int len) {
    int start = 0;
    int end = len - 1;
    while (start < end) {
        long tmp = nums[start];
        nums[start] = nums[end];
        nums[end] = tmp;
        start++;
        end--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long nums[] = {29L, 50L, 15L, 7L};
    int len = sizeof(nums) / sizeof(nums[0]);
    reverse_array(nums, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", nums[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves start forward
   and end backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second
   array. main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to compute 5 to the power of 7 without pow(). */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 5 to the power 7. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("5^7 = %lld\n", power(5, 7));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 5 to the power 7. */
// END

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Divide n by 10 and add one to result.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 338353 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int count_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result++;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 338353;
    printf("count of digits of %d: %d\n", number, count_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_digits() removes the last digit (n / 10) and adds one to result each
   time, until n reaches 0. main() applies it to 338353. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to print the factorial of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(value) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by every number from 2 to value.
   3. Return result.
   4. Print 12! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int value) {
    unsigned long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= value; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int value = 12;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", value, factorial(value));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() multiplies result by every number from 2 up to value. main()
   prints 12! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to write a function with four parameters that returns the maximum. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write max2() that returns the larger of two values.
   2. Write max_of_four() as max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d)).
   3. Print the largest of the four values. */
/* Return the larger of two values. */
int max2(int a, int b) {
    return a > b ? a : b;
}

/* Reuse max2 to compare four values. */
int max_of_four(int a, int b, int c, int d) {
    return max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d));
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 7, b = 2, c = 27, d = 35;
    printf("Largest: %d\n", max_of_four(a, b, c, d));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: max_of_four() takes four parameters and reuses the helper max2(), which
   returns the larger of two values: it compares a with b, c with d, and then the two
   winners. main() prints the largest of 7, 2, 27 and 35. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the sum of the elements of an array. */

int sum_values(const int nums[], int size) {

/* Caption: How do I check every element of an array to find a target value in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and key.
   2. Compare each element with key.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 7 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of key, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int items[], int count, int key) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (items[i] == key) {
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int items[] = {52, 9, 85, 7, 19, 76, 39};
    const int count = 7;
    int key = 7;
    int pos = linear_search(items, count, key);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", key, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", key);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of items one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to key, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 7 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I allocate an array with malloc and fill it with cubes in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 8 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill buffer with cubes.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(buffer) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 8;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *buffer = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (buffer == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        buffer[i] = i * i * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", buffer[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(buffer);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 8 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills buffer with cubes, the second prints
   them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Multiply two integers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Set x and y.
   2. Store x * y in product.
   3. Print the calculation. */
int main(void) {
    int x = 36, y = 32;

/* Caption: How do I count the odd values in a list of integers in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_odd() that takes data and length.
   2. For each element, test data[k] % 2 != 0.
   3. Add one to found for every odd number.
   4. Return found and print it. */
/* A number is odd when the remainder after dividing by 2 is one. */
int count_odd(const int data[], int length) {
    int found = 0;
    for (int k = 0; k < length; k++) {
        if (data[k] % 2 != 0) {
            found++;
        }
    }
    return found;
}

int main(void) {
    int data[] = {81, 11, 20, 61, 26, 47, 45, 77};
    const int length = 8;
    printf("Odd numbers: %d\n", count_odd(data, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_odd() tests each element of data with the % operator: a remainder of
   1 after dividing by 2 means the number is odd, so found goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 8 values are odd. */
// END

/* Caption: Multiply two 2x2 matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define N as 2.
   2. For every i and j, add a[i][k] * b[k][j] over k into product[i][j].
   3. Print product row by row. */
#define N 2

int main(void) {
    int a[N][N] = {{9, 3}, {8, 3}};
    int b[N][N] = {{2, 6}, {4, 9}};
    int product[N][N] = {0};
    /* product[i][j] is row i of a times column j of b. */
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) {
                product[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            printf("%4d", product[i][j]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: For each entry product[i][j] the innermost loop adds a[i][k] * b[k][j] over
   k, which is row i of a times column j of b. main() multiplies two 2x2 matrices and
   prints the product. */
// END

/* Caption: Build a FIFO queue using a ring buffer. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 10 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 6 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 10

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 7);
    enqueue(&q, 67);
    enqueue(&q, 69);
    enqueue(&q, 54);
    enqueue(&q, 88);
    enqueue(&q, 24);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 10 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 6 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to convert 723 to binary. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 723 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 723;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 16);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 723
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: Show the Fibonacci series with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with prev = 0 and curr = 1.
   2. Repeat 19 times and print prev each time.
   3. Compute next = prev + curr, then set prev = curr and curr = next. */
int main(void) {
    long prev = 0, curr = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 19; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", prev);
        long next = prev + curr;
        prev = curr;
        curr = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in prev and curr. Each round it prints
   prev, then moves the pair forward: prev becomes curr and curr becomes their sum. It
   prints the first 19 Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write average() that takes numbers and len.
   2. Add the values into the double total.
   3. Return total / len.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double average(const double numbers[], int len) {
    double total = 0.0;
    int j = 0;
    while (j < len) {
        total += numbers[j];
        j++;
    }
    return total / len;
}

int main(void) {
    double numbers[] = {53.5, 90.4, 39.0};
    const int len = 3;
    printf("Average: %.2f\n", average(numbers, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: average() adds the 3 values of numbers into the double total and divides by
   len, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers. main()
   prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to compute the factorial of a number with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(num) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by every number from 2 to num.
   3. Return result.
   4. Print 11! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int num) {
    unsigned long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= num; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int num = 11;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", num, factorial(num));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() multiplies result by every number from 2 up to num. main()
   prints 11! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to use dynamic memory to store the first 10 multiples. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 10 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill table with multiples.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(table) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 10;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *table = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (table == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        table[i] = 8 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", table[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(table);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 10 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it
   fails, which the program checks. The first loop fills table with multiples, the second
   prints them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I return a circle's area and circumference through pointers in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write circle_measures() with the pointers area and circumference.
   2. Store PI * r * r and 2 * PI * r through them.
   3. Print both for a radius of 22.2. */
#define PI 3.14159265

void circle_measures(double radius, double *area, double *circumference) {
    *area = PI * radius * radius;
    *circumference = 2 * PI * radius;
}

int main(void) {
    double radius = 22.2;
    double area, circumference;
    circle_measures(radius, &area, &circumference);
    printf("Area: %.2f, Circumference: %.2f\n", area, circumference);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: circle_measures() computes two results from one radius and stores them
   through the pointers area and circumference. main() declares both variables on one line,
   passes their addresses and prints the results for a radius of 22.2. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to search an array for a value and print its position. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and target.
   2. Compare each element with target.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 99 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of target, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int numbers[], int length, int target) {
    for (int k = 0; k < length; k++) {
        if (numbers[k] == target) {
            return k;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {63, 45, 20, 69, 47, 99};
    int length = sizeof(numbers) / sizeof(numbers[0]);
    int target = 99;
    int pos = linear_search(numbers, length, target);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", target, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", target);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of numbers one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to target, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 99 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Check whether a number lies between two limits. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write in_range(x, low, high).
   2. Return true when x >= low and x <= high.
   3. Print whether 57 is inside 45 to 95. */
/* true when low <= x <= high */
bool in_range(int x, int low, int high) {
    return x >= low && x <= high;
}

int main(void) {
    int value = 57, low = 45, high = 95;
    printf("%d is %s the range %d to %d\n", value,
           in_range(value, low, high) ? "inside" : "outside", low, high);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: in_range() takes the value and both limits and returns true only when the
   value is at least low and at most high. main() declares value, low and high on one line
   and prints whether 57 is inside 45 to 95. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to build a fixed-size integer stack in C. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stack with room for 16 items and a top counter.
   2. Write push() and pop(), returning false when the stack is full or empty.
   3. Push 5 values.
   4. Pop and print until the stack is empty. */
#define CAPACITY 16

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int top;   /* number of items on the stack */
} Stack;

bool push(Stack *s, int value) {
    if (s->top == CAPACITY) {
        return false;   /* stack is full */
    }
    s->items[s->top++] = value;
    return true;
}

bool pop(Stack *s, int *value) {
    if (s->top == 0) {
        return false;   /* stack is empty */
    }
    *value = s->items[--s->top];
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Stack s = {.top = 0};
    push(&s, 56);
    push(&s, 15);
    push(&s, 9);
    push(&s, 53);
    push(&s, 39);
    int value;
    /* Items come back out in reverse order (last in, first out). */
    while (pop(&s, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Stack keeps up to 16 items in an array, and top counts how many are
   stored. push() adds at the top and pop() removes from the top; both return false when
   they cannot. main() pushes 5 values and pops them all, so they come out in reverse order
   (last in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Find the least common multiple of two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm: replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   2. Write lcm() as a / gcd(a, b) * b.
   3. Print the LCM of 101 and 25. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

/* lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b (divide first to avoid overflow). */
long lcm(int a, int b) {
    return (long)a / gcd(a, b) * b;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("lcm(101, 25) = %ld\n", lcm(101, 25));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. lcm() divides a by the gcd before multiplying by b, which avoids overflow.
   main() prints the LCM of 101 and 25. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the arithmetic mean of 7 int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes prices and n.
   2. Add the values into the double result.
   3. Return result / n.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double compute_mean(const int prices[], int n) {
    double result = 0.0;
    int idx = 0;
    while (idx < n) {
        result += prices[idx];
        idx++;
    }
    return result / n;
}

int main(void) {
    int prices[] = {52, 70, 11, 40, 26, 75, 65};
    int n = 7;
    printf("Mean = %.2f\n", compute_mean(prices, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 7 values of prices into the double result and
   divides by n, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to write a function that swaps two int values through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two int values.
   2. Save *a in tmp, copy *b into *a, then tmp into *b.
   3. In main(), print a and b, call swap(&a, &b) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(int *a, int *b) {
    int tmp = *a;
    *a = *b;
    *b = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 24, b = 34;
    printf("Before: %d %d\n", a, b);
    swap(&a, &b);
    printf("After:  %d %d\n", a, b);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of a and b, so writing through the pointers
   *a and *b changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Print the bigger of two int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Read x and y.
   2. Pick the bigger of x and y.
   3. Print it. */
int main(void) {
    int x, y;
    printf("Enter two numbers: ");
    if (scanf("%d %d", &x, &y) != 2) {
        printf("Invalid input\n");
        return 1;
    }
    int best = (x > y) ? x : y;   /* the ?: operator picks one of two values */
    printf("The bigger is %d\n", best);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The program reads x and y from the keyboard with scanf and stops with a
   message if the input is not valid. The conditional operator (x > y) ? x : y picks the
   bigger value, which is printed. */
// END

/* Caption: Create a singly linked list by inserting at the head. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 5 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 7);
    head = push_front(head, 27);
    head = push_front(head, 78);
    head = push_front(head, 20);
    head = push_front(head, 58);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 5
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to print all prime numbers up to 76. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Print every prime from 2 to 76. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int n = 2; n <= 76; n++) {
        if (is_prime(n)) {
            printf("%d ", n);
        }
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}

   evenly, n is not prime. main() tests every number from 2 to 76 and prints the primes. */

/* Caption: Use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 51 and 252. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 51, y = 252;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 51 and 252. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write average() that takes values and length.
   2. Add the values into the double sum.
   3. Return sum / length.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double average(const double values[], int length) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    int idx = 0;
    while (idx < length) {
        sum += values[idx];
        idx++;
    }
    return sum / length;
}

int main(void) {
    double values[] = {20.9, 83.5, 88.8, 69.0, 45.3, 40.8, 93.0};
    int length = 7;
    printf("Average: %.2f\n", average(values, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: average() adds the 7 values of values into the double sum and divides by
   length, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Reverse an array by swapping from both ends. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for items.
   2. Set start to the first index and end to the last.
   3. Swap items[start] and items[end], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when start meets end and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(long items[], int n) {
    int start = 0;
    int end = n - 1;
    while (start < end) {
        long tmp = items[start];
        items[start] = items[end];
        items[end] = tmp;
        start++;
        end--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long items[] = {43L, 52L, 31L, 5L, 15L, 96L};
    const int n = 6;
    reverse_array(items, n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", items[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves start forward
   and end backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second
   array. main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to find a number in a sorted array with binary search. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to len - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 201. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int readings[], int len, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = len - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (readings[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (readings[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int readings[] = {32, 47, 53, 83, 101, 119, 164};
    int len = sizeof(readings) / sizeof(readings[0]);
    int index = binary_search(readings, len, 201);
    printf("Index of 201: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from lo to hi,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 201 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Return the largest element of an array of int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write largest_value() that takes scores and len.
   2. Store scores[0] in largest.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in largest.
   4. Return largest and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
int largest_value(const int scores[], int len) {
    int largest = scores[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < len; i++) {
        if (scores[i] > largest) {
            largest = scores[i];
        }
    }
    return largest;
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {35, 64, 97, 28, 11, 61, 37};
    int len = sizeof(scores) / sizeof(scores[0]);
    printf("Largest: %d\n", largest_value(scores, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: largest_value() takes the first element as the largest value so far and
   stores it in largest. The loop compares every other element with largest using > and
   keeps the largest one. main() prints the largest of the 7 values. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I create a singly linked list by inserting at the head in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 5 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 98);
    head = push_front(head, 74);
    head = push_front(head, 90);
    head = push_front(head, 34);
    head = push_front(head, 14);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 5
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Sort an array in ascending order using bubble sort. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the int array values.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for ascending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(int values[], int size) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < size - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (values[j] > values[j + 1]) {
                int tmp = values[j];
                values[j] = values[j + 1];
                values[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int values[] = {46, 41, 14, 46, 64, 75, 29, 13};
    int size = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    bubble_sort(values, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%d ", values[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through values again and again and swaps neighbours
   that are in the wrong order, so the largest values move to the end first. main() then
   prints the 8 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Return both the smallest and the largest value of an array through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write min_max() with the array, its length and the pointers min and max.
   2. Start both at the first element.
   3. Update *min and *max while looping over the rest.
   4. Declare low and high, pass their addresses and print them. */
/* One pass finds both results; they are stored through the pointers. */
void min_max(const int samples[], int n, int *min, int *max) {
    *min = samples[0];
    *max = samples[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
        if (samples[i] < *min) {
            *min = samples[i];
        }
        if (samples[i] > *max) {
            *max = samples[i];
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {89, 97, 26, 74};
    int n = sizeof(samples) / sizeof(samples[0]);
    int low, high;
    min_max(samples, n, &low, &high);
    printf("Min: %d, Max: %d\n", low, high);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: A C function can return only one value, so min_max() returns void and
   writes its two results through the pointer parameters min and max. main() declares low
   and high on one line and passes their addresses with &, then prints both results for the
   4 values. */
// END

int string_length(const char *str) {

/* Caption: Calculate 12! using recursion. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(num) that calls itself.
   2. Return 1 when num is 1 or less.
   3. Otherwise return num * factorial(num - 1).
   4. Print 12! as an unsigned long long. */
/* n! = n * (n - 1)!, and 0! = 1 stops the recursion. */
unsigned long long factorial(int num) {
    if (num <= 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    return num * factorial(num - 1);
}

int main(void) {
    int num = 12;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", num, factorial(num));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() calls itself: n! is n * (n - 1)!, and the recursion stops when
   num is 1 or less. main() prints 12! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow
   very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes marks and n.
   2. Add the values into the double acc.
   3. Return acc / n.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* The mean is the total divided by the count. */
double compute_mean(const double marks[], int n) {
    double acc = 0.0;
    for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
        acc += marks[j];
    }
    return acc / n;
}

int main(void) {
    double marks[] = {15.9, 26.3, 79.7, 9.1, 69.5, 64.3, 14.9, 56.5, 58.6};
    const int n = 9;
    printf("The average is %.2f\n", compute_mean(marks, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 9 values of marks into the double acc and divides
   by n, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers. main()
   prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to reverse the digits of a number. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Multiply result by 10, add n % 10, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 793085 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int reverse_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result = result * 10 + n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 793085;
    printf("reverse of digits of %d: %d\n", number, reverse_digits(number));
    return 0;

/* Caption: Write a program to implement a simple linked list with malloc and free. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ListNode with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct ListNode {
    int value;
    struct ListNode *next;
} ListNode;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
ListNode *push_front(ListNode *head, int value) {
    ListNode *node = malloc(sizeof(ListNode));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const ListNode *head) {
    for (const ListNode *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(ListNode *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        ListNode *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    ListNode *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 70);
    head = push_front(head, 75);
    head = push_front(head, 72);
    head = push_front(head, 26);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each ListNode holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes ages and size.
   2. Add the values into the double result.
   3. Return result / size.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* The mean is the total divided by the count. */
double compute_mean(const int ages[], int size) {
    double result = 0.0;
    for (int j = 0; j < size; j++) {
        result += ages[j];
    }
    return result / size;
}

int main(void) {
    int ages[] = {85, 51, 25, 57, 52, 37};
    int size = sizeof(ages) / sizeof(ages[0]);
    printf("Average: %.2f\n", compute_mean(ages, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 6 values of ages into the double result and divides
   by size, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

int string_length(const char *word) {

   ends every C string. main() prints the length of the word stack. */

/* Caption: How do I compute the factorial of a number with a loop in C? */

   3. Return result.
   4. Print 10! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int value) {

/* Caption: Find the greatest common divisor of two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 105 and 158. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 105, y = 158;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 105 and 158. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I write a function with four parameters that returns the maximum in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write max2() that returns the larger of two values.
   2. Write max_of_four() as max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d)).
   3. Print the largest of the four values. */
/* Return the larger of two values. */
int max2(int a, int b) {
    return a > b ? a : b;
}

/* Reuse max2 to compare four values. */
int max_of_four(int a, int b, int c, int d) {
    return max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d));
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 55, b = 89, c = 90, d = 23;
    printf("Largest: %d\n", max_of_four(a, b, c, d));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: max_of_four() takes four parameters and reuses the helper max2(), which
   returns the larger of two values: it compares a with b, c with d, and then the two
   winners. main() prints the largest of 55, 89, 90 and 23. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to show the right way to declare several pointers on one line. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Declare x and y on one line.
   2. Declare the pointers px and py on one line, each with its own *.
   3. Add 8 to x through px and print the values. */
int main(void) {
    int x = 24, y = 34;
    /* Each pointer needs its own '*': in "int *p, q;" only p is a pointer. */
    int *px = &x, *py = &y;
    *px += 8;
    printf("x = %d, y = %d\n", x, y);
    printf("*px = %d, *py = %d\n", *px, *py);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: int *px = &x, *py = &y; declares two pointers in one statement; each name
   needs its own *. *px += 8 changes x through the pointer, so x becomes 32 while y stays
   34. */
// END

/* Caption: Add two matrices element by element. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 3 and COLS as 4.
   2. Loop over every row r and column c.
   3. Store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print it. */
#define ROWS 3
#define COLS 4

int main(void) {
    int a[ROWS][COLS] = {{1, 5, 8, 8}, {6, 0, 8, 9}, {4, 4, 3, 9}};
    int b[ROWS][COLS] = {{9, 6, 5, 8}, {0, 5, 1, 3}, {2, 9, 7, 2}};
    int sum[ROWS][COLS];
    /* Each entry of the result is the sum of the matching entries. */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            sum[r][c] = a[r][c] + b[r][c];
            printf("%3d", sum[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Both matrices are 3x4 two-dimensional arrays. Two nested loops visit every
   row r and column c, store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print each row. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to reverse the digits of a number. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Multiply result by 10, add n % 10, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 453080 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int reverse_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result = result * 10 + n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 453080;
    printf("reverse of digits of %d: %d\n", number, reverse_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_digits() shifts result one place left (result * 10) and adds the
   last digit of n, which reverses the order. main() applies it to 453080. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to implement selection sort for an array of double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the double array prices.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(double prices[], int count) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < count; j++) {
            if (prices[chosen] > prices[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        double tmp = prices[i];
        prices[i] = prices[chosen];
        prices[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double prices[] = {29.6, 59.9, 87.8, 97.4, 53.0, 51.1, 93.2, 50.8};
    int count = sizeof(prices) / sizeof(prices[0]);
    selection_sort(prices, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", prices[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 8 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Count the even values in a list of integers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes marks and size.
   2. For each element, test marks[k] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to matches for every even number.
   4. Return matches and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int marks[], int size) {
    int matches = 0;
    for (int k = 0; k < size; k++) {
        if (marks[k] % 2 == 0) {
            matches++;
        }
    }
    return matches;
}

int main(void) {
    int marks[] = {57, 14, 66, 81, 35, 67, 1, 20, 79, 25, 1, 18};
    int size = sizeof(marks) / sizeof(marks[0]);
    printf("Count of even values = %d\n", count_even(marks, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_even() tests each element of marks with the % operator: a remainder
   of 0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so matches goes up by one. main()
   prints how many of the 12 values are even. */
// END
