/* Caption: How do I add up all the numbers in an array of double values in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write array_sum() that takes the array numbers and its length length.
   2. Start acc at 0 and add every element in a while loop.
   3. Return acc.
   4. In main(), fill numbers with 6 values and print the sum. */
/* Add every element to a running total. */
double array_sum(const double numbers[], int length) {
    double acc = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < length) {
        acc += numbers[i];
        i++;
    }
    return acc;
}

int main(void) {
    double numbers[] = {1.4, 14.6, 36.4, 34.6, 14.8, 26.8};
    int length = sizeof(numbers) / sizeof(numbers[0]);
    printf("The sum is %.2f\n", array_sum(numbers, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: array_sum() receives the array numbers and its length length. It starts acc
   at 0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills
   numbers with 6 double values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a function that returns the quotient and remainder through pointers. */

/* Plan:
   1. Write divide(a, b, &quotient, &remainder) that returns a bool.
   2. Return false if b is 0.
   3. Store a / b and a % b through the pointers and return true.
   4. Divide 91 by 27 and print the results or the error. */
/* Returns false for division by zero; otherwise stores both results. */
bool divide(int a, int b, int *quotient, int *remainder) {
    if (b == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *quotient = a / b;
    *remainder = a % b;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 91, b = 27;
    int q, r;
    if (divide(a, b, &q, &r)) {
        printf("%d / %d = %d remainder %d\n", a, b, q, r);
    } else {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: divide() has four parameters: two inputs and two pointers for the results.
   Its bool return value reports success, while the quotient and remainder are written
   through the pointers. main() divides 91 by 27 and prints both results. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to compute 7 to the power of 8 without pow(). */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 7 to the power 8. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("7^8 = %lld\n", power(7, 8));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 7 to the power 8. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I implement insertion sort for an array of int values in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the int array prices.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the smaller values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(int prices[], int length) {
    for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        int current = prices[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && prices[j] < current) {
            prices[j + 1] = prices[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        prices[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int prices[] = {83, 79, 94, 26, 30, 17, 78, 99, 74, 55};
    const int length = 10;
    insertion_sort(prices, length);
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        printf("%d ", prices[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the smaller values
   of the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 10
   values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Implement a simple linked list with malloc and free. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Item with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Item {
    int value;
    struct Item *next;
} Item;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Item *push_front(Item *head, int value) {
    Item *node = malloc(sizeof(Item));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Item *head) {
    for (const Item *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Item *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Item *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Item *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 46);
    head = push_front(head, 14);
    head = push_front(head, 97);
    head = push_front(head, 58);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Item holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Convert seconds into a struct with hours, minutes and seconds. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Duration struct with hours, minutes and seconds.
   2. Write from_seconds() that fills it using / and %.
   3. Convert 27030 seconds and print the members. */
typedef struct {
    int hours;
    int minutes;
    int seconds;
} Duration;

Duration from_seconds(int total) {
    Duration d;
    d.hours = total / 3600;
    d.minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    d.seconds = total % 60;
    return d;
}

int main(void) {
    Duration d = from_seconds(27030);
    printf("%d h %d min %d s\n", d.hours, d.minutes, d.seconds);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: from_seconds() fills the three members of a Duration struct using / and %,
   then returns the struct. main() converts 27030 seconds and prints the members. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I find a number in a sorted array with binary search in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to length - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 201. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int data[], int length, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = length - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (data[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (data[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int data[] = {30, 38, 57, 79, 91, 136, 172};
    const int length = 7;
    int index = binary_search(data, length, 201);
    printf("Index of 201: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from lo to hi,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 201 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to raise a number to an integer power with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 8 to the power 4. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("8^4 = %lld\n", power(8, 4));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 8 to the power 4. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to print an integer with its digits reversed. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Multiply result by 10, add n % 10, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 329834 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int reverse_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result = result * 10 + n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 329834;
    printf("reverse of digits of %d: %d\n", number, reverse_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_digits() shifts result one place left (result * 10) and adds the
   last digit of n, which reverses the order. main() applies it to 329834. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to write your own version of strcpy. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:

   2. Copy src into dest one character at a time.
   3. Stop after copying the null character.
   4. Copy refer into line and print it. */
/* Copy each character, including the final '\0'. */
void copy_string(char *dest, const char *src) {
    int i = 0;

        i++;
    }
}

/* Caption: Write a program to implement selection sort for an array of long values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the long array items.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(long items[], int size) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < size; j++) {
            if (items[chosen] > items[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        long tmp = items[i];
        items[i] = items[chosen];
        items[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long items[] = {34L, 75L, 90L, 9L, 49L, 88L};
    int size = 6;
    selection_sort(items, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", items[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 6 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the arithmetic mean of 9 double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write array_average() that takes prices and n.
   2. Add the values into the double total.
   3. Return total / n.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double array_average(const double prices[], int n) {
    double total = 0.0;
    for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        total += prices[k];
    }
    return total / n;
}

int main(void) {
    double prices[] = {88.9, 89.3, 86.5, 64.5, 10.1, 24.0, 53.6, 20.3, 64.7};
    const int n = 9;
    printf("Mean = %.2f\n", array_average(prices, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: array_average() adds the 9 values of prices into the double total and
   divides by n, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to compute the sum and the average of an array in one function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_and_average() with the pointers sum and average.
   2. Add the values into *sum.
   3. Store *sum / n in *average.
   4. Declare total and mean, pass their addresses and print them. */
void sum_and_average(const double v[], int n, double *sum, double *average) {
    *sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        *sum += v[i];
    }
    *average = *sum / n;
}

int main(void) {
    double marks[] = {64.7, 92.6, 79.7, 50.9, 63.6, 59.8, 41.1};
    int n = sizeof(marks) / sizeof(marks[0]);
    double total, mean;
    sum_and_average(marks, n, &total, &mean);
    printf("Sum: %.2f, Average: %.2f\n", total, mean);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_and_average() takes the array, its length and two pointers. It adds up
   the 7 values through *sum and then stores *sum / n in *average. main() declares total
   and mean on one line and passes their addresses. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I show the Fibonacci series with a loop in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with first = 0 and second = 1.
   2. Repeat 8 times and print first each time.
   3. Compute next = first + second, then set first = second and second = next. */
int main(void) {
    long first = 0, second = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", first);
        long next = first + second;
        first = second;
        second = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in first and second. Each round it
   prints first, then moves the pair forward: first becomes second and second becomes their
   sum. It prints the first 8 Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to test if "bridge" reads the same backwards. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for word.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check bridge and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *word) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(word) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (word[i] != word[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *word = "bridge";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", word, is_palindrome(word) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word bridge and
   prints the result. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 180 and 171. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 180, y = 171;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 180 and 171. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to implement a simple linked list with malloc and free. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 5 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 45);
    head = push_front(head, 96);
    head = push_front(head, 57);
    head = push_front(head, 8);
    head = push_front(head, 73);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 5
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Use selection sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the double array marks.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(double marks[], int len) {
    for (int i = 0; i < len - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < len; j++) {
            if (marks[chosen] > marks[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        double tmp = marks[i];
        marks[i] = marks[chosen];
        marks[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double marks[] = {47.1, 50.4, 35.1, 2.3, 31.7, 44.7};
    const int len = 6;
    selection_sort(marks, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", marks[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 6 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I find a number in a sorted array with binary search in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to length - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 201. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int scores[], int length, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = length - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (scores[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (scores[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {25, 43, 65, 74, 88, 108, 151, 156, 169, 184, 194, 195};
    int length = 12;
    int index = binary_search(scores, length, 201);
    printf("Index of 201: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from lo to hi,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 201 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to divide two integers and get both the quotient and the remainder. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write divide(a, b, &quotient, &remainder) that returns a bool.
   2. Return false if b is 0.
   3. Store a / b and a % b through the pointers and return true.
   4. Divide 156 by 22 and print the results or the error. */
/* Returns false for division by zero; otherwise stores both results. */
bool divide(int a, int b, int *quotient, int *remainder) {
    if (b == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *quotient = a / b;
    *remainder = a % b;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 156, b = 22;
    int q, r;
    if (divide(a, b, &q, &r)) {
        printf("%d / %d = %d remainder %d\n", a, b, q, r);
    } else {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: divide() has four parameters: two inputs and two pointers for the results.
   Its bool return value reports success, while the quotient and remainder are written
   through the pointers. main() divides 156 by 22 and prints both results. */
// END

}

/* Caption: C program to multiply two fractions using a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Fraction struct with num and den.
   2. Write multiply() that returns num = a.num * b.num and den = a.den * b.den.
   3. Print 4/9 times 5/7. */
typedef struct {
    int num;
    int den;
} Fraction;

/* Multiply the numerators and the denominators. */
Fraction multiply(Fraction a, Fraction b) {
    Fraction r = {a.num * b.num, a.den * b.den};
    return r;
}

int main(void) {
    Fraction x = {4, 9}, y = {5, 7};
    Fraction p = multiply(x, y);
    printf("%d/%d * %d/%d = %d/%d\n", x.num, x.den, y.num, y.den, p.num, p.den);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Fraction stores a numerator and a denominator. multiply() takes two
   Fractions and returns a new one with num = a.num * b.num and den = a.den * b.den. main()
   multiplies 4/9 by 5/7 (without reducing the result). */
// END

/* Caption: C program to find the smallest number in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write find_min() that takes data and count.
   2. Store data[0] in smallest.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the smallest value in smallest.
   4. Return smallest and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the smallest value seen so far. */
int find_min(const int data[], int count) {
    int smallest = data[0];
    for (int idx = 1; idx < count; idx++) {
        if (data[idx] < smallest) {
            smallest = data[idx];
        }
    }
    return smallest;
}

int main(void) {
    int data[] = {52, 86, 21, 16, 32, 75};
    int count = sizeof(data) / sizeof(data[0]);
    printf("Smallest: %d\n", find_min(data, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: find_min() takes the first element as the smallest value so far and stores
   it in smallest. The loop compares every other element with smallest using < and keeps
   the smallest one. main() prints the smallest of the 6 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to count how many even numbers are in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes ages and n.
   2. For each element, test ages[i] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to count for every even number.
   4. Return count and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int ages[], int n) {
    int count = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < n) {
        if (ages[i] % 2 == 0) {
            count++;
        }
        i++;
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    int ages[] = {7, 99, 67, 85, 52, 44, 2, 79, 95, 33};
    const int n = 10;
    printf("Even numbers: %d\n", count_even(ages, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_even() tests each element of ages with the % operator: a remainder of
   0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so count goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 10 values are even. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to split a number of seconds into hours, minutes and seconds with pointer parameters. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write split_seconds() with the pointers hours, minutes and seconds.
   2. Store total / 3600, (total % 3600) / 60 and total % 60 through them.
   3. Convert 70781 seconds and print the parts. */
void split_seconds(int total, int *hours, int *minutes, int *seconds) {
    *hours = total / 3600;
    *minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    *seconds = total % 60;
}

int main(void) {
    int total = 70781;
    int h, m, s;
    split_seconds(total, &h, &m, &s);
    printf("%d seconds = %d h %d min %d s\n", total, h, m, s);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: split_seconds() fills three results through pointers: hours is total /
   3600, minutes is what is left divided by 60, and seconds is total % 60. main() declares
   h, m and s on one line and converts 70781 seconds. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to check every element of an array to find a target value. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and wanted.
   2. Compare each element with wanted.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 13 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of wanted, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int numbers[], int length, int wanted) {
    for (int j = 0; j < length; j++) {
        if (numbers[j] == wanted) {
            return j;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {95, 73, 8, 25, 13};
    int length = 5;
    int wanted = 13;
    int pos = linear_search(numbers, length, wanted);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", wanted, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", wanted);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of numbers one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to wanted, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 13 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Use bubble sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the double array samples.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for ascending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(double samples[], int length) {
    for (int i = 0; i < length - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < length - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (samples[j] > samples[j + 1]) {
                double tmp = samples[j];
                samples[j] = samples[j + 1];
                samples[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double samples[] = {18.3, 60.0, 27.2, 6.6, 93.2, 44.2, 9.0, 62.0, 28.3};
    int length = sizeof(samples) / sizeof(samples[0]);
    bubble_sort(samples, length);
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", samples[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through samples again and again and swaps neighbours
   that are in the wrong order, so the largest values move to the end first. main() then
   prints the 9 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I find the number of digits in an integer in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Divide n by 10 and add one to result.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 694735 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int count_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result++;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 694735;
    printf("count of digits of %d: %d\n", number, count_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_digits() removes the last digit (n / 10) and adds one to result each
   time, until n reaches 0. main() applies it to 694735. */
// END

   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.

/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(long data[], int len) {

int main(void) {

/* Caption: Use binary search to locate a value in a sorted list. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set left to 0 and right to n - 1.
   3. While left <= right, compare the middle element middle with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 177. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int samples[], int n, int key) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = n - 1;
    while (left <= right) {
        int middle = left + (right - left) / 2;
        if (samples[middle] == key) {
            return middle;
        } else if (samples[middle] < key) {
            left = middle + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            right = middle - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {52, 53, 56, 95, 111, 129, 162, 177, 191, 194, 197};
    int n = sizeof(samples) / sizeof(samples[0]);
    int index = binary_search(samples, n, 177);
    printf("Index of 177: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from left to
   right, compares the middle element middle with the key and throws away the half that
   cannot contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 177 and prints
   its index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to divide two integers and get both the quotient and the remainder. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write divide(a, b, &quotient, &remainder) that returns a bool.
   2. Return false if b is 0.
   3. Store a / b and a % b through the pointers and return true.
   4. Divide 29 by 29 and print the results or the error. */
/* Returns false for division by zero; otherwise stores both results. */
bool divide(int a, int b, int *quotient, int *remainder) {
    if (b == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *quotient = a / b;
    *remainder = a % b;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 29, b = 29;
    int q, r;
    if (divide(a, b, &q, &r)) {
        printf("%d / %d = %d remainder %d\n", a, b, q, r);
    } else {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: divide() has four parameters: two inputs and two pointers for the results.
   Its bool return value reports success, while the quotient and remainder are written
   through the pointers. main() divides 29 by 29 and prints both results. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes numbers and length.
   2. Add the values into the double total.
   3. Return total / length.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* The mean is the total divided by the count. */
double compute_mean(const int numbers[], int length) {
    double total = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        total += numbers[i];
    }
    return total / length;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {98, 84, 6, 32, 69};
    int length = sizeof(numbers) / sizeof(numbers[0]);
    printf("Average: %.2f\n", compute_mean(numbers, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 5 values of numbers into the double total and
   divides by length, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole
   numbers. main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Reverse an array by swapping from both ends. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for marks.
   2. Set start to the first index and end to the last.
   3. Swap marks[start] and marks[end], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when start meets end and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(long marks[], int count) {
    int start = 0;
    int end = count - 1;
    while (start < end) {
        long tmp = marks[start];
        marks[start] = marks[end];
        marks[end] = tmp;
        start++;
        end--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long marks[] = {29L, 2L, 12L, 30L, 41L};
    int count = sizeof(marks) / sizeof(marks[0]);
    reverse_array(marks, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", marks[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves start forward
   and end backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second
   array. main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* Caption: Return the minimum, maximum and average of an array in a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stats struct with min, max and average.
   2. Write array_stats() that fills one Stats in a loop.
   3. Return the struct.
   4. Print st.min, st.max and st.average. */
typedef struct {
    int min;
    int max;
    double average;
} Stats;

/* Pack several results into one struct and return it. */
Stats array_stats(const int v[], int n) {
    Stats s = {v[0], v[0], 0.0};
    double total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (v[i] < s.min) {
            s.min = v[i];
        }
        if (v[i] > s.max) {
            s.max = v[i];
        }
        total += v[i];
    }
    s.average = total / n;
    return s;
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {4, 8, 69, 44, 16, 40, 6, 67, 75};
    int n = sizeof(samples) / sizeof(samples[0]);
    Stats st = array_stats(samples, n);
    printf("Min %d, Max %d, Average %.2f\n", st.min, st.max, st.average);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Stats groups three results. array_stats() fills one Stats while it loops
   over the 9 values and returns the whole struct, which is a clean way to return several
   results at once. main() reads them as st.min, st.max and st.average. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I find the greatest common divisor of two numbers in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 99 and 240. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 99, y = 240;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 99 and 240. */
// END

/* Caption: Sum a double array with a helper function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_array() that takes the array marks and its length count.
   2. Start sum at 0 and add every element in a while loop.
   3. Return sum.
   4. In main(), fill marks with 9 values and print the sum. */
/* Add every element to a running total. */
double sum_array(const double marks[], int count) {
    double sum = 0;
    int k = 0;
    while (k < count) {
        sum += marks[k];
        k++;
    }
    return sum;
}

int main(void) {
    double marks[] = {42.4, 61.0, 49.7, 30.5, 45.1, 83.9, 95.9, 95.1, 38.6};
    int count = sizeof(marks) / sizeof(marks[0]);
    printf("Total = %.2f\n", sum_array(marks, count));
    return 0;
}

   0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills marks
   with 9 double values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: Transpose a matrix. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 2 and COLS as 3.
   2. Copy m[r][c] into t[c][r] for every element.
   3. Print t row by row. */
#define ROWS 2
#define COLS 3

int main(void) {
    int m[ROWS][COLS] = {{8, 0, 3}, {8, 8, 7}};
    int t[COLS][ROWS];
    /* Element (r, c) moves to (c, r). */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            t[c][r] = m[r][c];
        }
    }
    for (int r = 0; r < COLS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < ROWS; c++) {
            printf("%3d", t[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The nested loops copy m[r][c] into t[c][r], so the 2x3 matrix becomes 3x2.
   A second pair of loops prints the result. */
// END

/* Caption: Convert temperatures from Celsius to Fahrenheit. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write to_fahrenheit() with F = C * 9 / 5 + 32.
   2. Loop c from -20 to 100 in steps of 10.
   3. Print each Celsius value with its Fahrenheit value. */
/* F = C * 9 / 5 + 32 */
double to_fahrenheit(double celsius) {
    return celsius * 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0;

    for (int c = -20; c <= 100; c += 10) {
        printf("%7d  %10.1f\n", c, to_fahrenheit(c));
    }
    return 0;
}

   to 100 degrees Celsius in steps of 10. */
// END

   by 2: 0 means even, anything else means odd, and the if-else prints which one it is. */

/* Caption: Write a program to find a number in a sorted array with binary search. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to count - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 201. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int numbers[], int count, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = count - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (numbers[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (numbers[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {1, 13, 52, 147, 166, 199};
    const int count = 6;
    int index = binary_search(numbers, count, 201);
    printf("Index of 201: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from lo to hi,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 201 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Swap two variables using pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two double values.
   2. Save *a in tmp, copy *b into *a, then tmp into *b.
   3. In main(), print a and b, call swap(&a, &b) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(double *a, double *b) {
    double tmp = *a;
    *a = *b;
    *b = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    double a = 39.1, b = 57.1;
    printf("Before: %.2f %.2f\n", a, b);
    swap(&a, &b);
    printf("After:  %.2f %.2f\n", a, b);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of a and b, so writing through the pointers
   *a and *b changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

    const int size = 9;

   stores it in current. The loop compares every other element with current using > and
   keeps the largest one. main() prints the largest of the 9 values. */

/* Caption: How do I compute the sum and the average of an array in one function in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_and_average() with the pointers sum and average.
   2. Add the values into *sum.
   3. Store *sum / n in *average.
   4. Declare total and mean, pass their addresses and print them. */
void sum_and_average(const double v[], int n, double *sum, double *average) {
    *sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        *sum += v[i];
    }
    *average = *sum / n;
}

int main(void) {
    double values[] = {4.1, 96.1, 73.6, 90.9, 49.7, 41.2, 27.3, 48.2};
    int n = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    double total, mean;
    sum_and_average(values, n, &total, &mean);
    printf("Sum: %.2f, Average: %.2f\n", total, mean);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_and_average() takes the array, its length and two pointers. It adds up
   the 8 values through *sum and then stores *sum / n in *average. main() declares total
   and mean on one line and passes their addresses. */
// END

/* Caption: Test if 96 is a prime number. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Check 96 and print the result. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 96;
    printf("%d %s prime\n", number, is_prime(number) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() checks 96 and prints whether it is prime. */
// END

/* Caption: Allocate an array with malloc and fill it with evens. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 12 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill table with evens.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(table) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 12;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *table = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (table == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        table[i] = 2 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", table[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(table);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 12 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it
   fails, which the program checks. The first loop fills table with evens, the second
   prints them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

    int seconds;

Duration from_seconds(int total) {

/* Caption: Implement a stack with an array (push and pop). */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stack with room for 16 items and a top counter.
   2. Write push() and pop(), returning false when the stack is full or empty.
   3. Push 4 values.
   4. Pop and print until the stack is empty. */
#define CAPACITY 16

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int top;   /* number of items on the stack */
} Stack;

bool push(Stack *s, int value) {
    if (s->top == CAPACITY) {
        return false;   /* stack is full */
    }
    s->items[s->top++] = value;
    return true;
}

bool pop(Stack *s, int *value) {
    if (s->top == 0) {
        return false;   /* stack is empty */
    }
    *value = s->items[--s->top];
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Stack s = {.top = 0};
    push(&s, 70);
    push(&s, 6);
    push(&s, 19);
    push(&s, 40);
    int value;
    /* Items come back out in reverse order (last in, first out). */
    while (pop(&s, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Stack keeps up to 16 items in an array, and top counts how many are
   stored. push() adds at the top and pop() removes from the top; both return false when
   they cannot. main() pushes 4 values and pops them all, so they come out in reverse order
   (last in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Program to implement a simple linked list with malloc and free. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Item with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 3 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Item {
    int value;
    struct Item *next;
} Item;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Item *push_front(Item *head, int value) {
    Item *node = malloc(sizeof(Item));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Item *head) {
    for (const Item *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Item *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Item *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Item *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 70);
    head = push_front(head, 10);
    head = push_front(head, 99);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Item holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 3
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to test if "pointer" reads the same backwards. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for text.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check pointer and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *text) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(text) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (text[i] != text[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *text = "pointer";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", text, is_palindrome(text) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word pointer and
   prints the result. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to find the smallest number in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write find_min() that takes nums and count.
   2. Store nums[0] in current.

   4. Return current and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the smallest value seen so far. */
double find_min(const double nums[], int count) {

    int count = 7;

   it in current. The loop compares every other element with current using < and keeps the
   smallest one. main() prints the smallest of the 7 values. */
// END

    const int n = 9;
    int wanted = 46;

    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", wanted, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", wanted);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of numbers one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to wanted, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 46 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the sum of the elements of an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write add_all() that takes the array scores and its length len.
   2. Start result at 0 and add every element in a while loop.
   3. Return result.
   4. In main(), fill scores with 7 values and print the sum. */
/* Add every element to a running total. */
double add_all(const double scores[], int len) {
    double result = 0;
    int idx = 0;
    while (idx < len) {
        result += scores[idx];
        idx++;
    }
    return result;

    int len = sizeof(scores) / sizeof(scores[0]);

    return 0;

   0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills scores
   with 7 double values and prints their sum. */

/* Caption: Program to find a number in a sorted array with binary search. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set left to 0 and right to size - 1.
   3. While left <= right, compare the middle element middle with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 201. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int numbers[], int size, int key) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = size - 1;
    while (left <= right) {
        int middle = left + (right - left) / 2;
        if (numbers[middle] == key) {
            return middle;
        } else if (numbers[middle] < key) {
            left = middle + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            right = middle - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {5, 30, 91, 97, 101, 115, 119, 137};
    int size = 8;
    int index = binary_search(numbers, size, 201);
    printf("Index of 201: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from left to
   right, compares the middle element middle with the key and throws away the half that
   cannot contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 201 and prints
   its index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Add up the digits of a number. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Add n % 10 to result, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 855037 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int sum_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result += n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 855037;
    printf("sum of digits of %d: %d\n", number, sum_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_digits() adds the last digit (n % 10) to result and then removes it (n
   / 10) until no digits are left. main() applies it to 855037. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write average() that takes items and len.
   2. Add the values into the double total.
   3. Return total / len.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* The mean is the total divided by the count. */
double average(const long items[], int len) {
    double total = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        total += items[i];
    }
    return total / len;
}

int main(void) {
    long items[] = {40L, 2L, 56L, 63L};
    const int len = 4;
    printf("The average is %.2f\n", average(items, len));
    return 0;

   len, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers. main()
   prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Create a singly linked list by inserting at the head. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 3 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 48);
    head = push_front(head, 90);
    head = push_front(head, 97);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 3
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Divide two numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Set num1 and num2.
   2. If num2 is 0, print an error and stop.
   3. Print num1 / num2 and the remainder num1 % num2. */
int main(void) {
    int num1 = 19, num2 = 55;
    /* Dividing by zero is not allowed, so check first. */
    if (num2 == 0) {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
        return 1;
    }
    /* Integer division drops the fraction; % gives the remainder. */
    printf("Quotient: %d, remainder: %d\n", num1 / num2, num1 % num2);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The program uses fixed values for num1 and num2. It checks that num2 is not
   zero, then prints num1 / num2, where integer division drops the fraction, and the
   remainder num1 % num2. */

/* Caption: Print all prime numbers up to 72. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Print every prime from 2 to 72. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int n = 2; n <= 72; n++) {
        if (is_prime(n)) {
            printf("%d ", n);
        }
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() tests every number from 2 to 72 and prints the primes. */
// END

/* Caption: Return the smallest element of an array of int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write min_of() that takes scores and length.
   2. Store scores[0] in current.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the smallest value in current.
   4. Return current and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the smallest value seen so far. */
int min_of(const int scores[], int length) {
    int current = scores[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
        if (scores[i] < current) {
            current = scores[i];
        }
    }
    return current;
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {88, 16, 97, 24, 65, 31, 25, 40};
    const int length = 8;
    printf("The smallest value is %d\n", min_of(scores, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: min_of() takes the first element as the smallest value so far and stores it
   in current. The loop compares every other element with current using < and keeps the
   smallest one. main() prints the smallest of the 8 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to reverse the characters of a word. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_string() for str.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap the two characters and move i and j inwards until they meet.
   4. Reverse memory and print it. */
/* Swap characters from both ends until they meet in the middle. */
void reverse_string(char *str) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(str) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        char tmp = str[i];
        str[i] = str[j];
        str[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char str[] = "memory";
    reverse_string(str);
    printf("%s\n", str);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_string() swaps characters from both ends of str, moving inwards
   until the two indexes meet. main() reverses the word memory in place and prints it. */
// END

   2. Store total / 3600, (total % 3600) / 60 and total % 60 through them.

void split_seconds(int total, int *hours, int *minutes, int *seconds) {
    *hours = total / 3600;
    *minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    *seconds = total % 60;
}

    printf("%d seconds = %d h %d min %d s\n", total, h, m, s);
    return 0;
}

   3600, minutes is what is left divided by 60, and seconds is total % 60. main() declares
   h, m and s on one line and converts 16049 seconds. */
// END

/* Caption: Allocate an array with malloc and fill it with multiples. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 11 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill arr with multiples.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(arr) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 11;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *arr = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (arr == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        arr[i] = 4 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", arr[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(arr);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 11 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it
   fails, which the program checks. The first loop fills arr with multiples, the second
   prints them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 237 and 154. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 237, y = 154;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 237 and 154. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I search an array for a value and print its position in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and needle.
   2. Compare each element with needle.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 106 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of needle, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int readings[], int length, int needle) {
    for (int k = 0; k < length; k++) {
        if (readings[k] == needle) {
            return k;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int readings[] = {59, 62, 76, 78, 82, 47, 30, 40, 44, 21};
    int length = 10;
    int needle = 106;
    int pos = linear_search(readings, length, needle);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", needle, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", needle);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of readings one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to needle, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 106 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a function that clamps a value between a minimum and a maximum. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write clamp(value, low, high).
   2. Return low if the value is too small and high if it is too big.
   3. Otherwise return the value.
   4. Set low = 17 and high = 47 and print clamp() for -10, 1 and 116. */
/* Return value, but never less than low or more than high. */
int clamp(int value, int low, int high) {
    if (value < low) {
        return low;
    }
    if (value > high) {
        return high;
    }
    return value;
}

int main(void) {
    int low = 17, high = 47;
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", -10, clamp(-10, low, high));
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 1, clamp(1, low, high));
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 116, clamp(116, low, high));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: clamp() takes three parameters: the value and the two limits. It returns
   low when the value is too small, high when it is too big and the value itself otherwise.
   main() declares low = 17 and high = 47 on one line and clamps -10, 1 and 116. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to calculate 3! using recursion. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(num) that calls itself.
   2. Return 1 when num is 1 or less.
   3. Otherwise return num * factorial(num - 1).
   4. Print 3! as an unsigned long long. */
/* n! = n * (n - 1)!, and 0! = 1 stops the recursion. */
unsigned long long factorial(int num) {
    if (num <= 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    return num * factorial(num - 1);
}

int main(void) {
    int num = 3;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", num, factorial(num));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() calls itself: n! is n * (n - 1)!, and the recursion stops when
   num is 1 or less. main() prints 3! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow
   very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to use binary search to locate a value in a sorted list. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set left to 0 and right to len - 1.
   3. While left <= right, compare the middle element middle with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 201. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int nums[], int len, int key) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = len - 1;
    while (left <= right) {
        int middle = left + (right - left) / 2;
        if (nums[middle] == key) {
            return middle;
        } else if (nums[middle] < key) {
            left = middle + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            right = middle - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int nums[] = {41, 42, 53, 57, 95, 100, 123, 140, 168, 173};
    int len = sizeof(nums) / sizeof(nums[0]);
    int index = binary_search(nums, len, 201);
    printf("Index of 201: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from left to
   right, compares the middle element middle with the key and throws away the half that
   cannot contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 201 and prints
   its index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to find a number in a sorted array with binary search. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set left to 0 and right to count - 1.
   3. While left <= right, compare the middle element middle with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 135. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int prices[], int count, int key) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = count - 1;
    while (left <= right) {
        int middle = left + (right - left) / 2;
        if (prices[middle] == key) {
            return middle;
        } else if (prices[middle] < key) {
            left = middle + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            right = middle - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int prices[] = {2, 6, 27, 53, 60, 61, 63, 73, 93, 107, 135, 198};
    int count = 12;
    int index = binary_search(prices, count, 135);
    printf("Index of 135: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from left to
   right, compares the middle element middle with the key and throws away the half that
   cannot contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 135 and prints
   its index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Print an integer with its digits reversed. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Multiply result by 10, add n % 10, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 914755 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int reverse_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result = result * 10 + n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 914755;
    printf("reverse of digits of %d: %d\n", number, reverse_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_digits() shifts result one place left (result * 10) and adds the
   last digit of n, which reverses the order. main() applies it to 914755. */
// END

/* Caption: Define a Point struct and measure the distance between two points. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Point struct with x and y.
   2. Write distance() using sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy).
   3. Print the distance between p and q. */
typedef struct {
    double x;
    double y;
} Point;

/* Pythagoras: sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). */
double distance(Point a, Point b) {
    double dx = b.x - a.x;
    double dy = b.y - a.y;
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

int main(void) {
    Point p = {-10, -9};
    Point q = {-7, 4};
    printf("Distance: %.3f\n", distance(p, q));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Point is a typedef struct with x and y. distance() uses Pythagoras, sqrt(dx
   * dx + dy * dy), to measure the gap between the two points, and main() prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to convert seconds into hours, minutes and seconds. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write split_seconds() with the pointers hours, minutes and seconds.
   2. Store total / 3600, (total % 3600) / 60 and total % 60 through them.
   3. Convert 75927 seconds and print the parts. */
void split_seconds(int total, int *hours, int *minutes, int *seconds) {
    *hours = total / 3600;
    *minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    *seconds = total % 60;
}

int main(void) {
    int total = 75927;
    int h, m, s;
    split_seconds(total, &h, &m, &s);
    printf("%d seconds = %d h %d min %d s\n", total, h, m, s);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: split_seconds() fills three results through pointers: hours is total /
   3600, minutes is what is left divided by 60, and seconds is total % 60. main() declares
   h, m and s on one line and converts 75927 seconds. */
// END

    };

/* Caption: Reverse the characters of a word. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_string() for str.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap the two characters and move i and j inwards until they meet.
   4. Reverse network and print it. */
/* Swap characters from both ends until they meet in the middle. */
void reverse_string(char *str) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(str) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        char tmp = str[i];
        str[i] = str[j];
        str[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char str[] = "network";
    reverse_string(str);
    printf("%s\n", str);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_string() swaps characters from both ends of str, moving inwards
   until the two indexes meet. main() reverses the word network in place and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Decide if 2052 is a leap year. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_leap(year).
   2. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year, unless it is divisible by 100.
   3. Years divisible by 400 are leap years again.
   4. Check 2052 and print the result. */
/* Leap years divide by 4, except centuries, which must divide by 400. */
int is_leap(int year) {
    return (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || year % 400 == 0;
}

int main(void) {
    int year = 2052;
    if (is_leap(year)) {
        printf("%d is a leap year\n", year);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not a leap year\n", year);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_leap() returns true for years divisible by 4, except century years,
   which must also be divisible by 400. main() checks 2052 and prints whether it is a leap
   year. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to add up the digits of a number. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Add n % 10 to result, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 800221 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int sum_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result += n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 800221;
    printf("sum of digits of %d: %d\n", number, sum_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_digits() adds the last digit (n % 10) to result and then removes it (n
   / 10) until no digits are left. main() applies it to 800221. */
// END

/* Caption: Raise a number to an integer power with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 6 to the power 10. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("6^10 = %lld\n", power(6, 10));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 6 to the power 10. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to compute the LCM of two integers using the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm: replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   2. Write lcm() as a / gcd(a, b) * b.
   3. Print the LCM of 185 and 229. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

/* lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b (divide first to avoid overflow). */
long lcm(int a, int b) {
    return (long)a / gcd(a, b) * b;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("lcm(185, 229) = %ld\n", lcm(185, 229));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. lcm() divides a by the gcd before multiplying by b, which avoids overflow.
   main() prints the LCM of 185 and 229. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to reverse an array by swapping from both ends. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for ages.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap ages[i] and ages[j], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when i meets j and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(long ages[], int count) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = count - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        long tmp = ages[i];
        ages[i] = ages[j];
        ages[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long ages[] = {74L, 65L, 16L, 44L, 84L, 4L};
    const int count = 6;
    reverse_array(ages, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", ages[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves i forward and
   j backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second array.
   main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to use dynamic memory to store the first 12 multiples. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 12 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill arr with multiples.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(arr) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 12;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *arr = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (arr == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        arr[i] = 7 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", arr[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(arr);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 12 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it
   fails, which the program checks. The first loop fills arr with multiples, the second
   prints them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to build a linked list, print it, and free it. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Item with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 3 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Item {
    int value;
    struct Item *next;
} Item;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Item *push_front(Item *head, int value) {
    Item *node = malloc(sizeof(Item));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Item *head) {
    for (const Item *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Item *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Item *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Item *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 21);
    head = push_front(head, 74);
    head = push_front(head, 35);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Item holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 3
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to save text to a file with fprintf and print it with fgets. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open data.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 2 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("data.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "c gives you direct control over memory\n");
    fprintf(file, "every program starts in main\n");
    fclose(file);

    /* Reopen the file for reading and print it line by line. */
    file = fopen("data.txt", "r");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fopen() in write mode creates data.txt, fprintf() writes 2 lines into it
   and fclose() saves it. The file is then opened again in read mode, and fgets() reads it
   back line by line into the buffer line, which is printed. Every fopen() result is
   checked for NULL. */
// END

int string_length(const char *word) {

   ends every C string. main() prints the length of the word bridge. */

/* Caption: Write a function that clamps a value between a minimum and a maximum. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write clamp(value, low, high).
   2. Return low if the value is too small and high if it is too big.
   3. Otherwise return the value.
   4. Set low = 20 and high = 33 and print clamp() for 70, 117 and 76. */
/* Return value, but never less than low or more than high. */
int clamp(int value, int low, int high) {
    if (value < low) {
        return low;
    }
    if (value > high) {
        return high;
    }
    return value;
}

int main(void) {
    int low = 20, high = 33;
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 70, clamp(70, low, high));
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 117, clamp(117, low, high));
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 76, clamp(76, low, high));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: clamp() takes three parameters: the value and the two limits. It returns
   low when the value is too small, high when it is too big and the value itself otherwise.
   main() declares low = 20 and high = 33 on one line and clamps 70, 117 and 76. */
// END

void copy_string(char *dest, const char *src) {

}

    copy_string(buffer, source);
    printf("Copied: %s\n", buffer);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: copy_string() copies src into dest one character at a time, including the
   final null character, which is what strcpy does. The array buffer must be big enough to
   hold the copy. main() copies the word refer and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to search an array for its largest value. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write find_max() that takes items and length.
   2. Store items[0] in m.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in m.
   4. Return m and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
long find_max(const long items[], int length) {
    long m = items[0];
    for (int j = 1; j < length; j++) {
        if (items[j] > m) {
            m = items[j];
        }
    }
    return m;
}

int main(void) {
    long items[] = {94L, 47L, 66L, 42L, 89L, 39L, 3L};
    const int length = 7;
    printf("Largest: %ld\n", find_max(items, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: find_max() takes the first element as the largest value so far and stores
   it in m. The loop compares every other element with m using > and keeps the largest one.
   main() prints the largest of the 7 values. */
// END

/* Walk through the array and accumulate each value. */

   adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills values with
   7 double values and prints their sum. */

/* Caption: Define a Point struct and measure the distance between two points. */

#include <math.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Point struct with x and y.
   2. Write distance() using sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy).
   3. Print the distance between p and q. */
typedef struct {
    double x;
    double y;
} Point;

/* Pythagoras: sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). */
double distance(Point a, Point b) {
    double dx = b.x - a.x;
    double dy = b.y - a.y;
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

    Point p = {10, -1};
    Point q = {-5, -9};
    printf("Distance: %.3f\n", distance(p, q));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Point is a typedef struct with x and y. distance() uses Pythagoras, sqrt(dx
   * dx + dy * dy), to measure the gap between the two points, and main() prints it. */
