/* Caption: How do I compute the product of two square matrices in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define N as 2.
   2. For every i and j, add a[i][k] * b[k][j] over k into product[i][j].
   3. Print product row by row. */
#define N 2

int main(void) {
    int a[N][N] = {{4, 7}, {6, 1}};
    int b[N][N] = {{2, 3}, {5, 5}};
    int product[N][N] = {0};
    /* product[i][j] is row i of a times column j of b. */
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) {
                product[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            printf("%4d", product[i][j]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: For each entry product[i][j] the innermost loop adds a[i][k] * b[k][j] over
   k, which is row i of a times column j of b. main() multiplies two 2x2 matrices and
   prints the product. */
// END

/* Caption: Copy one string into another by hand. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write copy_string(dest, src).
   2. Copy src into dest one character at a time.
   3. Stop after copying the null character.
   4. Copy compiler into buffer and print it. */
/* Copy each character, including the final '\0'. */
void copy_string(char *dest, const char *src) {
    int i = 0;
    while ((dest[i] = src[i]) != '\0') {
        i++;
    }
}

    char buffer[64];
    copy_string(buffer, source);
    printf("Copied: %s\n", buffer);
    return 0;
}

   final null character, which is what strcpy does. The array buffer must be big enough to
   hold the copy. main() copies the word compiler and prints it. */
// END

   3. Add one to matches for every odd number.

/* A number is odd when the remainder after dividing by 2 is one. */
int count_odd(const int values[], int len) {
    int matches = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < len) {
        if (values[i] % 2 != 0) {
            matches++;
        }
        i++;
    }
    return matches;
}

    int len = 5;
    printf("Count of odd values = %d\n", count_odd(values, len));
    return 0;
}

   of 1 after dividing by 2 means the number is odd, so matches goes up by one. main()
   prints how many of the 5 values are odd. */
// END

/* Caption: Swap two variables using pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two int values.
   2. Save *first in tmp, copy *second into *first, then tmp into *second.
   3. In main(), print first and second, call swap(&first, &second) and print them
      again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(int *first, int *second) {
    int tmp = *first;
    *first = *second;
    *second = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    int first = 52, second = 52;
    printf("Before: %d %d\n", first, second);
    swap(&first, &second);
    printf("After:  %d %d\n", first, second);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of first and second, so writing through the
   pointers *first and *second changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during
   the exchange. main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and
   after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to sort an array in ascending order using bubble sort. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the long array nums.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for ascending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(long nums[], int length) {
    for (int i = 0; i < length - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < length - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (nums[j] > nums[j + 1]) {
                long tmp = nums[j];
                nums[j] = nums[j + 1];
                nums[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long nums[] = {6L, 18L, 29L, 75L, 44L};
    int length = 5;
    bubble_sort(nums, length);
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", nums[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through nums again and again and swaps neighbours that
   are in the wrong order, so the largest values move to the end first. main() then prints
   the 5 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 78 and 240. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 78, y = 240;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 78 and 240. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to calculate the average of the values in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes values and n.
   2. Add the values into the double result.
   3. Return result / n.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double compute_mean(const int values[], int n) {
    double result = 0.0;
    for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
        result += values[j];
    }
    return result / n;
}

int main(void) {
    int values[] = {87, 6, 85, 16, 81, 44, 25, 43};
    int n = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    printf("Average: %.2f\n", compute_mean(values, n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 8 values of values into the double result and
   divides by n, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to implement a simple linked list with malloc and free. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Item with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 3 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Item {
    int value;
    struct Item *next;
} Item;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Item *push_front(Item *head, int value) {
    Item *node = malloc(sizeof(Item));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Item *head) {
    for (const Item *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Item *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Item *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Item *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 8);
    head = push_front(head, 37);
    head = push_front(head, 44);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Item holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 3
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Multiply two 3x3 matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define N as 3.
   2. For every i and j, add a[i][k] * b[k][j] over k into product[i][j].
   3. Print product row by row. */
#define N 3

int main(void) {
    int a[N][N] = {{2, 7, 2}, {9, 8, 2}, {0, 2, 9}};
    int b[N][N] = {{0, 6, 2}, {3, 4, 0}, {4, 9, 8}};
    int product[N][N] = {0};
    /* product[i][j] is row i of a times column j of b. */
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) {
                product[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            printf("%4d", product[i][j]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: For each entry product[i][j] the innermost loop adds a[i][k] * b[k][j] over
   k, which is row i of a times column j of b. main() multiplies two 3x3 matrices and
   prints the product. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I print the factorial of an integer in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(n) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by every number from 2 to n.
   3. Return result.
   4. Print 4! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int n) {
    unsigned long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int n = 4;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", n, factorial(n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() multiplies result by every number from 2 up to n. main() prints
   4! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I count how many words are separated by spaces in a string in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <ctype.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_words() with words = 0 and an in_word flag.
   2. A space ends a word; a non-space after a space starts a new word and adds one to
      words.
   3. Return words and print it. */
/* A new word starts when a non-space follows a space (or the start). */
int count_words(const char *text) {
    int words = 0;
    int in_word = 0;
    for (int i = 0; text[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (isspace((unsigned char)text[i])) {
            in_word = 0;
        } else if (!in_word) {
            in_word = 1;
            words++;
        }
    }
    return words;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *sentence = "strings end with a null character";
    printf("Words: %d\n", count_words(sentence));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_words() uses the flag in_word: a new word starts when a non-space
   character follows a space or the start of the text. main() prints the number of words in
   the sentence. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to use binary search to locate a value in a sorted list. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set left to 0 and right to length - 1.
   3. While left <= right, compare the middle element middle with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 3. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int marks[], int length, int key) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = length - 1;
    while (left <= right) {
        int middle = left + (right - left) / 2;
        if (marks[middle] == key) {
            return middle;
        } else if (marks[middle] < key) {
            left = middle + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            right = middle - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int marks[] = {2, 3, 21, 48, 88, 137, 143, 151, 174, 187, 193};
    int length = sizeof(marks) / sizeof(marks[0]);
    int index = binary_search(marks, length, 3);
    printf("Index of 3: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from left to
   right, compares the middle element middle with the key and throws away the half that
   cannot contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 3 and prints
   its index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to compute the sum and the average of an array in one function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_and_average() with the pointers sum and average.
   2. Add the values into *sum.
   3. Store *sum / n in *average.
   4. Declare total and mean, pass their addresses and print them. */
void sum_and_average(const double v[], int n, double *sum, double *average) {
    *sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        *sum += v[i];
    }
    *average = *sum / n;
}

int main(void) {
    double ages[] = {76.4, 77.7, 91.8};
    int n = sizeof(ages) / sizeof(ages[0]);
    double total, mean;
    sum_and_average(ages, n, &total, &mean);
    printf("Sum: %.2f, Average: %.2f\n", total, mean);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_and_average() takes the array, its length and two pointers. It adds up
   the 3 values through *sum and then stores *sum / n in *average. main() declares total
   and mean on one line and passes their addresses. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I use selection sort to put numbers in ascending order in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the int array numbers.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(int numbers[], int len) {
    for (int i = 0; i < len - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < len; j++) {
            if (numbers[chosen] > numbers[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        int tmp = numbers[i];
        numbers[i] = numbers[chosen];
        numbers[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {85, 31, 34, 1, 54, 76, 33, 95};
    const int len = 8;
    selection_sort(numbers, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%d ", numbers[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 8 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to find the largest of four numbers with a function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write max2() that returns the larger of two values.
   2. Write max_of_four() as max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d)).
   3. Print the largest of the four values. */
/* Return the larger of two values. */
int max2(int a, int b) {
    return a > b ? a : b;
}

/* Reuse max2 to compare four values. */
int max_of_four(int a, int b, int c, int d) {
    return max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d));
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 59, b = 78, c = 49, d = 5;
    printf("Largest: %d\n", max_of_four(a, b, c, d));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: max_of_four() takes four parameters and reuses the helper max2(), which
   returns the larger of two values: it compares a with b, c with d, and then the two
   winners. main() prints the largest of 59, 78, 49 and 5. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to create a singly linked list by inserting at the head. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 5 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 2);
    head = push_front(head, 14);
    head = push_front(head, 93);
    head = push_front(head, 35);
    head = push_front(head, 40);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 5
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);

        ListNode *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;

}

    head = push_front(head, 64);
    head = push_front(head, 12);
    head = push_front(head, 6);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each ListNode holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()

   2. Return false if b is 0.
   3. Store a / b and a % b through the pointers and return true.
   4. Divide 343 by 0 and print the results or the error. */
/* Returns false for division by zero; otherwise stores both results. */
bool divide(int a, int b, int *quotient, int *remainder) {
    if (b == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *quotient = a / b;
    *remainder = a % b;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {

    int q, r;
    if (divide(a, b, &q, &r)) {
        printf("%d / %d = %d remainder %d\n", a, b, q, r);
    } else {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: divide() has four parameters: two inputs and two pointers for the results.
   Its bool return value reports success, while the quotient and remainder are written
   through the pointers. main() divides 343 by 0, which fails because the divisor is zero. */
// END

/* Caption: Use binary search to locate a value in a sorted list. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to len - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 27. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int values[], int len, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = len - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (values[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (values[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int values[] = {16, 27, 33, 44, 137, 142, 156, 163, 166, 168, 176};
    const int len = 11;
    int index = binary_search(values, len, 27);
    printf("Index of 27: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from lo to hi,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 27 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to implement a circular queue with an array. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 10 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 6 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 10

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 45);
    enqueue(&q, 91);
    enqueue(&q, 6);
    enqueue(&q, 60);
    enqueue(&q, 6);
    enqueue(&q, 33);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 10 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 6 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Count the occurrences of a character in a sentence. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_char() with count = 0.
   2. Compare each character with the target m.
   3. Return count and print it. */
int count_char(const char *text, char target) {
    int count = 0;
    /* Compare every character with the target. */
    for (int i = 0; text[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (text[i] == target) {
            count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *sentence = "learning c teaches how computers work";
    printf("'m' appears %d times\n", count_char(sentence, 'm'));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_char() compares every character of the text with the target character
   and counts the matches. main() prints how many times m appears in the sentence. */
// END

/* Caption: Search an array for its largest value. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write largest_value() that takes items and count.
   2. Store items[0] in best.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in best.
   4. Return best and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
int largest_value(const int items[], int count) {
    int best = items[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {
        if (items[i] > best) {
            best = items[i];
        }
    }
    return best;
}

int main(void) {
    int items[] = {85, 85, 42, 95};
    int count = 4;
    printf("The largest value is %d\n", largest_value(items, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: largest_value() takes the first element as the largest value so far and
   stores it in best. The loop compares every other element with best using > and keeps the
   largest one. main() prints the largest of the 4 values. */
// END

        best = num1;

/* Caption: Build a linked list, print it, and free it. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 32);
    head = push_front(head, 56);
    head = push_front(head, 26);
    head = push_front(head, 2);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to implement selection sort for an array of double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the double array items.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(double items[], int size) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < size; j++) {
            if (items[chosen] > items[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        double tmp = items[i];
        items[i] = items[chosen];
        items[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double items[] = {65.2, 2.7, 72.3, 87.7, 98.3, 91.2, 96.5, 57.9};
    int size = sizeof(items) / sizeof(items[0]);
    selection_sort(items, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", items[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 8 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to print the binary representation of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 781 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 781;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 12);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 781
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I search an array for a value and print its position in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and wanted.
   2. Compare each element with wanted.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 41 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of wanted, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int marks[], int count, int wanted) {
    for (int j = 0; j < count; j++) {
        if (marks[j] == wanted) {
            return j;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int marks[] = {7, 29, 41, 54, 88, 88};
    int count = sizeof(marks) / sizeof(marks[0]);
    int wanted = 41;
    int pos = linear_search(marks, count, wanted);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", wanted, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", wanted);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of marks one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to wanted, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 41 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Allocate an array with malloc and fill it with evens. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 9 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill list with evens.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(list) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 9;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *list = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (list == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        list[i] = 2 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", list[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(list);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 9 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills list with evens, the second prints them,
   and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Implement a circular queue with an array. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 8 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 6 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 8

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 40);
    enqueue(&q, 24);
    enqueue(&q, 92);
    enqueue(&q, 31);
    enqueue(&q, 10);
    enqueue(&q, 36);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 8 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 6 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Copy one string into another by hand. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write copy_string(dest, src).
   2. Copy src into dest one character at a time.
   3. Stop after copying the null character.
   4. Copy stats into buffer and print it. */
/* Copy each character, including the final '\0'. */
void copy_string(char *dest, const char *src) {
    int i = 0;
    while ((dest[i] = src[i]) != '\0') {
        i++;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char source[] = "stats";
    char buffer[100];
    copy_string(buffer, source);
    printf("Copied: %s\n", buffer);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: copy_string() copies src into dest one character at a time, including the
   final null character, which is what strcpy does. The array buffer must be big enough to
   hold the copy. main() copies the word stats and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Write lines to a text file and read them back. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open notes.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 2 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("notes.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "structs group related data together\n");
    fprintf(file, "loops repeat a block of code\n");
    fclose(file);

    /* Reopen the file for reading and print it line by line. */
    file = fopen("notes.txt", "r");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fopen() in write mode creates notes.txt, fprintf() writes 2 lines into it
   and fclose() saves it. The file is then opened again in read mode, and fgets() reads it
   back line by line into the buffer line, which is printed. Every fopen() result is
   checked for NULL. */
// END

/* Caption: Use insertion sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the int array numbers.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(int numbers[], int size) {
    for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
        int current = numbers[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && numbers[j] > current) {
            numbers[j + 1] = numbers[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        numbers[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {62, 78, 71, 39, 83, 44, 92, 35};
    const int size = 8;
    insertion_sort(numbers, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%d ", numbers[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 8 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to count how many vowels a string contains. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_vowels() with count = 0.
   2. For each character, check whether strchr finds it in aeiouAEIOU.
   3. Return count and print it. */
/* strchr finds the letter in the list of vowels, or returns NULL. */
int count_vowels(const char *text) {
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; text[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (strchr("aeiouAEIOU", text[i]) != NULL) {
            count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *sentence = "learning c teaches how computers work";
    printf("Vowels: %d\n", count_vowels(sentence));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_vowels() uses strchr to test whether each character is one of
   aeiouAEIOU and counts the matches. main() prints the number of vowels in the sentence. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to sum a int array with a helper function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write add_all() that takes the array scores and its length count.
   2. Start total at 0 and add every element in a for loop.
   3. Return total.
   4. In main(), fill scores with 4 values and print the sum. */
/* Add every element to a running total. */
int add_all(const int scores[], int count) {
    int total = 0;
    for (int j = 0; j < count; j++) {
        total += scores[j];
    }
    return total;
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {38, 18, 27, 22};
    int count = sizeof(scores) / sizeof(scores[0]);
    printf("Total = %d\n", add_all(scores, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: add_all() receives the array scores and its length count. It starts total
   at 0, adds every element to it in a for loop and returns the total. main() fills scores
   with 4 int values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to use a struct to store a rectangle and print its area and perimeter. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Rectangle struct with width and height.
   2. Write area() and perimeter().
   3. Make a 14 by 18 rectangle and print both results. */
typedef struct {
    int width;
    int height;
} Rectangle;

int area(Rectangle r) {
    return r.width * r.height;
}

int perimeter(Rectangle r) {
    return 2 * (r.width + r.height);
}

int main(void) {
    Rectangle box = {14, 18};
    printf("Area: %d, Perimeter: %d\n", area(box), perimeter(box));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Rectangle stores a width and a height. area() returns width * height and
   perimeter() returns 2 * (width + height). main() makes a 14 by 18 rectangle and prints
   both results. */
// END

/* Caption: Show the right way to declare several pointers on one line. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Declare x and y on one line.
   2. Declare the pointers px and py on one line, each with its own *.
   3. Add 18 to x through px and print the values. */
int main(void) {
    int x = 36, y = 1;
    /* Each pointer needs its own '*': in "int *p, q;" only p is a pointer. */
    int *px = &x, *py = &y;
    *px += 18;
    printf("x = %d, y = %d\n", x, y);
    printf("*px = %d, *py = %d\n", *px, *py);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: int *px = &x, *py = &y; declares two pointers in one statement; each name
   needs its own *. *px += 18 changes x through the pointer, so x becomes 54 while y stays
   1. */
// END

/* Caption: List the prime numbers below a limit. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Print every prime from 2 to 108. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int n = 2; n <= 108; n++) {
        if (is_prime(n)) {
            printf("%d ", n);
        }
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() tests every number from 2 to 108 and prints the primes. */
// END

/* Caption: Use selection sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the int array values.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(int values[], int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (values[chosen] > values[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        int tmp = values[i];
        values[i] = values[chosen];
        values[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int values[] = {8, 62, 73, 88, 14, 70};
    int n = 6;
    selection_sort(values, n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", values[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 6 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I split a number of seconds into hours, minutes and seconds with pointer parameters in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write split_seconds() with the pointers hours, minutes and seconds.
   2. Store total / 3600, (total % 3600) / 60 and total % 60 through them.
   3. Convert 26529 seconds and print the parts. */
void split_seconds(int total, int *hours, int *minutes, int *seconds) {
    *hours = total / 3600;
    *minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    *seconds = total % 60;
}

int main(void) {
    int total = 26529;
    int h, m, s;
    split_seconds(total, &h, &m, &s);
    printf("%d seconds = %d h %d min %d s\n", total, h, m, s);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: split_seconds() fills three results through pointers: hours is total /
   3600, minutes is what is left divided by 60, and seconds is total % 60. main() declares
   h, m and s on one line and converts 26529 seconds. */
// END

   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and target.

   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 195 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of target, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int prices[], int size, int target) {
    for (int k = 0; k < size; k++) {
        if (prices[k] == target) {
            return k;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int prices[] = {72, 3, 7, 12, 39, 14, 32, 64, 14};
    int size = 9;
    int target = 195;
    int pos = linear_search(prices, size, target);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", target, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", target);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of prices one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to target, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 195 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Declare x and y on one line.
   2. Declare the pointers px and py on one line, each with its own *.
   3. Add 15 to x through px and print the values. */
int main(void) {
    int x = 44, y = 34;
    /* Each pointer needs its own '*': in "int *p, q;" only p is a pointer. */
    int *px = &x, *py = &y;
    *px += 15;
    printf("x = %d, y = %d\n", x, y);
    printf("*px = %d, *py = %d\n", *px, *py);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: int *px = &x, *py = &y; declares two pointers in one statement; each name
   needs its own *. *px += 15 changes x through the pointer, so x becomes 59 while y stays
   34. */
// END

/* Caption: Check whether a year is a leap year. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_leap(year).
   2. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year, unless it is divisible by 100.
   3. Years divisible by 400 are leap years again.
   4. Check 2048 and print the result. */
/* Leap years divide by 4, except centuries, which must divide by 400. */
int is_leap(int year) {
    return (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || year % 400 == 0;
}

int main(void) {
    int year = 2048;
    if (is_leap(year)) {
        printf("%d is a leap year\n", year);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not a leap year\n", year);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_leap() returns true for years divisible by 4, except century years,
   which must also be divisible by 400. main() checks 2048 and prints whether it is a leap
   year. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to allocate an array with malloc and fill it with evens. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 14 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill arr with evens.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(arr) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 14;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *arr = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (arr == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        arr[i] = 2 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", arr[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(arr);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 14 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it
   fails, which the program checks. The first loop fills arr with evens, the second prints
   them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Create a singly linked list by inserting at the head. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ListNode with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct ListNode {
    int value;
    struct ListNode *next;
} ListNode;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
ListNode *push_front(ListNode *head, int value) {
    ListNode *node = malloc(sizeof(ListNode));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const ListNode *head) {
    for (const ListNode *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(ListNode *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        ListNode *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    ListNode *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 6);
    head = push_front(head, 61);
    head = push_front(head, 3);
    head = push_front(head, 55);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each ListNode holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I count how many vowels a string contains in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_vowels() with count = 0.
   2. For each character, check whether strchr finds it in aeiouAEIOU.
   3. Return count and print it. */
/* strchr finds the letter in the list of vowels, or returns NULL. */
int count_vowels(const char *text) {
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; text[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (strchr("aeiouAEIOU", text[i]) != NULL) {
            count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *sentence = "always free the memory you allocate";
    printf("Vowels: %d\n", count_vowels(sentence));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_vowels() uses strchr to test whether each character is one of
   aeiouAEIOU and counts the matches. main() prints the number of vowels in the sentence. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to find the arithmetic mean of 3 double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes numbers and count.
   2. Add the values into the double sum.
   3. Return sum / count.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double compute_mean(const double numbers[], int count) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    int k = 0;
    while (k < count) {
        sum += numbers[k];
        k++;
    }
    return sum / count;
}

int main(void) {
    double numbers[] = {87.1, 48.8, 52.4};
    int count = 3;
    printf("The average is %.2f\n", compute_mean(numbers, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 3 values of numbers into the double sum and divides
   by count, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Swap two variables using pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two int values.
   2. Save *a in tmp, copy *b into *a, then tmp into *b.
   3. In main(), print a and b, call swap(&a, &b) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(int *a, int *b) {
    int tmp = *a;
    *a = *b;
    *b = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 64, b = 59;
    printf("Before: %d %d\n", a, b);
    swap(&a, &b);
    printf("After:  %d %d\n", a, b);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of a and b, so writing through the pointers
   *a and *b changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Transpose a matrix. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 4 and COLS as 3.
   2. Copy m[r][c] into t[c][r] for every element.
   3. Print t row by row. */
#define ROWS 4
#define COLS 3

int main(void) {
    int m[ROWS][COLS] = {{2, 9, 1}, {3, 1, 1}, {6, 6, 1}, {6, 1, 9}};
    int t[COLS][ROWS];
    /* Element (r, c) moves to (c, r). */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            t[c][r] = m[r][c];
        }
    }
    for (int r = 0; r < COLS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < ROWS; c++) {
            printf("%3d", t[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The nested loops copy m[r][c] into t[c][r], so the 4x3 matrix becomes 3x4.
   A second pair of loops prints the result. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the index of a number using linear search. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and target.
   2. Compare each element with target.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 61 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of target, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int scores[], int n, int target) {
    for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
        if (scores[j] == target) {
            return j;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {11, 69, 24, 61, 6, 93, 47, 60, 86, 74};
    int n = 10;
    int target = 61;
    int pos = linear_search(scores, n, target);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", target, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", target);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of scores one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to target, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 61 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a function with four parameters that returns the maximum. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write max2() that returns the larger of two values.
   2. Write max_of_four() as max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d)).
   3. Print the largest of the four values. */
/* Return the larger of two values. */
int max2(int a, int b) {
    return a > b ? a : b;
}

/* Reuse max2 to compare four values. */
int max_of_four(int a, int b, int c, int d) {
    return max2(max2(a, b), max2(c, d));
}

int main(void) {
    int a = 76, b = 81, c = 92, d = 54;
    printf("Largest: %d\n", max_of_four(a, b, c, d));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: max_of_four() takes four parameters and reuses the helper max2(), which
   returns the larger of two values: it compares a with b, c with d, and then the two
   winners. main() prints the largest of 76, 81, 92 and 54. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to print the factorial of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(num) that calls itself.
   2. Return 1 when num is 1 or less.
   3. Otherwise return num * factorial(num - 1).
   4. Print 5! as an unsigned long long. */
/* n! = n * (n - 1)!, and 0! = 1 stops the recursion. */
unsigned long long factorial(int num) {
    if (num <= 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    return num * factorial(num - 1);
}

int main(void) {
    int num = 5;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", num, factorial(num));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() calls itself: n! is n * (n - 1)!, and the recursion stops when
   num is 1 or less. main() prints 5! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow
   very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I sum a int array with a helper function in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write add_all() that takes the array readings and its length count.
   2. Start total at 0 and add every element in a for loop.
   3. Return total.
   4. In main(), fill readings with 5 values and print the sum. */
/* Add every element to a running total. */
int add_all(const int readings[], int count) {
    int total = 0;
    for (int k = 0; k < count; k++) {
        total += readings[k];
    }
    return total;
}

int main(void) {
    int readings[] = {96, 70, 43, 78, 59};
    const int count = 5;
    printf("Sum: %d\n", add_all(readings, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: add_all() receives the array readings and its length count. It starts total
   at 0, adds every element to it in a for loop and returns the total. main() fills
   readings with 5 int values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 290 and 39. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 290, y = 39;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 290 and 39. */
// END

/* Caption: Print the factorial of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(x) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by every number from 2 to x.
   3. Return result.
   4. Print 11! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int x) {
    unsigned long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= x; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 11;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", x, factorial(x));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() multiplies result by every number from 2 up to x. main() prints
   11! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to print the first 22 Fibonacci numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write fib(n) that returns n when n < 2.
   2. Otherwise return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2).
   3. Print fib(i) for i from 0 to 21. */
/* Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two before it. */
long fib(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return n;
    }
    return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2);
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 22; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", fib(i));
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fib() returns n for 0 and 1 and otherwise adds the two previous Fibonacci
   numbers by calling itself twice, which is simple but slow for large n. main() prints the
   first 22 numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to use selection sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the int array values.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(int values[], int size) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < size; j++) {
            if (values[chosen] > values[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        int tmp = values[i];
        values[i] = values[chosen];
        values[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int values[] = {50, 20, 12, 79, 18, 10, 29};
    int size = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    selection_sort(values, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%d ", values[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 7 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I find the index of a number using linear search in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and wanted.
   2. Compare each element with wanted.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 23 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of wanted, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int nums[], int length, int wanted) {
    for (int idx = 0; idx < length; idx++) {
        if (nums[idx] == wanted) {
            return idx;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int nums[] = {23, 52, 95, 56, 99, 87, 81, 27, 84, 84};
    int length = sizeof(nums) / sizeof(nums[0]);
    int wanted = 23;
    int pos = linear_search(nums, length, wanted);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", wanted, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", wanted);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of nums one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to wanted, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 23 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to find the number of digits in an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Divide n by 10 and add one to result.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 767407 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int count_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result++;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 767407;
    printf("count of digits of %d: %d\n", number, count_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_digits() removes the last digit (n / 10) and adds one to result each
   time, until n reaches 0. main() applies it to 767407. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to return two values from a function using pointer parameters. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write min_max() with the array, its length and the pointers min and max.
   2. Start both at the first element.
   3. Update *min and *max while looping over the rest.
   4. Declare lowest and highest, pass their addresses and print them. */
/* One pass finds both results; they are stored through the pointers. */
void min_max(const int scores[], int count, int *min, int *max) {
    *min = scores[0];
    *max = scores[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {
        if (scores[i] < *min) {
            *min = scores[i];
        }
        if (scores[i] > *max) {
            *max = scores[i];
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {8, 62, 54, 15, 55, 13, 86, 3};
    int count = 8;
    int lowest, highest;
    min_max(scores, count, &lowest, &highest);
    printf("Min: %d, Max: %d\n", lowest, highest);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: A C function can return only one value, so min_max() returns void and
   writes its two results through the pointer parameters min and max. main() declares
   lowest and highest on one line and passes their addresses with &, then prints both
   results for the 8 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Use binary search to locate a value in a sorted list. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to count - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 38. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int items[], int count, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = count - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (items[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (items[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int items[] = {14, 30, 38, 145, 170, 191};
    int count = 6;
    int index = binary_search(items, count, 38);
    printf("Index of 38: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from lo to hi,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 38 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Show the Fibonacci series with a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with prev = 0 and curr = 1.
   2. Repeat 23 times and print prev each time.
   3. Compute next = prev + curr, then set prev = curr and curr = next. */
int main(void) {
    long prev = 0, curr = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 23; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", prev);
        long next = prev + curr;
        prev = curr;
        curr = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in prev and curr. Each round it prints
   prev, then moves the pair forward: prev becomes curr and curr becomes their sum. It
   prints the first 23 Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to compute 8 to the power of 8 without pow(). */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 8 to the power 8. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("8^8 = %lld\n", power(8, 8));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 8 to the power 8. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I sort an array in ascending order using insertion sort in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the int array scores.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(int scores[], int len) {
    for (int i = 1; i < len; i++) {
        int current = scores[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && scores[j] > current) {
            scores[j + 1] = scores[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        scores[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {89, 98, 56, 93, 43, 40, 69, 67, 99};
    const int len = 9;
    insertion_sort(scores, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%d ", scores[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 9 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Implement a circular queue with an array. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 8 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 5 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 8

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 85);
    enqueue(&q, 59);
    enqueue(&q, 57);
    enqueue(&q, 74);
    enqueue(&q, 84);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 8 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 5 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to compute the sum and the average of an array in one function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_and_average() with the pointers sum and average.
   2. Add the values into *sum.
   3. Store *sum / n in *average.
   4. Declare total and mean, pass their addresses and print them. */
void sum_and_average(const double v[], int n, double *sum, double *average) {
    *sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        *sum += v[i];
    }
    *average = *sum / n;
}

int main(void) {
    double values[] = {26.8, 21.7, 72.7, 25.4, 96.2, 71.7};
    int n = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    double total, mean;
    sum_and_average(values, n, &total, &mean);
    printf("Sum: %.2f, Average: %.2f\n", total, mean);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_and_average() takes the array, its length and two pointers. It adds up
   the 6 values through *sum and then stores *sum / n in *average. main() declares total
   and mean on one line and passes their addresses. */
// END

    return 0;

   perimeter() returns 2 * (width + height). main() makes a 5 by 22 rectangle and prints
   both results. */

    for (int idx = 0; idx < n; idx++) {

            return idx;

    return -1;
}

    const int n = 7;
    int key = 29;

    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", key, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", key);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of values one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to key, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 29 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to list the prime numbers below a limit. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Print every prime from 2 to 84. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int n = 2; n <= 84; n++) {
        if (is_prime(n)) {
            printf("%d ", n);
        }
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() tests every number from 2 to 84 and prints the primes. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to use selection sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the int array scores.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(int scores[], int size) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < size; j++) {
            if (scores[chosen] > scores[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        int tmp = scores[i];
        scores[i] = scores[chosen];
        scores[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {72, 51, 92, 16, 88, 58, 29};
    const int size = 7;
    selection_sort(scores, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%d ", scores[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 7 values in ascending order. */
// END

   how many of the 8 values are odd. */

/* Caption: Calculate the average of the values in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write compute_mean() that takes samples and size.
   2. Add the values into the double result.
   3. Return result / size.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double compute_mean(const double samples[], int size) {
    double result = 0.0;
    for (int k = 0; k < size; k++) {
        result += samples[k];
    }
    return result / size;
}

int main(void) {
    double samples[] = {59.3, 30.8, 9.0, 75.6, 71.1, 23.9};
    int size = 6;
    printf("The average is %.2f\n", compute_mean(samples, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: compute_mean() adds the 6 values of samples into the double result and
   divides by size, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole
   numbers. main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to copy one string into another by hand. */

/* Plan:

   2. Copy src into dest one character at a time.
   3. Stop after copying the null character.
   4. Copy garden into line and print it. */
/* Copy each character, including the final '\0'. */
void copy_string(char *dest, const char *src) {
    int i = 0;
    while ((dest[i] = src[i]) != '\0') {
        i++;
    }
}

    char line[64];
    copy_string(line, source);
    printf("Copied: %s\n", line);
    return 0;

   hold the copy. main() copies the word garden and prints it. */

/* Caption: Write a C program to reverse a string in place. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_string() for word.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap the two characters and move i and j inwards until they meet.
   4. Reverse program and print it. */
/* Swap characters from both ends until they meet in the middle. */
void reverse_string(char *word) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(word) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        char tmp = word[i];
        word[i] = word[j];
        word[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char word[] = "program";
    reverse_string(word);
    printf("%s\n", word);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_string() swaps characters from both ends of word, moving inwards
   until the two indexes meet. main() reverses the word program in place and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to compute the product of two square matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define N as 2.
   2. For every i and j, add a[i][k] * b[k][j] over k into product[i][j].
   3. Print product row by row. */
#define N 2

int main(void) {
    int a[N][N] = {{3, 8}, {8, 0}};
    int b[N][N] = {{2, 5}, {4, 3}};
    int product[N][N] = {0};
    /* product[i][j] is row i of a times column j of b. */
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) {
                product[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            printf("%4d", product[i][j]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: For each entry product[i][j] the innermost loop adds a[i][k] * b[k][j] over
   k, which is row i of a times column j of b. main() multiplies two 2x2 matrices and
   prints the product. */
// END

   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 7 to the power 6. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {

    return result;
}

    return 0;

/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 7 to the power 6. */

/* Caption: Write a function that returns the distance between two points given x1, y1, x2 and y2. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write distance(x1, y1, x2, y2).
   2. Compute dx and dy, then return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy).
   3. Print the distance between (-6, 1) and (-8, -8). */
/* Pythagoras: the distance is sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). */
double distance(double x1, double y1, double x2, double y2) {
    double dx = x2 - x1, dy = y2 - y1;
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

int main(void) {
    printf("Distance: %.3f\n", distance(-6, 1, -8, -8));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: distance() takes the coordinates of both points as four parameters. It
   declares dx and dy on one line and uses Pythagoras with sqrt() from math.h. main()
   prints the distance between (-6, 1) and (-8, -8). */
// END

int string_length(const char *buffer) {

/* Return the sum of the first n elements. */
long sum_array(const long ages[], int len) {
    long result = 0;

    int len = 9;

   0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills ages

/* Caption: Add two matrices element by element. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 3 and COLS as 3.
   2. Loop over every row r and column c.
   3. Store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print it. */
#define ROWS 3
#define COLS 3

int main(void) {
    int a[ROWS][COLS] = {{6, 6, 2}, {3, 4, 1}, {5, 7, 9}};
    int b[ROWS][COLS] = {{9, 1, 2}, {4, 8, 6}, {4, 8, 1}};
    int sum[ROWS][COLS];
    /* Each entry of the result is the sum of the matching entries. */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            sum[r][c] = a[r][c] + b[r][c];
            printf("%3d", sum[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Both matrices are 3x3 two-dimensional arrays. Two nested loops visit every
   row r and column c, store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print each row. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a function that clamps a value between a minimum and a maximum. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write clamp(value, low, high).
   2. Return low if the value is too small and high if it is too big.
   3. Otherwise return the value.
   4. Set low = 65 and high = 96 and print clamp() for 56, 88 and 28. */
/* Return value, but never less than low or more than high. */
int clamp(int value, int low, int high) {
    if (value < low) {
        return low;
    }
    if (value > high) {
        return high;
    }
    return value;
}

int main(void) {
    int low = 65, high = 96;
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 56, clamp(56, low, high));
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 88, clamp(88, low, high));
    printf("clamp(%d) = %d\n", 28, clamp(28, low, high));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: clamp() takes three parameters: the value and the two limits. It returns
   low when the value is too small, high when it is too big and the value itself otherwise.
   main() declares low = 65 and high = 96 on one line and clamps 56, 88 and 28. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to check whether a word is a palindrome. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for buffer.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check integer and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *buffer) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(buffer) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (buffer[i] != buffer[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *buffer = "integer";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", buffer, is_palindrome(buffer) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word integer and
   prints the result. */
// END

#include <string.h>

/* Plan:

}

    printf("Vowels: %d\n", count_vowels(sentence));

}

   aeiouAEIOU and counts the matches. main() prints the number of vowels in the sentence. */
