/* Caption: Write a C program to use binary search to locate a value in a sorted list. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set low to 0 and high to len - 1.
   3. While low <= high, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 9. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int prices[], int len, int key) {
    int low = 0;
    int high = len - 1;
    while (low <= high) {
        int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (prices[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (prices[mid] < key) {
            low = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            high = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int prices[] = {9, 21, 31, 74, 97, 150, 175, 188};
    int len = sizeof(prices) / sizeof(prices[0]);
    int index = binary_search(prices, len, 9);
    printf("Index of 9: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from low to high,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 9 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Test if 462 is a prime number. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Check 462 and print the result. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 462;
    printf("%d %s prime\n", number, is_prime(number) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() checks 462 and prints whether it is prime. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to implement selection sort for an array of double values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the double array values.
   2. For each position, find the largest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(double values[], int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (values[chosen] < values[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        double tmp = values[i];
        values[i] = values[chosen];
        values[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double values[] = {16.6, 19.0, 35.1, 18.4, 95.8};
    const int n = 5;
    selection_sort(values, n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", values[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the largest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 5 values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to count the odd values in a list of integers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_odd() that takes nums and length.
   2. For each element, test nums[i] % 2 != 0.
   3. Add one to found for every odd number.
   4. Return found and print it. */
/* A number is odd when the remainder after dividing by 2 is one. */
int count_odd(const int nums[], int length) {
    int found = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        if (nums[i] % 2 != 0) {
            found++;
        }
    }
    return found;
}

int main(void) {
    int nums[] = {60, 97, 92, 93, 19, 69, 15, 67, 13};
    const int length = 9;
    printf("Odd numbers: %d\n", count_odd(nums, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_odd() tests each element of nums with the % operator: a remainder of
   1 after dividing by 2 means the number is odd, so found goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 9 values are odd. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to save text to a file with fprintf and print it with fgets. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open log.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 4 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */

    FILE *file = fopen("log.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "learning c teaches how computers work\n");
    fprintf(file, "always free the memory you allocate\n");
    fprintf(file, "structs group related data together\n");

    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}

/* Caption: Write a C program to print the factorial of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(n) that calls itself.
   2. Return 1 when n is 1 or less.
   3. Otherwise return n * factorial(n - 1).
   4. Print 15! as an unsigned long long. */
/* n! = n * (n - 1)!, and 0! = 1 stops the recursion. */
unsigned long long factorial(int n) {
    if (n <= 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    return n * factorial(n - 1);
}

int main(void) {
    int n = 15;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", n, factorial(n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() calls itself: n! is n * (n - 1)!, and the recursion stops when
   n is 1 or less. main() prints 15! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very
   fast. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I compute the factorial of a number with a loop in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(n) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by every number from 2 to n.
   3. Return result.
   4. Print 3! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int n) {
    unsigned long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int n = 3;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", n, factorial(n));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() multiplies result by every number from 2 up to n. main() prints
   3! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: Create a singly linked list by inserting at the head. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Item with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 4 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Item {
    int value;
    struct Item *next;
} Item;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Item *push_front(Item *head, int value) {
    Item *node = malloc(sizeof(Item));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Item *head) {
    for (const Item *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Item *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Item *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Item *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 86);
    head = push_front(head, 3);
    head = push_front(head, 2);
    head = push_front(head, 94);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Item holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 4
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 93 and 79. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 93, y = 79;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 93 and 79. */
// END

long long power(int base, int exp) {

    return 0;

   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 7 to the power 2. */

/* Caption: Write a function that swaps two int values through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two int values.
   2. Save *x in tmp, copy *y into *x, then tmp into *y.
   3. In main(), print x and y, call swap(&x, &y) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(int *x, int *y) {
    int tmp = *x;
    *x = *y;
    *y = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 83, y = 70;
    printf("Before: %d %d\n", x, y);
    swap(&x, &y);
    printf("After:  %d %d\n", x, y);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of x and y, so writing through the pointers
   *x and *y changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to multiply two fractions using a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Fraction struct with num and den.
   2. Write multiply() that returns num = a.num * b.num and den = a.den * b.den.
   3. Print 4/4 times 9/7. */
typedef struct {
    int num;
    int den;
} Fraction;

/* Multiply the numerators and the denominators. */
Fraction multiply(Fraction a, Fraction b) {
    Fraction r = {a.num * b.num, a.den * b.den};

}

int main(void) {
    Fraction x = {4, 4}, y = {9, 7};
    Fraction p = multiply(x, y);
    printf("%d/%d * %d/%d = %d/%d\n", x.num, x.den, y.num, y.den, p.num, p.den);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Fraction stores a numerator and a denominator. multiply() takes two
   Fractions and returns a new one with num = a.num * b.num and den = a.den * b.den. main()
   multiplies 4/4 by 9/7 (without reducing the result). */
// END

/* Caption: Print an integer with its digits reversed. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Multiply result by 10, add n % 10, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 483013 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int reverse_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result = result * 10 + n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 483013;
    printf("reverse of digits of %d: %d\n", number, reverse_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_digits() shifts result one place left (result * 10) and adds the
   last digit of n, which reverses the order. main() applies it to 483013. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to sum a long array with a helper function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_array() that takes the array values and its length length.
   2. Start total at 0 and add every element in a while loop.
   3. Return total.
   4. In main(), fill values with 7 values and print the sum. */
/* Walk through the array and accumulate each value. */
long sum_array(const long values[], int length) {
    long total = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < length) {
        total += values[i];
        i++;
    }
    return total;
}

int main(void) {
    long values[] = {94L, 81L, 9L, 89L, 21L, 42L, 6L};
    int length = sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]);
    printf("The sum is %ld\n", sum_array(values, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: sum_array() receives the array values and its length length. It starts
   total at 0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills
   values with 7 long values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: Show how to declare variables of different types on one line each. */

/* Plan:
   1. Declare three ints on one line.

   3. Print each group and the sum of the ints. */

    /* Variables of the same type can share one declaration, separated by commas. */
    int a = 86, b = 49, c = 41;
    double x = 40.2, y = 2.9;
    char first = 'O', last = 'X';
    printf("a = %d, b = %d, c = %d\n", a, b, c);
    printf("x = %.2f, y = %.2f\n", x, y);
    printf("first = %c, last = %c\n", first, last);
    printf("a + b + c = %d\n", a + b + c);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each line declares several variables of one type, separated by commas, and

/* Caption: Write a program to write a function that swaps two long values through pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two long values.
   2. Save *first in tmp, copy *second into *first, then tmp into *second.
   3. In main(), print first and second, call swap(&first, &second) and print them
      again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(long *first, long *second) {
    long tmp = *first;
    *first = *second;
    *second = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    long first = 62L, second = 86L;
    printf("Before: %ld %ld\n", first, second);
    swap(&first, &second);
    printf("After:  %ld %ld\n", first, second);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of first and second, so writing through the
   pointers *first and *second changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during
   the exchange. main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and
   after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Check every element of an array to find a target value. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and target.
   2. Compare each element with target.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 49 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of target, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int scores[], int size, int target) {
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        if (scores[i] == target) {
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int scores[] = {49, 77, 7, 22, 34, 96, 22, 86};
    int size = sizeof(scores) / sizeof(scores[0]);
    int target = 49;
    int pos = linear_search(scores, size, target);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", target, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", target);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of scores one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to target, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 49 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to compute 8 to the power of 2 without pow(). */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 8 to the power 2. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("8^2 = %lld\n", power(8, 2));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 8 to the power 2. */
// END

/* Caption: Sort an array in descending order using bubble sort. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write bubble_sort() for the double array scores.
   2. Compare each pair of neighbours.
   3. Swap them when they are in the wrong order for descending order.
   4. Repeat the passes until the array is sorted.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Repeatedly swap neighbours that are in the wrong order. */
void bubble_sort(double scores[], int len) {
    for (int i = 0; i < len - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < len - 1 - i; j++) {
            if (scores[j] < scores[j + 1]) {
                double tmp = scores[j];
                scores[j] = scores[j + 1];
                scores[j + 1] = tmp;
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double scores[] = {42.4, 34.4, 33.5, 10.1, 19.8};
    int len = 5;
    bubble_sort(scores, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", scores[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: bubble_sort() walks through scores again and again and swaps neighbours
   that are in the wrong order, so the smallest values move to the end first. main() then
   prints the 5 values in descending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the distance between two points using a struct. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Point struct with x and y.
   2. Write distance() using sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy).
   3. Print the distance between p and q. */
typedef struct {
    double x;
    double y;
} Point;

/* Pythagoras: sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). */
double distance(Point a, Point b) {
    double dx = b.x - a.x;
    double dy = b.y - a.y;
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

int main(void) {
    Point p = {-2, 7};
    Point q = {-10, -10};
    printf("Distance: %.3f\n", distance(p, q));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Point is a typedef struct with x and y. distance() uses Pythagoras, sqrt(dx
   * dx + dy * dy), to measure the gap between the two points, and main() prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to find the total of all elements in an array using a loop. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write sum_array() that takes the array nums and its length length.
   2. Start result at 0 and add every element in a while loop.
   3. Return result.
   4. In main(), fill nums with 8 values and print the sum. */
/* Add every element to a running total. */
int sum_array(const int nums[], int length) {
    int result = 0;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < length) {
        result += nums[i];
        i++;
    }
    return result;

    int length = 8;
    printf("Total = %d\n", sum_array(nums, length));

   at 0, adds every element to it in a while loop and returns the total. main() fills nums
   with 8 int values and prints their sum. */
// END

/* Caption: Build a linked list, print it, and free it. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Item with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 6 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Item {
    int value;
    struct Item *next;
} Item;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Item *push_front(Item *head, int value) {
    Item *node = malloc(sizeof(Item));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Item *head) {
    for (const Item *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Item *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Item *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Item *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 93);
    head = push_front(head, 51);
    head = push_front(head, 8);
    head = push_front(head, 37);
    head = push_front(head, 3);
    head = push_front(head, 71);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Item holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 6
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Return the largest element of an array of int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write max_of() that takes items and length.
   2. Store items[0] in largest.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the largest value in largest.
   4. Return largest and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the largest value seen so far. */
int max_of(const int items[], int length) {
    int largest = items[0];
    for (int idx = 1; idx < length; idx++) {
        if (items[idx] > largest) {
            largest = items[idx];
        }
    }
    return largest;
}

int main(void) {
    int items[] = {62, 22, 12, 17, 22};
    const int length = 5;
    printf("The largest value is %d\n", max_of(items, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: max_of() takes the first element as the largest value so far and stores it
   in largest. The loop compares every other element with largest using > and keeps the
   largest one. main() prints the largest of the 5 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Print the binary representation of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 363 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 363;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 12);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 363
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to check whether a number is prime. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Check 139 and print the result. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 139;
    printf("%d %s prime\n", number, is_prime(number) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() checks 139 and prints whether it is prime. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to count how many digits a number has. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Divide n by 10 and add one to result.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 527834 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int count_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result++;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 527834;
    printf("count of digits of %d: %d\n", number, count_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_digits() removes the last digit (n / 10) and adds one to result each
   time, until n reaches 0. main() applies it to 527834. */
// END

/* Caption: Count how many odd numbers are in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_odd() that takes nums and len.
   2. For each element, test nums[idx] % 2 != 0.
   3. Add one to matches for every odd number.
   4. Return matches and print it. */
/* A number is odd when the remainder after dividing by 2 is one. */
int count_odd(const int nums[], int len) {
    int matches = 0;
    int idx = 0;
    while (idx < len) {
        if (nums[idx] % 2 != 0) {
            matches++;
        }
        idx++;
    }
    return matches;
}

int main(void) {
    int nums[] = {41, 84, 95, 72, 55, 55, 70};
    const int len = 7;
    printf("Odd numbers: %d\n", count_odd(nums, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_odd() tests each element of nums with the % operator: a remainder of
   1 after dividing by 2 means the number is odd, so matches goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 7 values are odd. */
// END

/* Caption: Add two 4x4 matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 4 and COLS as 4.
   2. Loop over every row r and column c.
   3. Store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print it. */
#define ROWS 4
#define COLS 4

int main(void) {
    int a[ROWS][COLS] = {{4, 2, 8, 7}, {5, 4, 3, 4}, {6, 7, 6, 2}, {4, 4, 2, 6}};
    int b[ROWS][COLS] = {{3, 0, 4, 8}, {3, 6, 2, 3}, {8, 2, 6, 2}, {5, 4, 4, 4}};
    int sum[ROWS][COLS];
    /* Each entry of the result is the sum of the matching entries. */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            sum[r][c] = a[r][c] + b[r][c];
            printf("%3d", sum[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Both matrices are 4x4 two-dimensional arrays. Two nested loops visit every
   row r and column c, store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print each row. */
// END

int reverse_digits(int n) {

/* Caption: Implement insertion sort for an array of int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the int array numbers.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(int numbers[], int size) {
    for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
        int current = numbers[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && numbers[j] > current) {
            numbers[j + 1] = numbers[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        numbers[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {1, 48, 94, 26, 71};
    int size = sizeof(numbers) / sizeof(numbers[0]);
    insertion_sort(numbers, size);
    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        printf("%d ", numbers[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 5 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I copy one string into another by hand in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write copy_string(dest, src).
   2. Copy src into dest one character at a time.
   3. Stop after copying the null character.
   4. Copy level into line and print it. */
/* Copy each character, including the final '\0'. */
void copy_string(char *dest, const char *src) {
    int i = 0;
    while ((dest[i] = src[i]) != '\0') {
        i++;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char source[] = "level";
    char line[100];
    copy_string(line, source);
    printf("Copied: %s\n", line);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: copy_string() copies src into dest one character at a time, including the
   final null character, which is what strcpy does. The array line must be big enough to
   hold the copy. main() copies the word level and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Print the binary representation of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 948 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 948;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 10);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 948
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: Check every element of an array to find a target value. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write linear_search() with the array, its length and wanted.
   2. Compare each element with wanted.
   3. Return the index of the first match, or -1.
   4. In main(), search for 158 and print the result. */
/* Return the index of wanted, or -1 when it is not in the array. */
int linear_search(const int numbers[], int length, int wanted) {
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
        if (numbers[i] == wanted) {
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int numbers[] = {98, 85, 17, 47, 64, 18, 68, 89, 66, 69};
    const int length = 10;
    int wanted = 158;
    int pos = linear_search(numbers, length, wanted);
    if (pos >= 0) {
        printf("Found %d at index %d\n", wanted, pos);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not in the array\n", wanted);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: linear_search() checks the elements of numbers one by one and returns the
   index of the first one equal to wanted, or -1 when it reaches the end without a match.
   main() searches for 158 and prints where it is, or that it is missing. */
// END

/* Caption: Create a singly linked list by inserting at the head. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 3 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 64);
    head = push_front(head, 6);
    head = push_front(head, 8);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 3
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I search a sorted array by halving the search range each step in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set low to 0 and high to length - 1.
   3. While low <= high, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 56. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int readings[], int length, int key) {
    int low = 0;
    int high = length - 1;
    while (low <= high) {
        int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (readings[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (readings[mid] < key) {
            low = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            high = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int readings[] = {14, 32, 44, 56, 64, 102, 122, 176, 180};
    int length = 9;
    int index = binary_search(readings, length, 56);
    printf("Index of 56: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from low to high,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 56 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the minimum and maximum of an array with one function. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write min_max() with the array, its length and the pointers min and max.
   2. Start both at the first element.
   3. Update *min and *max while looping over the rest.
   4. Declare lowest and highest, pass their addresses and print them. */
/* One pass finds both results; they are stored through the pointers. */
void min_max(const int samples[], int size, int *min, int *max) {
    *min = samples[0];
    *max = samples[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
        if (samples[i] < *min) {
            *min = samples[i];
        }
        if (samples[i] > *max) {
            *max = samples[i];
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {83, 69, 24, 77, 56, 23};
    int size = sizeof(samples) / sizeof(samples[0]);
    int lowest, highest;
    min_max(samples, size, &lowest, &highest);
    printf("Min: %d, Max: %d\n", lowest, highest);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: A C function can return only one value, so min_max() returns void and
   writes its two results through the pointer parameters min and max. main() declares
   lowest and highest on one line and passes their addresses with &, then prints both
   results for the 6 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to use dynamic memory to store the first 6 multiples. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 6 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill arr with multiples.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(arr) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 6;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *arr = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (arr == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        arr[i] = 8 * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", arr[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(arr);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 6 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills arr with multiples, the second prints
   them, and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Test if 101 is a prime number. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Check 101 and print the result. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 101;
    printf("%d %s prime\n", number, is_prime(number) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() checks 101 and prints whether it is prime. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to use Euclid's algorithm to compute the GCD. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write gcd() with Euclid's algorithm.
   2. Replace (a, b) by (b, a % b) until b is 0.
   3. Return a and print the GCD of 138 and 290. */
/* Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b becomes zero. */
int gcd(int a, int b) {
    while (b != 0) {
        int r = a % b;
        a = b;
        b = r;
    }
    return a;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 138, y = 290;
    printf("gcd(%d, %d) = %d\n", x, y, gcd(x, y));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: gcd() uses Euclid's algorithm: it keeps replacing (a, b) with (b, a % b)
   until b is 0. The last non-zero value is the greatest common divisor, and main() prints
   the GCD of 138 and 290. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to swap two variables using pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two double values.
   2. Save *first in tmp, copy *second into *first, then tmp into *second.
   3. In main(), print first and second, call swap(&first, &second) and print them
      again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(double *first, double *second) {
    double tmp = *first;
    *first = *second;
    *second = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    double first = 71.0, second = 11.6;
    printf("Before: %.2f %.2f\n", first, second);
    swap(&first, &second);
    printf("After:  %.2f %.2f\n", first, second);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of first and second, so writing through the
   pointers *first and *second changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during
   the exchange. main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and
   after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Count how many odd numbers are in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_odd() that takes samples and length.
   2. For each element, test samples[k] % 2 != 0.
   3. Add one to matches for every odd number.
   4. Return matches and print it. */
/* A number is odd when the remainder after dividing by 2 is one. */
int count_odd(const int samples[], int length) {
    int matches = 0;
    int k = 0;
    while (k < length) {
        if (samples[k] % 2 != 0) {
            matches++;
        }
        k++;
    }
    return matches;
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {5, 90, 22, 17, 8, 87, 31, 40};
    const int length = 8;
    printf("Odd numbers: %d\n", count_odd(samples, length));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_odd() tests each element of samples with the % operator: a remainder
   of 1 after dividing by 2 means the number is odd, so matches goes up by one. main()
   prints how many of the 8 values are odd. */
// END

/* Caption: Find the arithmetic mean of 7 int values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write mean() that takes readings and len.
   2. Add the values into the double acc.
   3. Return acc / len.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* The mean is the total divided by the count. */
double mean(const int readings[], int len) {
    double acc = 0.0;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < len; idx++) {
        acc += readings[idx];
    }
    return acc / len;
}

int main(void) {
    int readings[] = {46, 56, 7, 51, 61, 50, 85};
    int len = sizeof(readings) / sizeof(readings[0]);
    printf("Mean = %.2f\n", mean(readings, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: mean() adds the 7 values of readings into the double acc and divides by
   len, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers. main()
   prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Build a fixed-size integer stack in C. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stack with room for 8 items and a top counter.
   2. Write push() and pop(), returning false when the stack is full or empty.
   3. Push 5 values.
   4. Pop and print until the stack is empty. */
#define CAPACITY 8

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int top;   /* number of items on the stack */
} Stack;

bool push(Stack *s, int value) {
    if (s->top == CAPACITY) {
        return false;   /* stack is full */
    }
    s->items[s->top++] = value;
    return true;
}

bool pop(Stack *s, int *value) {
    if (s->top == 0) {
        return false;   /* stack is empty */
    }
    *value = s->items[--s->top];
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Stack s = {.top = 0};
    push(&s, 43);
    push(&s, 36);
    push(&s, 22);
    push(&s, 81);
    push(&s, 83);
    int value;
    /* Items come back out in reverse order (last in, first out). */
    while (pop(&s, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Stack keeps up to 8 items in an array, and top counts how many are
   stored. push() adds at the top and pop() removes from the top; both return false when
   they cannot. main() pushes 5 values and pops them all, so they come out in reverse order
   (last in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write array_average() that takes nums and count.
   2. Add the values into the double sum.
   3. Return sum / count.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double array_average(const int nums[], int count) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int k = 0; k < count; k++) {
        sum += nums[k];
    }
    return sum / count;
}

int main(void) {
    int nums[] = {22, 50, 57, 95, 52, 76};
    const int count = 6;
    printf("The average is %.2f\n", array_average(nums, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: array_average() adds the 6 values of nums into the double sum and divides
   by count, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers.
   main() prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to multiply two 3x3 matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define N as 3.
   2. For every i and j, add a[i][k] * b[k][j] over k into product[i][j].
   3. Print product row by row. */
#define N 3

int main(void) {
    int a[N][N] = {{5, 1, 7}, {7, 2, 5}, {1, 2, 5}};
    int b[N][N] = {{5, 0, 2}, {6, 1, 3}, {5, 7, 0}};
    int product[N][N] = {0};
    /* product[i][j] is row i of a times column j of b. */
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) {
                product[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
            printf("%4d", product[i][j]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: For each entry product[i][j] the innermost loop adds a[i][k] * b[k][j] over
   k, which is row i of a times column j of b. main() multiplies two 3x3 matrices and
   prints the product. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I check whether a year is a leap year in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_leap(year).
   2. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year, unless it is divisible by 100.
   3. Years divisible by 400 are leap years again.
   4. Check 1933 and print the result. */
/* Leap years divide by 4, except centuries, which must divide by 400. */
int is_leap(int year) {
    return (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || year % 400 == 0;
}

int main(void) {
    int year = 1933;
    if (is_leap(year)) {
        printf("%d is a leap year\n", year);
    } else {
        printf("%d is not a leap year\n", year);
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_leap() returns true for years divisible by 4, except century years,
   which must also be divisible by 400. main() checks 1933 and prints whether it is a leap
   year. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to use selection sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the int array items.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(int items[], int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (items[chosen] > items[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        int tmp = items[i];
        items[i] = items[chosen];
        items[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int items[] = {42, 71, 37, 61, 67};
    const int n = 5;
    selection_sort(items, n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", items[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 5 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I build a FIFO queue using a ring buffer in C? */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Queue with room for 8 items, a head and a count.
   2. Write enqueue() that stores at (head + count) % CAPACITY.
   3. Write dequeue() that takes the item at head and moves head on.
   4. Add 6 values, then remove and print them in order. */
#define CAPACITY 8

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int head;
    int count;
} Queue;

bool enqueue(Queue *q, int value) {
    if (q->count == CAPACITY) {
        return false;
    }
    /* The tail wraps around to the start of the array. */
    q->items[(q->head + q->count) % CAPACITY] = value;
    q->count++;
    return true;
}

bool dequeue(Queue *q, int *value) {
    if (q->count == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = q->items[q->head];
    q->head = (q->head + 1) % CAPACITY;
    q->count--;
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Queue q = {.head = 0, .count = 0};
    enqueue(&q, 75);
    enqueue(&q, 98);
    enqueue(&q, 58);
    enqueue(&q, 92);
    enqueue(&q, 38);
    enqueue(&q, 39);
    int value;
    /* Items come out in the order they went in (first in, first out). */
    while (dequeue(&q, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Queue stores up to 8 items in a ring buffer: head is the oldest item
   and % CAPACITY wraps positions back to the start of the array. enqueue() adds at the
   back and dequeue() removes from the front, so main() gets its 6 values back in the same
   order (first in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: Program to print the binary representation of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 575 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 575;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 8);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 575
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: Use dynamic memory to store the first 9 cubes. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Use malloc to get room for 9 ints and check for NULL.
   2. Fill list with cubes.
   3. Print the values.
   4. Call free(list) at the end. */
int main(void) {
    int n = 9;
    /* Ask the heap for room for n ints; malloc returns NULL on failure. */
    int *list = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
    if (list == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "malloc failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        list[i] = i * i * i;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d ", list[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    free(list);   /* give the memory back */
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: malloc() reserves room for 9 ints on the heap and returns NULL if it fails,
   which the program checks. The first loop fills list with cubes, the second prints them,
   and free() gives the memory back at the end. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a function that returns a Fraction struct. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Fraction struct with num and den.
   2. Write multiply() that returns num = a.num * b.num and den = a.den * b.den.
   3. Print 5/4 times 2/2. */
typedef struct {
    int num;
    int den;
} Fraction;

/* Multiply the numerators and the denominators. */
Fraction multiply(Fraction a, Fraction b) {
    Fraction r = {a.num * b.num, a.den * b.den};
    return r;
}

int main(void) {
    Fraction x = {5, 4}, y = {2, 2};
    Fraction p = multiply(x, y);
    printf("%d/%d * %d/%d = %d/%d\n", x.num, x.den, y.num, y.den, p.num, p.den);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Fraction stores a numerator and a denominator. multiply() takes two
   Fractions and returns a new one with num = a.num * b.num and den = a.den * b.den. main()
   multiplies 5/4 by 2/2 (without reducing the result). */
// END

/* Caption: Find the arithmetic mean of 8 long values. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write mean() that takes marks and size.
   2. Add the values into the double total.
   3. Return total / size.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double mean(const long marks[], int size) {
    double total = 0.0;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < size; idx++) {
        total += marks[idx];
    }
    return total / size;
}

int main(void) {
    long marks[] = {15L, 59L, 25L, 24L, 17L, 35L, 40L, 15L};
    const int size = 8;
    printf("Mean = %.2f\n", mean(marks, size));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: mean() adds the 8 values of marks into the double total and divides by
   size, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers. main()
   prints it with two decimals. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I compute 7 to the power of 7 without pow() in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write power(base, exp) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by base exp times.
   3. Print 7 to the power 7. */
/* Multiply the base by itself exp times. */
long long power(int base, int exp) {
    long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("7^7 = %lld\n", power(7, 7));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: power() starts result at 1 and multiplies it by base exp times. It uses
   long long because powers grow quickly. main() prints 7 to the power 7. */
// END

   of 0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so found goes up by one. main()
   prints how many of the 12 values are even. */

/* Caption: Write a C program to add two 2x4 matrices. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define ROWS as 2 and COLS as 4.
   2. Loop over every row r and column c.
   3. Store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print it. */
#define ROWS 2
#define COLS 4

int main(void) {
    int a[ROWS][COLS] = {{3, 5, 3, 1}, {4, 4, 8, 4}};
    int b[ROWS][COLS] = {{0, 4, 4, 6}, {3, 6, 5, 6}};
    int sum[ROWS][COLS];
    /* Each entry of the result is the sum of the matching entries. */
    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < COLS; c++) {
            sum[r][c] = a[r][c] + b[r][c];
            printf("%3d", sum[r][c]);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Both matrices are 2x4 two-dimensional arrays. Two nested loops visit every
   row r and column c, store a[r][c] + b[r][c] in sum and print each row. */
// END

/* Caption: Implement a stack with an array (push and pop). */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Stack with room for 10 items and a top counter.
   2. Write push() and pop(), returning false when the stack is full or empty.
   3. Push 6 values.
   4. Pop and print until the stack is empty. */
#define CAPACITY 10

typedef struct {
    int items[CAPACITY];
    int top;   /* number of items on the stack */
} Stack;

bool push(Stack *s, int value) {
    if (s->top == CAPACITY) {
        return false;   /* stack is full */
    }
    s->items[s->top++] = value;
    return true;
}

bool pop(Stack *s, int *value) {
    if (s->top == 0) {
        return false;   /* stack is empty */
    }
    *value = s->items[--s->top];
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    Stack s = {.top = 0};
    push(&s, 47);
    push(&s, 11);
    push(&s, 13);
    push(&s, 13);
    push(&s, 92);
    push(&s, 24);
    int value;
    /* Items come back out in reverse order (last in, first out). */
    while (pop(&s, &value)) {
        printf("%d ", value);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The Stack keeps up to 10 items in an array, and top counts how many are
   stored. push() adds at the top and pop() removes from the top; both return false when
   they cannot. main() pushes 6 values and pops them all, so they come out in reverse order
   (last in, first out). */
// END

/* Caption: How do I print the first 13 Fibonacci numbers in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with first = 0 and second = 1.
   2. Repeat 13 times and print first each time.
   3. Compute next = first + second, then set first = second and second = next. */
int main(void) {
    long first = 0, second = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 13; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", first);
        long next = first + second;
        first = second;
        second = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in first and second. Each round it
   prints first, then moves the pair forward: first becomes second and second becomes their
   sum. It prints the first 13 Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Use insertion sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the int array samples.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(int samples[], int count) {
    for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {
        int current = samples[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && samples[j] > current) {
            samples[j + 1] = samples[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        samples[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    int samples[] = {5, 19, 82, 23, 13, 54, 20, 74, 55, 36};
    int count = 10;
    insertion_sort(samples, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%d ", samples[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 10 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to reverse the elements of an array in place. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write reverse_array() for marks.
   2. Set i to the first index and j to the last.
   3. Swap marks[i] and marks[j], then move both inwards.
   4. Stop when i meets j and print the array. */
/* Swap the outer pair, then move both ends toward the middle. */
void reverse_array(long marks[], int count) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = count - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        long tmp = marks[i];
        marks[i] = marks[j];
        marks[j] = tmp;
        i++;
        j--;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long marks[] = {83L, 75L, 50L, 42L, 9L, 85L, 56L};
    int count = 7;
    reverse_array(marks, count);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", marks[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_array() swaps the first and last elements, then moves i forward and
   j backward until they meet, so the array is reversed in place without a second array.
   main() prints the reversed values. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to copy one string into another by hand. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write copy_string(dest, src).
   2. Copy src into dest one character at a time.
   3. Stop after copying the null character.
   4. Copy bridge into buffer and print it. */
/* Copy each character, including the final '\0'. */
void copy_string(char *dest, const char *src) {
    int i = 0;
    while ((dest[i] = src[i]) != '\0') {
        i++;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    char source[] = "bridge";
    char buffer[32];
    copy_string(buffer, source);
    printf("Copied: %s\n", buffer);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: copy_string() copies src into dest one character at a time, including the
   final null character, which is what strcpy does. The array buffer must be big enough to
   hold the copy. main() copies the word bridge and prints it. */
// END

/* Caption: Use insertion sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write insertion_sort() for the long array readings.
   2. Take each element in turn as current.
   3. Shift the larger values of the sorted part one place right.
   4. Put current into the gap.
   5. Print the sorted values. */
/* Insert each element into the already sorted part on its left. */
void insertion_sort(long readings[], int len) {
    for (int i = 1; i < len; i++) {
        long current = readings[i];
        int j = i - 1;
        while (j >= 0 && readings[j] > current) {
            readings[j + 1] = readings[j];   /* shift bigger values right */
            j--;
        }
        readings[j + 1] = current;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long readings[] = {72L, 21L, 56L, 30L, 9L, 82L, 60L, 22L, 85L, 7L};
    int len = 10;
    insertion_sort(readings, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", readings[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: insertion_sort() takes each element in turn and shifts the larger values of
   the sorted part one place right until the element fits. main() then prints the 10 values
   in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I write lines to a text file and read them back in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Open output.txt in write mode and check for NULL.
   2. Write 2 lines with fprintf and close the file.
   3. Open it again in read mode.
   4. Read and print each line with fgets, then close the file. */
int main(void) {
    FILE *file = fopen("output.txt", "w");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    fprintf(file, "strings end with a null character\n");
    fprintf(file, "every program starts in main\n");
    fclose(file);

    /* Reopen the file for reading and print it line by line. */
    file = fopen("output.txt", "r");
    if (file == NULL) {
        perror("fopen");
        return 1;
    }
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), file) != NULL) {
        printf("%s", line);
    }
    fclose(file);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: fopen() in write mode creates output.txt, fprintf() writes 2 lines into it
   and fclose() saves it. The file is then opened again in read mode, and fgets() reads it
   back line by line into the buffer line, which is printed. Every fopen() result is
   checked for NULL. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to convert 860 to binary. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write print_binary(n, bits).
   2. Go through the bits from the highest to the lowest.
   3. Print 1 when (n >> b) & 1 is set, otherwise 0.
   4. Print 860 in binary. */
/* Check each bit from the highest to the lowest. */
void print_binary(unsigned int n, int bits) {
    for (int b = bits - 1; b >= 0; b--) {
        putchar((n >> b) & 1 ? '1' : '0');
    }
    putchar('\n');
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned int number = 860;
    printf("%u in binary: ", number);
    print_binary(number, 8);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: print_binary() checks one bit at a time, from the highest to the lowest: (n
   >> b) & 1 is 1 when bit b is set, so it prints the character 1 or 0. main() prints 860
   in binary. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to divide two integers and get both the quotient and the remainder. */

#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write divide(a, b, &quotient, &remainder) that returns a bool.
   2. Return false if b is 0.
   3. Store a / b and a % b through the pointers and return true.
   4. Divide 140 by 6 and print the results or the error. */
/* Returns false for division by zero; otherwise stores both results. */
bool divide(int a, int b, int *quotient, int *remainder) {

        return false;

    *quotient = a / b;
    *remainder = a % b;

        printf("%d / %d = %d remainder %d\n", a, b, q, r);
    } else {
        printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: divide() has four parameters: two inputs and two pointers for the results.
   Its bool return value reports success, while the quotient and remainder are written
   through the pointers. main() divides 140 by 6 and prints both results. */
// END

/* Caption: Program to find the smallest number in an array. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write find_min() that takes values and len.
   2. Store values[0] in best.
   3. Loop over the other elements and keep the smallest value in best.
   4. Return best and print it. */
/* Start with the first element and keep the smallest value seen so far. */
long find_min(const long values[], int len) {
    long best = values[0];
    for (int idx = 1; idx < len; idx++) {
        if (values[idx] < best) {
            best = values[idx];
        }
    }
    return best;
}

int main(void) {
    long values[] = {24L, 31L, 9L, 77L, 25L, 45L, 86L, 38L};
    const int len = 8;
    printf("Smallest: %ld\n", find_min(values, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: find_min() takes the first element as the smallest value so far and stores
   it in best. The loop compares every other element with best using < and keeps the
   smallest one. main() prints the smallest of the 8 values. */
// END

/* Caption: Use binary search to locate a value in a sorted list. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Make sure the array is sorted.
   2. Set lo to 0 and hi to count - 1.
   3. While lo <= hi, compare the middle element mid with the key.
   4. Return the index if it matches; otherwise keep only the half that can hold the
      key.
   5. Return -1 if the range becomes empty, and print the index of 97. */
/* The array must be sorted. Each step halves the range that can still hold the key. */
int binary_search(const int readings[], int count, int key) {
    int lo = 0;
    int hi = count - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (readings[mid] == key) {
            return mid;
        } else if (readings[mid] < key) {
            lo = mid + 1;   /* key is in the right half */
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1;   /* key is in the left half */
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    int readings[] = {54, 56, 85, 87, 97, 125, 138, 146, 164, 165, 186, 196};
    int count = sizeof(readings) / sizeof(readings[0]);
    int index = binary_search(readings, count, 97);
    printf("Index of 97: %d\n", index);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: binary_search() needs a sorted array. It keeps the range from lo to hi,
   compares the middle element mid with the key and throws away the half that cannot
   contain it, so it needs only about log2(n) steps. main() looks for 97 and prints its
   index, or -1 if it is not there. */
// END

/* Caption: How do I count how many even numbers are in an array in C? */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write count_even() that takes nums and count.
   2. For each element, test nums[j] % 2 == 0.
   3. Add one to matches for every even number.
   4. Return matches and print it. */
/* A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero. */
int count_even(const int nums[], int count) {
    int matches = 0;
    for (int j = 0; j < count; j++) {
        if (nums[j] % 2 == 0) {
            matches++;
        }
    }
    return matches;
}

int main(void) {
    int nums[] = {79, 71, 90, 90, 54, 71, 14, 5, 10, 64, 4};
    int count = sizeof(nums) / sizeof(nums[0]);
    printf("Count of even values = %d\n", count_even(nums, count));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: count_even() tests each element of nums with the % operator: a remainder of
   0 after dividing by 2 means the number is even, so matches goes up by one. main() prints
   how many of the 11 values are even. */
// END

/* Caption: Compute the mean of a list of numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write average() that takes items and len.
   2. Add the values into the double sum.
   3. Return sum / len.
   4. Print the average with two decimals. */
/* Sum the values, then divide by how many there are. */
double average(const int items[], int len) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int j = 0; j < len; j++) {
        sum += items[j];
    }
    return sum / len;
}

int main(void) {
    int items[] = {7, 33, 93, 96, 20};
    int len = sizeof(items) / sizeof(items[0]);
    printf("Average: %.2f\n", average(items, len));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: average() adds the 5 values of items into the double sum and divides by
   len, so the mean keeps its decimal part even when the values are whole numbers. main()
   prints it with two decimals. */
// END

   both results. */

/* Caption: Write a C program to implement a simple linked list with malloc and free. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define Node with a value and a next pointer.
   2. Write push_front() that mallocs a node and links it in front of head.
   3. Write print_list() that follows next until NULL.
   4. Write free_list() that frees every node.
   5. Push 6 values, print the list and free it. */
typedef struct Node {
    int value;
    struct Node *next;
} Node;

/* Allocate a new node and put it in front of the current head. */
Node *push_front(Node *head, int value) {
    Node *node = malloc(sizeof(Node));
    if (node == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Out of memory\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    node->value = value;
    node->next = head;
    return node;
}

void print_list(const Node *head) {
    for (const Node *cur = head; cur != NULL; cur = cur->next) {
        printf("%d -> ", cur->value);
    }
    printf("NULL\n");
}

/* Free every node; save next before freeing the current one. */
void free_list(Node *head) {
    while (head != NULL) {
        Node *next = head->next;
        free(head);
        head = next;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Node *head = NULL;
    head = push_front(head, 96);
    head = push_front(head, 65);
    head = push_front(head, 41);
    head = push_front(head, 36);
    head = push_front(head, 12);
    head = push_front(head, 7);
    print_list(head);
    free_list(head);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: Each Node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. push_front()
   allocates a node with malloc, puts it in front of head and returns it; print_list()
   follows the next pointers until NULL; free_list() frees every node. main() pushes 6
   values, so they print in reverse order. */
// END

/* Caption: Reverse the digits of a number. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start result at 0.
   2. Multiply result by 10, add n % 10, then divide n by 10.
   3. Repeat until n is 0.
   4. Apply it to 2838 and print the result. */
/* Take the last digit with % 10, then drop it with / 10. */
int reverse_digits(int n) {
    int result = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        result = result * 10 + n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 2838;
    printf("reverse of digits of %d: %d\n", number, reverse_digits(number));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: reverse_digits() shifts result one place left (result * 10) and adds the
   last digit of n, which reverses the order. main() applies it to 2838. */
// END

/* Caption: Print the factorial of an integer. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write factorial(value) with result = 1.
   2. Multiply result by every number from 2 to value.
   3. Return result.
   4. Print 12! as an unsigned long long. */
/* Multiply 1 * 2 * ... * n. */
unsigned long long factorial(int value) {
    unsigned long long result = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= value; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    return result;
}

int main(void) {
    int value = 12;
    printf("%d! = %llu\n", value, factorial(value));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: factorial() multiplies result by every number from 2 up to value. main()
   prints 12! as an unsigned long long, because factorials grow very fast. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to use selection sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the double array marks.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(double marks[], int len) {
    for (int i = 0; i < len - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < len; j++) {
            if (marks[chosen] > marks[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        double tmp = marks[i];
        marks[i] = marks[chosen];
        marks[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    double marks[] = {9.6, 15.7, 20.8, 28.6, 13.9, 9.4, 24.7, 57.9, 48.9};
    const int len = 9;
    selection_sort(marks, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%.2f ", marks[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 9 values in ascending order. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to generate the Fibonacci sequence. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with first = 0 and second = 1.
   2. Repeat 24 times and print first each time.
   3. Compute next = first + second, then set first = second and second = next. */
int main(void) {
    long first = 0, second = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 24; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", first);
        long next = first + second;
        first = second;
        second = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in first and second. Each round it
   prints first, then moves the pair forward: first becomes second and second becomes their
   sum. It prints the first 24 Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: Write a program to test if 287 is a prime number. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_prime(n); numbers below 2 are not prime.
   2. Try every divisor d while d * d <= n.
   3. Return false if one divides n, otherwise true.
   4. Check 287 and print the result. */
/* A prime has no divisor between 2 and its square root. */
bool is_prime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) {
        return false;
    }
    for (int d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
        if (n % d == 0) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    int number = 287;
    printf("%d %s prime\n", number, is_prime(number) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_prime() tries every divisor d from 2 while d * d <= n; if one divides n
   evenly, n is not prime. main() checks 287 and prints whether it is prime. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to compute the distance between two points with a four-parameter function. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write distance(x1, y1, x2, y2).
   2. Compute dx and dy, then return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy).
   3. Print the distance between (3, -8) and (-2, 6). */
/* Pythagoras: the distance is sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). */
double distance(double x1, double y1, double x2, double y2) {
    double dx = x2 - x1, dy = y2 - y1;
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

int main(void) {
    printf("Distance: %.3f\n", distance(3, -8, -2, 6));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: distance() takes the coordinates of both points as four parameters. It
   declares dx and dy on one line and uses Pythagoras with sqrt() from math.h. main()
   prints the distance between (3, -8) and (-2, 6). */
// END

/* Caption: Write a C program to compute the length of a string without strlen. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write string_length() with a counter len = 0.
   2. Move through the string until the null character.
   3. Return len and print the length of madam. */
/* Count characters until the terminating '\0'. */
int string_length(const char *word) {
    int len = 0;
    while (word[len] != '\0') {
        len++;
    }
    return len;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *word = "madam";
    printf("Length of \"%s\" is %d\n", word, string_length(word));
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: string_length() counts characters until it reaches the null character that
   ends every C string. main() prints the length of the word madam. */
// END

/* Caption: Swap two variables using pointers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write swap() that takes pointers to two int values.
   2. Save *x in tmp, copy *y into *x, then tmp into *y.
   3. In main(), print x and y, call swap(&x, &y) and print them again. */
/* Pass addresses so the function can change the caller's variables. */
void swap(int *x, int *y) {
    int tmp = *x;
    *x = *y;
    *y = tmp;
}

int main(void) {
    int x = 83, y = 29;
    printf("Before: %d %d\n", x, y);
    swap(&x, &y);
    printf("After:  %d %d\n", x, y);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: swap() receives the addresses of x and y, so writing through the pointers
   *x and *y changes the caller's variables. tmp holds one value during the exchange.
   main() declares both variables on one line and prints them before and after the swap. */
// END

/* Caption: Print the first 17 Fibonacci numbers. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Start with a = 0 and b = 1.
   2. Repeat 17 times and print a each time.
   3. Compute next = a + b, then set a = b and b = next. */
int main(void) {
    long a = 0, b = 1;
    /* Print a term, then slide the pair one step along the sequence. */
    for (int i = 0; i < 17; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", a);
        long next = a + b;
        a = b;
        b = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: The loop keeps the last two numbers in a and b. Each round it prints a,
   then moves the pair forward: a becomes b and b becomes their sum. It prints the first 17
   Fibonacci numbers. */
// END

/* Caption: C program to check whether a word is a palindrome. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write is_palindrome() for word.
   2. Compare the first and last characters, moving inwards.
   3. Return false at the first mismatch, otherwise true.
   4. Check compiler and print the result. */
/* Compare characters from the front and back, moving inwards. */
bool is_palindrome(const char *word) {
    int i = 0;
    int j = strlen(word) - 1;
    while (i < j) {
        if (word[i] != word[j]) {
            return false;
        }
        i++;
        j--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main(void) {
    const char *word = "compiler";
    printf("%s %s a palindrome\n", word, is_palindrome(word) ? "is" : "is not");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: is_palindrome() compares the first and last characters and moves inwards;
   any mismatch means the word is not a palindrome. main() checks the word compiler and
   prints the result. */
// END

/* Caption: Return a Duration struct built from a number of seconds. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Define a Duration struct with hours, minutes and seconds.
   2. Write from_seconds() that fills it using / and %.
   3. Convert 79002 seconds and print the members. */
typedef struct {
    int hours;
    int minutes;
    int seconds;
} Duration;

Duration from_seconds(int total) {
    Duration d;
    d.hours = total / 3600;
    d.minutes = (total % 3600) / 60;
    d.seconds = total % 60;
    return d;
}

int main(void) {
    Duration d = from_seconds(79002);
    printf("%d h %d min %d s\n", d.hours, d.minutes, d.seconds);
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: from_seconds() fills the three members of a Duration struct using / and %,
   then returns the struct. main() converts 79002 seconds and prints the members. */
// END

/* Caption: Use selection sort to put numbers in ascending order. */
#include <stdio.h>

/* Plan:
   1. Write selection_sort() for the long array samples.
   2. For each position, find the smallest remaining element.
   3. Swap it into that position.
   4. Print the sorted values. */
/* Select the right element for each position and swap it into place. */
void selection_sort(long samples[], int len) {
    for (int i = 0; i < len - 1; i++) {
        int chosen = i;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < len; j++) {
            if (samples[chosen] > samples[j]) {
                chosen = j;
            }
        }
        long tmp = samples[i];
        samples[i] = samples[chosen];
        samples[chosen] = tmp;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    long samples[] = {88L, 65L, 50L, 27L, 49L, 84L, 59L, 58L, 25L};
    const int len = 9;
    selection_sort(samples, len);
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        printf("%ld ", samples[i]);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
/* Explanation: selection_sort() finds the smallest remaining element for each position and
   swaps it into place. main() then prints the 9 values in ascending order. */
// END
